summary: Built a presigned PUT route in a Next.js app so the browser uploads avatars straight to a bucket. The first test upload returned 200 and the object showed up in the console. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The presigner lives in its own package, separate from the S3 client, so it was installed alongside the client from the start.
The curl PUT returned 200 on the first try because the Content-Type header matched the value included in the signature.

context.task: Add avatar upload to a profile page

method: Claude Code in a Next.js App Router project. Installed @aws-sdk/client-s3 and @aws-sdk/s3-request-presigner, added a route handler that returns a PUT URL from getSignedUrl with a 300 second expiry, then ran curl with a 64 KB PNG.
limitations: Tested with one bucket in eu-west-1 and a single small file; no real browser CORS preflight was run.

summary: Wrote a Lambda that saves thumbnails back to the bucket. The first PutObject came back AccessDenied because the execution role lacked s3:PutObject on the thumbs prefix, and it worked after the policy edit. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: AccessDenied came back as HTTP 403 with no hint about which action or prefix was missing, so the agent checked the role policy by hand.
Granting s3:PutObject on the bucket ARN alone did not cover the keys, so the object ARN with the thumbs path was needed too.

context.task: Generate thumbnails for uploaded images in a Lambda

method: Cursor edited a Lambda handler that resizes with sharp and writes with PutObjectCommand from the v3 SDK. Deployed with SAM and invoked with a test S3 event. The inline role policy was edited in the console between attempts.
limitations: One function with a 1 MB test image; no concurrency or cold start numbers were recorded.

summary: Codex wrote a cron script that uploads a nightly CSV export with boto3 upload_file and ContentType set. The object landed under the dated prefix on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ExtraArgs accepted ContentType and Metadata keys, and the agent set ContentType to text/csv on every call.
The cron job read credentials from an instance profile, so no key file had to live on the host.

context.task: Upload nightly CSV export to a dated prefix

method: Codex CLI in a small Python repo. Wrote upload_export.py with the boto3 client upload_file call and ExtraArgs, ran it once by hand, then added a crontab line. Checked the result with aws s3 ls on the dated prefix.
limitations: One export file of about 12 MB; the cron schedule was not left running long enough to see a second night.

summary: Devin ran create-bucket in ap-south-1 without a location constraint. The call failed with IllegalLocationConstraintException and the run ended at the sandbox time limit. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Outside us-east-1 the request needs a LocationConstraint that matches the region, and the agent retried the same command twice before reading the error text.
The agent copied a us-east-1 snippet from memory, and that snippet had no create-bucket-configuration block.

context.task: Create a static-site bucket in ap-south-1

method: Devin in a cloud sandbox with the AWS CLI v2 preconfigured. Ran aws s3api create-bucket with a generated name and region ap-south-1, changed the bucket name and retried, then stopped when the session timer ran out.
limitations: Sandbox session had a fixed timer; the corrected command was never run in this session.

summary: Aider added a CORS rule to a Django upload bucket so the browser could PUT parts and read the ETag header. Multipart uploads from the page finished on the first attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ETag has to be listed in ExposeHeaders or the page cannot read it, and without it CompleteMultipartUpload has no part values to work with.
Listing ETag in ExposeHeaders made it readable on the actual PUT response, and the preflight stayed clean.

context.task: Enable browser multipart uploads to a bucket

method: Aider in a Django project with boto3 configured from environment credentials. Wrote a put_bucket_cors call with AllowedMethods PUT and GET, AllowedHeaders '*', and ExposeHeaders ETag, then tested a two-part upload from the dev server page.
limitations: Tested from one localhost origin only; the production origin and its CDN were not checked.

summary: OpenHands wrote a manual multipart loop for a 300 MB video. S3 rejected every part except the last with EntityTooSmall until the part size went from 2 MiB to 8 MiB. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Parts other than the last must be at least 5 MiB, so the 2 MiB chunks from the first loop were rejected with EntityTooSmall.
The Upload helper from lib-storage handles part splitting and retries, and the agent only looked at it after the manual loop failed twice.

context.task: Upload a 300 MB video from a Node script

method: OpenHands in a sandboxed Node workspace. Wrote a CreateMultipartUpload, UploadPart, CompleteMultipartUpload loop with 2 MiB parts, then switched to fixed 8 MiB parts and reran the same 300 MB file.
limitations: One test video on a single network path; no throughput comparison between part sizes was recorded.

summary: Cline applied a lifecycle rule that moves log objects to Glacier Instant Retrieval after 30 days. The get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration output matched the file on the first apply. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The rule uses a Filter with a Prefix of logs/, so the transition stays away from the rest of the bucket.
The value GLACIER_IR came back from the get call exactly as written in the file, so no conversion step was needed.

context.task: Move log objects to a colder storage class

method: Cline in a macOS terminal with AWS CLI v2 and a named profile. Wrote lifecycle.json with one rule, ran aws s3api put-bucket-lifecycle-configuration, then get-bucket-lifecycle-configuration to confirm the rule matched.
limitations: The bucket held only a few test objects; the transition after 30 days was not observed.

summary: Goose wrote a Go program that counts 2,400 keys with the ListObjectsV2 paginator. The total matched the console after the third page came back with 400 entries. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ListObjectsV2 returns at most 1,000 keys per call, and the paginator handled the continuation token so the loop body stayed short.
Listing the 2,400 keys took about 1.4 seconds across three requests from the build runner, with the median request near 410 ms.

context.task: Count keys under a prefix in a large bucket

method: Goose in a Go module with the aws-sdk-go-v2 s3 package. Built the ListObjectsV2 paginator for the prefix, iterated the pages while counting keys, and printed the total. Ran it from a CI job on an Ubuntu runner.
limitations: One prefix in one bucket, all objects small text files; object sizes were not varied.

summary: Windsurf set a presigned download link to 14 days. S3 refused it with AuthorizationQueryParametersError because the expiry was over the SigV4 maximum, and the run stopped there. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: SigV4 presigned URLs cap the expiry at seven days, and the 1,209,600 second value the agent set was rejected on the first request.
The agent changed the bucket policy first and only read the X-Amz-Expires message on the second rejection.

context.task: Generate a download link valid for two weeks

method: Windsurf in a Node script that calls getSignedUrl with GetObjectCommand and expiresIn 1209600. Ran the script twice, edited the bucket policy between runs, then stopped after the second rejection.
limitations: Only the SDK presign path was tried; no CLI presign or CloudFront signed URL was compared.

summary: A custom agent built an S3 client in us-east-1 for a bucket in eu-central-1. HeadObject raised PermanentRedirect until the client region matched the bucket, and the next call passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: PermanentRedirect came back on the first HeadObject, and the fix took one line once the bucket region was checked in the console.
The region set in the constructor overrode the AWS_REGION variable, so changing the environment alone did not fix the client already built with us-east-1.

context.task: Read metadata from a regional bucket in a worker

method: A custom SDK agent in a Node worker. Built S3Client with region us-east-1 from a hardcoded default, ran HeadObjectCommand against an eu-central-1 bucket, then read the bucket region from the console and rebuilt the client.
limitations: One bucket and one worker; cross-region reads at volume were not tested.

summary: Claude Code turned on default SSE-KMS with a customer managed key and bucket keys for an uploads bucket. A test put-object returned the key id in its output. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Bucket keys were enabled in the same put-bucket-encryption call, and the agent confirmed the KMS events in the CloudTrail list for the test writes.
Default encryption applies only to new uploads, so the 14 earlier objects stayed on SSE-S3 until they were copied over.

context.task: Enforce KMS encryption on uploads

method: Claude Code with AWS CLI v2 under an admin role. Ran aws kms describe-key on an existing customer managed key, then put-bucket-encryption with aws:kms and BucketKeyEnabled true, and checked the key id on a test put-object.
limitations: Single region and one key; key rotation and cross-account key grants were not exercised.

summary: Cursor set up static hosting for a docs bundle by turning off Block Public Access on that one bucket and adding a read-only policy. The index page came back 200 from the website endpoint. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Public read needs the bucket-level block turned off first, and the account-level settings were already off for that account.
A missing path returned the error document instead of the index page, which matched the error key set in the website configuration.

context.task: Host a static docs bundle from a bucket

method: Cursor in a plain HTML repo with AWS CLI v2. Ran put-public-access-block with all four flags false on one bucket, applied a bucket policy granting s3:GetObject to principal *, enabled put-bucket-website with index.html and error.html, then curled the index page.
limitations: One bundle of four HTML files; no CDN or custom domain in front of the bucket was tested.

summary: Devin's sandbox resolved the regional S3 hostname, but outbound connections on port 443 were blocked by the egress allowlist. Every SDK call hit its timeout until the session ended. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: DNS lookups succeeded, but the TCP connect on port 443 hung on each call, which looked like a timeout rather than a credentials error.
The SDK surfaced a timeout error after its retries, and the agent spent most of its budget tuning retry counts instead of testing the network path.

context.task: Upload a build artifact to a bucket from a sandbox
context.blocker: egress allowlist blocks port 443 to S3

method: Devin in a cloud sandbox with @aws-sdk/client-s3 installed and credentials set through environment variables. Ran PutObjectCommand from a Node script, raised the retry count and timeout, then tried the AWS CLI v2 before the session ended.
limitations: Only the sandbox network was tested; the same script was not run from a laptop or CI runner.

summary: Aider ran a list call from a Docker container on a laptop and got RequestTimeTooSkewed. The VM clock had drifted, and resyncing it let the next call pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: RequestTimeTooSkewed failed every call until the VM clock was resynced, and the traceback alone did not say the clock was the cause.
Comparing the date inside the container with the host date showed a gap of several minutes, which explained the rejection.

context.task: List objects from a local dev container

method: Aider in a Python project with boto3 and a list_objects_v2 smoke test run inside a Docker container on macOS with Docker Desktop. Compared the container date with the host, resynced the Linux VM clock, and reran the same script.
limitations: Only one laptop was tested; the drift was not reproduced on a Linux host or a second machine.

summary: Claude Code added a presigned POST form for direct uploads with a 10 MB size cap enforced by the signed policy. A deliberately oversized test file was refused and a 2 MB PNG was stored. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The content-length-range condition rejected the 14 MB test file with a policy condition error and accepted the 2 MB PNG on the same form.
The helper returns a url and a fields map, and the form needs every field placed before the file part or the upload is rejected.

context.task: Let browsers upload avatars directly with a size cap

method: Claude Code worked inside a Next.js app with the App Router. Used createPresignedPost with Conditions for content-length-range 0 to 10485760 and an exact image/png match, then posted from a small HTML form to test it.
limitations: Two local test files from one machine; cross-origin behavior and retry handling were not exercised.

summary: Codex wired ObjectCreated events on an intake bucket to an SQS queue. After the queue policy let the S3 service principal send messages, a test upload produced one message. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The queue policy allowed the S3 service principal to send messages with a condition on the source bucket ARN, and it was written before the notification config was applied.
The SQS message body held a JSON document with a Records array, and the object key came through URL-encoded with plus signs for spaces.

context.task: Trigger a worker when files land in a bucket

method: Codex CLI with the AWS CLI v2. Created the SQS queue, attached a queue policy with aws:SourceArn set to the intake bucket, applied put-bucket-notification-configuration with an s3:ObjectCreated:* filter, then uploaded one JSON file to test.
limitations: One intake prefix and one queue; the dead-letter queue setup was not tested.

summary: Windsurf's browser PUT to a presigned URL failed preflight because the bucket CORS AllowedHeaders list left out Content-Type. Adding it made the upload return 200. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The preflight response lacked Content-Type in Access-Control-Allow-Headers, so the browser blocked the PUT before it left the page.
The devtools console showed a generic CORS error with the request marked blocked, and the S3 response itself never appeared.

context.task: Upload a file from the browser to a presigned URL

method: Windsurf in a React app built with Vite, with the presigned URL from a Node route. Ran the browser PUT from localhost, read the failed preflight in devtools, added Content-Type to AllowedHeaders, and retried.
limitations: Only the localhost origin was allowed; production origin CORS and a second browser were not tested.

summary: A custom agent tried to create a bucket named test-uploads. S3 returned BucketAlreadyExists because bucket names are global, and the run ended without a usable name. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Bucket names share one global namespace, so a generic name collided with a bucket owned by another account on the first create call.
The agent retried the create call with the same name three times and got BucketAlreadyExists each time before the run stopped.

context.task: Create a bucket for test uploads

method: A custom SDK agent in a Node worker with a CreateBucketCommand call in us-east-1 and no location config. Retried with the same bucket name three times before the time budget ran out.
limitations: One account and one naming scheme; no prefix or suffix pattern was attempted.

summary: Claude Code tagged three test objects with retention=short and added a lifecycle rule that expires only tagged keys after 7 days. Both calls applied on the first try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The lifecycle filter matched on the tag, and untagged objects under the same prefix were left alone during the test run.
The test object carried two key value pairs, which kept the call well inside the per-object tag limit.

context.task: Expire only tagged test objects after a week

method: Claude Code in a shell with AWS CLI v2 and an SSO profile. Ran put-object-tagging on three test keys, wrote a lifecycle JSON with a Filter Tag entry and Expiration Days 7, applied it, and listed the rules back.
limitations: Three test objects under one prefix; the seven day expiry itself was not observed to run.

summary: Cline added a route that returns a presigned GET with a ResponseContentDisposition value, so the browser saves the PDF under a readable name. The first click produced a download with that name. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: generate_presigned_url passes ResponseContentDisposition through to the response, so the file name comes from the call and not from the stored key.
The stored key includes a dated folder, which would have shown up in the download name without the override.

context.task: Serve a PDF download with a readable file name

method: Cline in a Flask app with boto3. Added a route that calls generate_presigned_url with ClientMethod get_object, ExpiresIn 900, and Params holding Bucket, Key and ResponseContentDisposition. Opened the returned link in a browser.
limitations: One PDF of about 300 KB; large files and range requests were not tested.

summary: OpenHands looked for a deleted report with list_objects and found nothing. list_object_versions showed a delete marker on top, and removing that marker restored the object on the second attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: list_objects skips noncurrent versions and delete markers, so the deleted file stayed invisible until list_object_versions was called.
Deleting the delete marker by its VersionId restored the object without copying bytes, and the file kept its original size.

context.task: Recover a file deleted from a versioned bucket

method: OpenHands in a Python script with boto3 against a versioned bucket. Ran list_objects_v2 under the prefix, then list_object_versions with the same prefix, filtered DeleteMarkers, and called delete_object with that version id.
limitations: One prefix holding a few hundred versions; lifecycle expiry of noncurrent versions was not in play.

summary: Cursor wrote a Node batch uploader with p-limit set to eight parallel PUTs. About 1,200 small JSON files went up in roughly four minutes with no throttling errors. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Eight parallel PutObject calls kept the upload steady, and no SlowDown responses appeared in the logs.
The median PutObject latency was about 180 ms from the build host in us-east-1, so the batch was bound by request count.

context.task: Upload 1,200 small JSON files in a batch

method: Cursor in a TypeScript script run with tsx on a Linux CI runner. Read the files, wrapped each PutObjectCommand send in p-limit with concurrency 8, set ContentType application/json, and logged the elapsed time at the end.
limitations: All files under 50 KB; larger objects and multipart behavior were not measured.

summary: Goose started a copy job of 18,000 objects with short-lived SSO credentials. The session expired midway, and every later copy-object call failed with ExpiredToken until the agent stopped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The temporary credentials ran out before the copy job finished, and the job had no refresh step, so later calls all returned ExpiredToken.
The copy loop wrote no checkpoint, so after the failure the agent could not tell which keys had already been copied.

context.task: Copy 18,000 objects to a new prefix

method: Goose in a shell with an AWS CLI v2 loop that calls s3api copy-object for each key from list-objects-v2. Started on an SSO profile and did not refresh the login, then stopped after ExpiredToken errors filled the log.
limitations: One 18,000 key prefix; a longer role session with a refresh step was not tried.

summary: Aider ran aws s3 sync with --delete against a dist folder after a dry run. The dry run listed 14 uploads and 2 deletes, and the real sync matched those counts. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The --dryrun flag printed each planned upload and delete, which the agent used to confirm the deletes before running the real sync.
The --delete flag removes bucket keys that are absent from the local folder, so the agent scoped the run to the app prefix to keep other keys safe.

context.task: Mirror a static build folder to a bucket prefix

method: Aider in a Vite project after npm run build. Ran aws s3 sync on the dist folder to the app prefix of the bucket with --dryrun and --delete, reviewed the plan output, then ran the same command without the dry run flag.
limitations: One static build of about 16 files; large assets and versioned delete behavior were not checked.

summary: Claude Code uploaded a PDF with put-object and no content type, so the browser offered a download instead of a preview. A copy-object onto the same key with metadata-directive REPLACE fixed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: S3 stored the upload as binary/octet-stream because put-object got no ContentType, and the browser treated the PDF as a file to download.
Changing the stored content type means copying the object onto itself with the new value, which the agent did only after the first preview failed.

context.task: Make an uploaded PDF preview in the browser

method: Claude Code in a shell that ran aws s3api put-object for a PDF export, then loaded the object URL in Chrome. Ran aws s3api copy-object onto the same key with metadata-directive REPLACE and ContentType application/pdf, then reloaded.
limitations: One PDF in one bucket; the same fix was not checked for thumbnails or other binary types.

summary: Codex restricted an origin bucket to a CloudFront distribution through an Origin Access Control policy. Direct object URLs returned 403, and requests through the distribution kept returning the file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The bucket policy allowed the CloudFront service principal with a condition on the distribution ARN, which cut off the old public read path.
Requests through the distribution returned 200 right after the bucket policy was saved, so no cache flush was needed for the test.

context.task: Hide an origin bucket behind a CDN

method: Codex CLI with AWS CLI v2. Created an OAC with create-origin-access-control, pointed the distribution origin at it with update-distribution, applied a bucket policy scoped to the distribution ARN, and tested direct object reads from a laptop shell.
limitations: One distribution and one prefix; signed URL and private content flows were not covered.

summary: Windsurf deployed a VPC-attached Lambda that uploads to S3 with no gateway endpoint and no NAT route. Calls timed out for the whole run, and the agent stopped without a working path. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The function sat in private subnets with no route to the internet and no S3 gateway endpoint, so PutObject hung until the function timeout.
The timeout traces pointed at the networking gap, while the function logs alone only showed a request that never finished.

context.task: Upload generated reports from a VPC Lambda
context.blocker: no route to S3 from private subnets

method: Windsurf with SAM and a Node.js Lambda attached to two private subnets. Ran PutObjectCommand from the handler and raised the function timeout twice. The gateway endpoint or NAT route was not added before the run ended.
limitations: Only the private subnet layout was tried; a public subnet with NAT was not built in this run.

summary: Custom agent read size and checksum for 500 objects with GetObjectAttributes instead of downloading bodies. The total came to 2.1 GB and matched the inventory report. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Asking for ObjectSize and Checksum returned both in one call per key, so no object bodies were read.
Objects uploaded without an additional checksum returned no checksum field, and the agent recorded those rows as empty rather than deriving an MD5.

context.task: Audit size and checksum for archived objects

method: Custom SDK agent running on Node in a worker. Listed keys under the prefix with ListObjectsV2, called GetObjectAttributesCommand per key with ObjectAttributes ObjectSize and Checksum, and wrote results to a local CSV.
limitations: 500 keys under one prefix; the call pattern at larger key counts was not tested.

summary: Cursor read a GetObject body with String(), which logged the placeholder text instead of the file. Switching to transformToString returned the stored JSON and the parser ran cleanly. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The Body field is a stream in Node, so string conversion produced a placeholder and JSON.parse threw on the first line.
The transformToString helper on the body reads the whole stream and resolves to a string, which replaced a manual chunk loop.

context.task: Parse a JSON config stored in a bucket

method: Cursor in an Express service that loads GetObjectCommand output at startup. First wrote String(response.Body), ran the server and saw the placeholder in the logs, then replaced it with await response.Body.transformToString() and restarted.
limitations: One config file of about 4 KB; large bodies and streaming to disk were not part of this run.

summary: Claude Code enabled versioning on a source and a destination bucket, then added a replication rule to a second region. A test object appeared in the destination about two minutes later. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Replication needs versioning on both buckets, so the agent turned it on for both before adding the rule.
The test object showed up in the destination a little over two minutes after upload, and the source object status read COMPLETED.

context.task: Copy new uploads to a second region

method: Claude Code with AWS CLI v2 under an IAM role. Ran put-bucket-versioning on both buckets, created a replication role with an s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication policy, applied put-bucket-replication with one rule, and uploaded one test file.
limitations: One source prefix and one test object; delete marker replication and existing objects were not checked.

summary: Devin tried to make one uploaded file public with put-object-acl on a bucket where ACLs were disabled. The call failed with AccessControlListNotSupported, and the agent did not reach a bucket policy fix in time. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Newer buckets default to bucket owner enforced, which turns ACLs off, so the ACL call failed no matter what the IAM policy allowed.
The agent spent most of its budget searching for an ACL permission fix before it checked the bucket ownership setting.

context.task: Make one uploaded file publicly readable

method: Devin in a sandbox with AWS CLI v2. Ran aws s3api put-object-acl with public-read on a test object, repeated it after editing the IAM policy, and searched the docs for a permission fix before the session timer ended.
limitations: One test bucket created that week; the bucket policy route for public reads was not completed.

summary: OpenHands used aws s3 cp with --recursive and --exclude for .tmp files to pull 340 log files into a local folder. The local count matched the listing and no temp files came down. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The --exclude filter matched the .tmp suffix against the full key path, so temp files nested in subfolders were skipped too.
The recursive copy finished in under a minute from the workstation, and the local file count matched the listing.

context.task: Pull a folder of log files to a local directory

method: OpenHands in a terminal session with AWS CLI v2. Ran aws s3 cp with --recursive, --exclude *.tmp, and the logs prefix as source, then compared aws s3 ls output with the local file count.
limitations: One prefix with plain text logs under 2 MB each; no compressed or versioned objects.

summary: Claude Code's server-side presigned PUT returned SignatureDoesNotMatch because the browser sent a Content-Type header the URL had not signed. Signing ContentType in the command fixed it on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Any header the client adds that the URL did not sign breaks the signature, and the browser added Content-Type from the file type.
SignatureDoesNotMatch came back as HTTP 403 with a canonical request dump, which made the header difference easy to spot.

context.task: Upload a user file with a presigned PUT

method: Claude Code in a Next.js App Router project, calling getSignedUrl with PutObjectCommand and no ContentType. The browser fetch PUT sent the File with its detected type and got 403. The agent added ContentType to the command, regenerated the URL, and retried.
limitations: One PNG from one browser; other header combinations and mobile browsers were not checked.

summary: Goose ran copy-object onto its own key with a new metadata map. A head-object call afterwards showed the new metadata keys, and the old custom key was gone. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The old user metadata disappeared only because metadata-directive was set to REPLACE in that same call.
head-object returned ContentLength and ETag along with the new Metadata map, which was enough to confirm the change without a download.

context.task: Rewrite custom metadata on an archived file

method: Goose in a Linux shell with AWS CLI v2. Ran aws s3api copy-object with the same source and destination key, --metadata-directive REPLACE, and a new --metadata map, then aws s3api head-object to read the result.
limitations: One object of about 6 MB in a single bucket; storage class and encryption settings were left as they were.

summary: Streamed a 2 GB backup file into the bucket with the Upload helper. Worker memory stayed near 90 MB, and the object size matched the local file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Piping a read stream into the Upload helper kept resident memory flat, and the parts went out with the default queue size of four.
The helper lives in its own package, so the agent installed the lib-storage package before the stream example would compile.

context.task: Upload a large database backup from a worker

method: Custom SDK agent in a Node worker. Created a read stream on the backup file, passed it as Body to the Upload helper from @aws-sdk/lib-storage with queueSize 4 and partSize 16 MiB, then compared head-object ContentLength to the local file size.
limitations: Single backup file on one worker; no failure injection was run to test the retry path.

summary: Triage script for support tickets with the Python SDK. The first run came back cut off mid-JSON at 512 output tokens, and the second run passed after max_tokens went up to 2048. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: stop_reason was max_tokens on one of the four batch calls, so json.loads raised on the unterminated array at the end of that reply.
The category rules went into the top-level system string, and the messages list held only the ticket text.

context.task: Classify 40 support tickets into JSON categories

method: Claude Code in a small Python repo that reads an exported ticket CSV. Wrote one messages.create call per batch of ten tickets, parsed each reply with json.loads, then reran with a higher output cap after the truncation showed up.
limitations: Only the 40-row sample file was run; the full ticket queue was not sent in this session.

summary: Streaming chat route in a Next.js App Router project, forwarding text deltas from the TypeScript SDK to a client component. The browser began rendering text before the upstream response finished. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: client.messages.stream with an on('text') handler delivered deltas, and finalMessage() after the loop returned the usage block.
The route closed its ReadableStream on the message_stop event instead of waiting for the socket to close, so idle connections did not linger.

context.task: Stream chat replies to the browser from a route handler

method: Cursor in a Next.js App Router project. Added a POST route that opens a stream against the Messages API, pipes text deltas into a ReadableStream, and renders them in a client component. Checked with a local dev server and a throttled network profile.
limitations: Tested only on a local dev server; no production traffic or concurrent sessions were exercised.

summary: Weather tool loop in Python failed on the second turn. The tool output went back as a plain user text block, and the follow-up request returned a 400 that the loop could not recover from. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The agent appended the tool output as text without a tool_result block that referenced the tool_use id, and the follow-up call was rejected with a 400.
The input_schema for the city parameter was accepted as written; the failure came only from the follow-up message shape.

context.task: Wire a get_weather tool into a chat loop

method: Codex CLI in a scratch Python project with a while loop around messages.create. Defined one tool with an input_schema for city, ran one sample question, and replayed the assistant tool_use block with the output pasted as plain text.
limitations: Single fake weather tool with a stubbed backend; the real forecast service was never called in this run.

summary: Ran 5,000 product reviews through Message Batches for sentiment labels. Results were matched back by custom_id after the batch finished overnight. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The status check reported in_progress for most of the wait, and the script slept between polls instead of hammering the endpoint.
custom_id was set to the review row number, so the join back to the CSV was a dictionary lookup with no fuzzy matching.

context.task: Label 5,000 product reviews by sentiment in one batch

method: Custom Python agent wrapper using the official SDK. Wrote one JSONL request file with a custom_id per review, submitted it as a single batch, polled the batch status with a 60-second sleep, and joined the result lines to the source CSV.
limitations: Sentiment labels were spot-checked on 50 rows only; no accuracy benchmark was run on this data.

summary: Pulled line items from scanned intake forms by sending each page as a base64 JPEG image block. Every page came back as parseable JSON on the first pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each page went in as an image content block with a base64 source and media_type image/jpeg; the JPEG exports from the scanner were used as-is.
The prompt asked for a fixed set of keys per line item, and no reply needed a second pass for missing fields across 12 pages.

context.task: Extract line items from 12 scanned intake pages

method: Cline in a Node script under a scratch folder. Read each scanned page from disk, encoded it as base64, sent one messages.create per page with a JSON schema in the prompt, and wrote the parsed rows to a CSV. Ran against all 12 pages in one pass.
limitations: The 12 pages were clean scans of typed forms; handwriting and skewed photos were not part of this run.

summary: Chat widget on a static marketing site tried to call the API from the browser. The SDK refused to run client-side without an explicit flag, and the run was abandoned before any key handling was settled. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The TypeScript client threw on construction in the browser bundle until dangerouslyAllowBrowser was set, and the agent stopped there rather than ship a key in the page.
The site was a static export with no server routes, so there was no place to hold the key without adding a backend.

context.task: Add a chat widget to a static marketing site

method: Windsurf in a static-export site. Added a React chat component that imported the TypeScript SDK and constructed the client in the browser bundle, then ran the dev server to check the console.
limitations: Only the local dev build was checked; no production bundle or deployment target was tried in this session.

summary: Long system prompt with cache_control stopped hitting the cache on every request. A timestamp at the top of the system text changed each call, so the second run recovered only after moving it into the user turn. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: cache_read_input_tokens stayed at zero across 30 calls while cache_creation_input_tokens grew on each one, which pointed at a changing prefix.
Placing the cache_control marker on the last system block, with the timestamp moved below it, produced cache reads from the second call on.

context.task: Cache a 9,000-token system prompt for a support bot
context.docs_vs_reality: cache hits needed an identical prefix, which the timestamp broke

method: Claude Code editing a Python support-bot service. Added a cache_control breakpoint to the system block, ran 30 sample conversations, read the usage fields from each response, and then moved the per-request timestamp into the user message.
limitations: Measured only on a replayed set of 30 conversations; no live traffic or long idle gaps between requests were tested.

summary: Counted tokens for a 180-page policy handbook before deciding chunk sizes. The count endpoint gave a total in one call, and the chunker was sized to fit under the input limit with headroom. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: messages.count_tokens returned input_tokens for the full document in a single round trip, so no local tokenizer was needed.
Chunks of about 40 pages each came in well under the input limit, and the count call was cheap enough to run before every job.

context.task: Size chunks for a 180-page policy handbook

method: Goose with a Python script in a scratch folder. Read the handbook text, called messages.count_tokens with the full text in one user message, then split the text into 40-page chunks and counted each chunk before the summary calls.
limitations: Only the one handbook was counted; scanned pages with OCR gaps were not part of the document.

summary: Streaming summarizer got an error event partway through a reply even though the HTTP status was 200. A retry loop with backoff finished the job on the third try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: An overloaded_error arrived as an SSE error event after several content_block_delta events, so the status code alone never signaled the failure.
A retry with exponential backoff around the stream call succeeded on the third attempt and kept the partial text out of the final output.

context.task: Summarize long meeting notes via streaming

method: OpenHands agent in a Node worker that streams summaries for queued meeting notes. Added a wrapper that catches error events on the stream, waits with exponential backoff, and restarts the request from the saved prompt.
limitations: Ran against 25 queued notes on one worker; no sustained load or multi-region tests were done.

summary: Bulk eval runner sent 2,000 prompts with no pacing and kept getting 429 rate_limit_error responses. The agent stopped when its time budget ran out with about 40 percent of prompts scored. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Most requests after the first minute returned 429, and the retry-after header was present but ignored by the runner.
All prompts were dispatched through one thread pool with no shared limiter, so concurrency stayed at the pool size the whole time.

context.task: Score 2,000 eval prompts against a rubric

method: Custom Python eval runner built on the SDK with a ThreadPoolExecutor of 32 workers. Read prompts from a JSONL file, called messages.create for each, and wrote scores to a results file. The run was launched once with no backoff code.
limitations: Single run on one API key with no pacing variant tried, so later throughput numbers are not available.

summary: Forced a single tool call with tool_choice so the reply always came back as an input_schema object for a product card. Every card in the 15-item test set parsed without a repair step. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Setting tool_choice to the named tool meant the reply contained a tool_use block with the schema fields and no free text to strip.
Required fields were listed in the schema, and the parser rejected nothing across 15 items because the model filled each one.

context.task: Turn product blurbs into typed JSON cards

method: Windsurf in a Node script with a 15-item fixture file. Defined a tool with an input_schema for name, price label, and tags, set tool_choice to that tool, and read the tool_use input from the response instead of parsing free text.
limitations: Fixture of 15 synthetic product blurbs; no real catalog data or adversarial inputs were tested.

summary: Raw HTTP script sent messages without max_tokens and got a 400 on every call. The agent spent its budget retrying the same body before it reread the request. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 400 body pointed at max_tokens, but the agent changed the model string and the headers first.
Calling the messages path with requests needed the x-api-key and anthropic-version headers set by hand, which the SDK would have done.

context.task: Call the Messages API from a Python script without an SDK

method: Devin in a sandbox with a standalone Python script that used requests to post to the messages path. Set the model, messages, and headers manually, then retried the same request body after each 400 with small edits.
limitations: Sandbox run without the SDK installed; only the raw HTTP path was tried and no SDK comparison was made.

summary: FastAPI service on Cloud Run calls the Messages API with the key mounted from Secret Manager. The first deploy served a valid reply from the chat route without any config changes. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The key was mounted as an environment variable from Secret Manager, and the SDK read it without any constructor argument.
The first request after idle took about four seconds, most of it container startup and the SDK import.

context.task: Deploy a chat route to Cloud Run

method: Claude Code in a FastAPI repo with a Dockerfile. Added a chat route that calls messages.create, built the image, pushed it, and deployed to Cloud Run with the key mounted from Secret Manager. Tested the route with curl from a laptop after deploy.
limitations: Single Cloud Run service in one region; no traffic split or autoscaling thresholds were tested.

summary: Moved a system instruction into the messages list with role system and the request came back as a 400. Moving it to the top-level system parameter fixed the second call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The messages list accepted user and assistant roles only in this script, and a system entry in the list produced a 400 with invalid_request_error.
A plain string passed as system at top level behaved the same as the earlier prompt text and needed no other change.

context.task: Port a chat prompt copied from another SDK's format

method: Codex CLI porting a small chat script from a messages list copied from another SDK. Kept the instruction message in the list, got the 400, then moved the instruction to the system argument and reran the same test prompt.
limitations: One test prompt and one follow-up turn; no multi-turn or tool calls were exercised.

summary: Node script loads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY from a local .env with dotenv and prints a one-sentence summary of a README. The run finished on the first try once the file sat in the project root. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: dotenv/config was imported as the first line so the SDK constructor saw the key when the client was created.
The quickstart showed the key as an export in the shell, and the agent had to add dotenv on its own for a project file.

context.task: Summarize a README with a Node script

method: Claude Code in a scratch Node project using tsx to run a single file. Installed the TypeScript SDK and dotenv, wrote a small script that reads README.md and asks for a one-sentence summary, then ran it once.
limitations: One README in a fresh scratch folder; the script was not tested with multi-file input or a CI secret.

summary: On Windows PowerShell the curl alias mangled the JSON body and the API returned a 400. Switching to Invoke-RestMethod with a hashtable body produced a valid reply on the next attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The curl alias on Windows PowerShell passed the JSON with stripped quotes, and the server rejected the body before any model call ran.
Invoke-RestMethod with ConvertTo-Json serialized the body and sent the x-api-key and anthropic-version headers without quoting trouble.

context.task: Smoke test the Messages API from a Windows dev box

method: Goose on a Windows 11 machine with a one-line smoke test. First sent the request with curl in PowerShell, then rebuilt the body as a hashtable and sent it with Invoke-RestMethod, reading back the first content block from the reply.
limitations: One smoke test on one Windows machine; no WSL or macOS comparison was run.

summary: Replay harness pushed a chat backend through 120 scripted turns with a helper that trims history before each call. No request was rejected for size, and the reply latency stayed flat across the run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Trimming happened before each call and kept the system prompt plus the last 20 turns, so the reply never waited on a second request to fit the window.
A 120-turn replay used a canned user script and finished without a single rejected request.

context.task: Keep a long chat session inside the request size

method: Cursor in a FastAPI service. Added a helper that keeps the system prompt and the last 20 turns before calling messages.create, then ran a replay harness of 120 scripted turns against the local server.
limitations: Replay used scripted turns only; real user messages with long pasted content were not part of the run.

summary: Batch job script tried to fetch results while the batch was still processing and got an error instead of rows. A second run that waited for the ended status wrote all 800 classifications. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script read the results URL as soon as the job was created, which failed because the batch still showed in_progress.
The batch section described the processing_status field, and the script only checked for its presence instead of the ended value.

context.task: Classify 800 tickets through a batch and save the results
context.docs_vs_reality: docs said to poll status; script assumed completion

method: Aider in a Python repo with a batch submit script. Created the batch from a JSONL file, then wrote the results reader. The first run tried the results before the status changed to ended; the second run polled until ended and wrote one CSV row per custom_id.
limitations: Single batch of 800 short tickets; no larger batch or cancellation path was exercised.

summary: Nightly GitHub Actions job posts a fixed prompt to the messages path with curl and writes the reply to the job summary. The secret was read from repository settings and the job passed on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The step piped the content text through jq and appended it to GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, so the rendered output read as a short markdown report.
The API key came from the repository secret and appeared only as an env value in the step, so the workflow log stayed clean.

context.task: Post a nightly changelog digest to the job summary

method: Codex CLI wrote a workflow file with a single job on a hosted Ubuntu runner. The step builds a JSON body with jq, calls the messages path with curl, and writes the reply text into the job summary.
limitations: Ran only on the default branch with a fixed prompt; pull request triggers and forked branches were not covered.

summary: Tool definition for a calendar lookup had a trailing comma in its JSON schema, so the request body never parsed. The devin run ended on the second retry without a valid call to the API. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A stray trailing comma after the last property in input_schema broke JSON.parse before any HTTP call was made, so the error came from local code.
The parse error pointed at line 41 of the tools file, which was useful, but the agent edited the wrong object first.

context.task: Add a calendar lookup tool to a scheduling bot

method: Devin in a Node scheduling bot. Added a tool entry with an input_schema for date and attendee fields, then ran the bot against one sample request. The run stopped after the second failed attempt to parse the tools file.
limitations: Stub calendar backend; the run ended before any real calendar call was attempted.

summary: FastAPI handler switched from the sync client to the async client so concurrent chat requests stopped blocking each other. A local load of 20 parallel requests finished without queueing. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The sync client call inside an async route held the event loop, so a second request waited for the first reply to finish.
AsyncAnthropic with await messages.create kept the loop free, and the handler logic stayed the same.

context.task: Stop concurrent chat requests from blocking in FastAPI

method: Claude Code in a FastAPI service with uvicorn. Replaced the sync client construction with AsyncAnthropic, awaited messages.create in the route, and drove 20 parallel requests with a small async load script.
limitations: Local uvicorn with a single worker; no multi-worker deployment or real network latency to the API was measured.

summary: Image question in aider failed on the first call because source.data held a full data URL. Stripping the prefix and keeping media_type separate fixed it on the second call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: source.data expects the bare base64 payload, so a prefixed data URL string was rejected with a 400.
Sending media_type image/png for a PNG screenshot worked once the prefix was gone.

context.task: Ask a question about a UI screenshot

method: Aider in a Python script that loads one PNG screenshot. Encoded the file with base64 and built an image content block first with a data URL prefix, then removed the prefix on the retry and reran the same question.
limitations: One screenshot of a single settings page; no multi-image messages or large files were sent.

summary: Summarized 14 meeting transcripts by chunking each one at paragraph breaks and merging the chunk summaries in a second pass. The final notes for all 14 meetings were written without manual edits. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A second call that merged chunk summaries kept action items grouped by owner, which the single-pass prompt had not done.
Speaker labels were stripped before chunking, so the model did not have to infer who said what from the speaker tags.

context.task: Write notes for 14 meeting transcripts

method: Claude Code with a Python script in a notes repo. Split each transcript at paragraph breaks into chunks under a fixed token budget, summarized each chunk, then ran one merge call per meeting to produce owner-grouped action items.
limitations: Transcripts were internal test recordings with two speakers each; larger meetings and crosstalk were not covered.

summary: Chat call returned 404 not_found_error because the model string had a trailing space copied from a docs page. Trimming the string and rerunning the smoke test returned a normal reply. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A trailing space after the model identifier turned an otherwise valid call into a 404 with not_found_error.
The error body named the model in its message, which made the stray space easy to find in the request log.

context.task: Smoke test a chat call in a Node script

method: Cursor in a Node script run with tsx. Copied the model identifier from a docs page into a constant, ran the call, and after the 404 trimmed the constant and reran the same prompt.
limitations: One smoke test in a local script; no other model identifiers were tried after the fix.

summary: Eval harness logs input and output tokens per case from the usage block, so token spend per rubric can be compared across 60 cases. The totals matched the billing dashboard totals for the sample day. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each response carried input_tokens and output_tokens, and the harness summed them per case without estimating locally.
cache_read_input_tokens was zero on every case because the rubric prompt changed per row.

context.task: Log token spend per eval case

method: Custom Python eval harness built on the SDK with pytest fixtures. Each case records the usage object from messages.create into a SQLite table, and a summary query groups tokens by rubric name.
limitations: Sample of 60 cases on one rubric; no multi-rubric or retry-heavy runs were included.

summary: Installed an old SDK major by accident, and the import the sample relied on did not exist in that release. The run ended on the third install attempt without a working client. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The sample failed at import time under the older major, and the error named a missing attribute on the client module.
The lockfile was never regenerated, so pip kept resolving the old major on every reinstall in the sandbox.

context.task: Run a sample script against the Messages API

method: Codex CLI in a sandbox with a pip-managed virtualenv. Installed the Python SDK from a requirements file that pinned an older major, then ran the sample import. Reinstalled three times without touching the pin.
limitations: Single sandbox image with a stale requirements file; the current major was not installed in this run.

summary: Node CLI reads a diff from stdin and asks for a commit subject in the imperative mood. Piping git diff through it produced a one-line subject on the first try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script read process.stdin to the end before calling the API, which made the pipe from git diff work without temp files.
max_tokens was set to 120, and the subject line never came close to that cap.

context.task: Draft commit subjects from a staged diff

method: Goose in a scratch Node package with a single entry file. Read stdin until EOF, sent the diff in one user message with a short system instruction, and printed the first line of the reply. Tested with a git diff pipe.
limitations: Tested only on small diffs under a few hundred lines; very large diffs were not sent.

summary: Agent tool loop kept asking for the same file read because each tool_result sent an empty string. A loop cap of eight rounds stopped it, and the second run returned the file text correctly. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: stop_reason stayed tool_use for eight rounds because the tool output was an empty string, so the model kept asking for the same file.
A hard cap of eight rounds ended the loop with a clear log line, which made the empty-output bug easy to spot.

context.task: Let an agent read files via a tool loop

method: OpenHands running a Python tool loop with a read_file tool. First run returned empty strings from the tool handler, so the model asked for the same path repeatedly until the eight-round cap. Second run returned file text and the loop finished in three rounds.
limitations: Read tool limited to one fixture directory; no large files or concurrent tool calls were tested.

summary: Extracted the payment terms section from a 6-page PDF by sending it as a base64 document block. The reply quoted the right clause on the first attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The PDF went in as a document content block with a base64 source, and the question sat in a text block after it.
The quoted clause matched the source paragraph word for word on the spot check.

context.task: Pull payment terms from a 6-page PDF

method: Windsurf in a Python script in a sample folder. Read one PDF as bytes, base64-encoded it into a document block, added a text block asking for the payment terms section, and printed the reply.
limitations: One six-page text PDF; scanned PDFs and PDFs with embedded tables were not part of this run.

summary: Multiple-choice labeler used a stop sequence after the closing parenthesis, so replies stayed to one letter and the parser never had to trim prose. It matched the answer key on 47 of 50 sample items. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A stop sequence on the closing parenthesis cut the reply right after the letter, and stop_reason came back as stop_sequence.
Three replies came back with a leading space before the letter, which the regex had to allow for.

context.task: Label 50 multiple-choice items with one letter each
context.docs_vs_reality: stop sequences behaved as the docs describe

method: Custom Python labeler using the SDK in a small pipeline. Set stop_sequences to a closing parenthesis, prompted for one letter per item, and compared parsed letters with a 50-row answer key stored as CSV.
limitations: Fifty items from one quiz set; no other subject areas or harder distractors were included.

summary: Jupyter notebook loads the API key from the kernel environment and asks for a short table summary of a CSV. Each cell ran in order after the notebook restart. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Keys exported in the shell before launching Jupyter were visible to the kernel, so the client needed no extra setup.
Restarting the kernel reset the client object, and rerunning the first cell rebuilt it cleanly.

context.task: Summarize a sales CSV in a notebook

method: Cline in a Jupyter notebook under a scratch folder. Created the client in the first cell, loaded a CSV with pandas, passed a trimmed table as text in the prompt, and printed the summary in a markdown cell.
limitations: Single notebook on a sample CSV of about 400 rows; kernel restarts beyond one were not tested.

summary: Next.js middleware imported the Node-only SDK path and the build failed on the edge runtime. The agent tried a route handler move, but the attempt budget ran out before the build passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Importing the SDK in middleware pulled in Node-only modules, and the build step stopped with an error naming the unsupported module.
The routing notes covered edge middleware limits, but the agent did not read them before writing the import.

context.task: Gate a chat route in middleware before the API call

method: Windsurf in a Next.js App Router project. Added a chat call inside middleware.ts that imported the TypeScript SDK, ran the production build, then iterated on the import error twice before the route handler move, and the attempt budget ended before the build passed.
limitations: Build-only check on one Next.js project; the deployed edge behavior and a route handler version were not verified.

summary: Tone classifier uses eight few-shot examples in the system prompt and returns one label per message. On a held-out set of 200 messages the labels were consistent across two reruns. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Eight short examples in the system block kept the labels stable, though the two reruns disagreed on four messages.
Asking for one lowercase word per message meant the reply needed no parsing beyond a strip.

context.task: Label message tone for a support queue

method: OpenHands in a Python repo with a labeling script. Built a system prompt with eight examples, ran it on 200 held-out messages twice, and compared the two label files line by line.
limitations: Held-out set was drawn from one support queue; no other channels or languages were included.

summary: CI job failed with 401 authentication_error because the repository secret was not exposed to that workflow's environment. Adding the secret to the right environment and rerunning fixed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The secret existed at repository level, but the job referenced a deployment environment name, so the variable came through empty.
The 401 body named authentication_error, which pointed at the key and not the request shape.

context.task: Run a nightly eval step in CI

method: Claude Code editing a GitHub Actions workflow for a Python eval step. The first run failed on a missing key; the second run added the secret scope to the job's environment block and reran the same eval subset.
limitations: One workflow on the default branch; no environment protection rules or required reviewers were configured in this run.

summary: Extracted contract dates and party roles from 30 text snippets through a tool schema with required fields. All 30 came back as objects, and the parser needed no regex fallback. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Listing four fields in required meant each returned object had all four keys, including the ones the text did not mention, which were set to null.
Dates came back in mixed formats on a first draft of the schema, and asking for ISO 8601 in the field description fixed that before the final run.

context.task: Pull contract dates and party roles from snippets

method: Codex CLI in a Python script with a tool definition named record_terms. Defined four required properties, set tool_choice to that tool, and looped over 30 snippet files, writing each returned input object to a JSON lines file.
limitations: Thirty synthetic snippets written for the test; real signed contracts with scanned signatures were not used.

summary: Batch submission reused the same custom_id for two different prompts, so the results could not be matched back to the rows. The agent abandoned the batch after the results file arrived without a clean mapping. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Both review rows had custom_id set to the same value because the loop variable was not incremented, so the join produced duplicate labels.
The results file had 1,400 lines for 1,400 requests, and the mapping was still ambiguous because of the repeated ids.

context.task: Label 1,400 reviews through a batch and join the results

method: Cline in a Python batch script. Built the request file in a loop that forgot to advance a counter, submitted the batch, and then tried to join the results on custom_id against the source CSV.
limitations: One batch of 1,400 requests from a sample CSV; no resubmission was attempted after the join failed.

summary: Usage logger appends input_tokens and output_tokens from each response to a CSV, grouped by feature flag. The first week of sample traffic produced one row per call with no gaps. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Every response included usage with input and output counts, so the logger needed no tokenizer dependency.
A thin wrapper around messages.create wrote the row after the call returned, which left failed calls out of the CSV.

context.task: Log per-feature token usage to CSV

method: Aider in a Python package with a single wrapper module. Added a function that calls messages.create and appends a row with the usage fields, then ran a sample of 25 calls against a test setup.
limitations: Ran 25 sample calls against one test setup; the feature-flag grouping was not checked against real traffic.

summary: First run hit a 429 during a burst of 30 requests and the SDK's built-in retry absorbed it. Wall time roughly doubled, but the run completed without changes to the code. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A 429 with a retry-after header appeared after the 22nd request, and the SDK waited before retrying.
Total time roughly doubled compared with the earlier pilot, which had fewer requests in flight.

context.task: Run a 30-prompt batch of rewrites

method: Claude Code running a Python script that loops over 30 rewrite prompts with a thread pool of four. Ran the script with default SDK settings, and the 429 was absorbed by the SDK retry before the run finished without any code changes.
limitations: One burst of 30 short prompts on a single key; sustained load and longer prompts were not tested.

summary: Release notes generator reads git log between two tags and drafts grouped bullets. Every commit from the range appeared in the draft, and two grouping mistakes were fixed by hand. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Prefixes like feat and fix were used as hints in the prompt, and the model still placed two commits in the wrong group.
Passing the log with one commit per line and a short hash prefix kept the input under 6,000 tokens for 180 commits.

context.task: Draft release notes between two tags

method: Cline in a Node CLI in a monorepo. Ran git log between two tags with a fixed format, passed the lines to messages.create with a grouping instruction, and printed the markdown draft to stdout for review.
limitations: Single release range of 180 commits in one repo; scoped packages and squash-merged PRs were not covered.

summary: Pull request from a fork ran the eval job and got a 401 because repository secrets are not passed to fork workflows. The agent stopped without a working key for that run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Secrets were empty for the forked pull request, and the eval step failed with a 401 before any prompts were sent.
The workflow file had no guard for forked branches, so the failure looked like a broken key instead of a missing secret.

context.task: Run an eval step on a community pull request

method: Devin reviewing a fork pull request against a workflow that runs the Python eval on pull_request events. Read the job logs, traced the empty secret, and stopped before adding any guard or fallback key to the workflow.
limitations: Single fork PR on a test repo; no maintainer-approved run or pull_request_target variant was tried.

summary: Localized 240 UI strings into four languages with a JSON output contract and placeholder checks. The placeholders in each translated string matched the source on the final pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Strings with curly placeholders came back intact in 236 of 240 cases, and the four failures were retranslated after a regex check.
The reply was a JSON object keyed by string id, so merging into the locale files needed no reshaping.

context.task: Translate 240 UI strings into four locales

method: Cursor in a React app with JSON locale files. Sent strings in batches of 40 with ids as keys, required a JSON object back, ran a regex check for curly placeholders, and retranslated only the mismatches.
limitations: Four target locales and short UI labels only; long help text and right-to-left layout were not reviewed.

summary: FastAPI route parses the model reply into a pydantic model and returns 422 when fields are missing. Across 50 local test requests the parser rejected none of the replies. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The reply was parsed with model_validate_json, and a missing field produced a 422 response in the route rather than a 500.
Asking for JSON only with a fixed key order kept the replies parseable without a fence-stripping step.

context.task: Validate model JSON in a FastAPI route

method: Claude Code in a FastAPI project with pydantic v2 models. Added a route that calls messages.create, parses the text block with model_validate_json, and returns the model. Tested with 50 local requests from a pytest file.
limitations: Local tests against a stub route; no production schema drift or malformed multi-block replies were tested.

summary: Streaming tool call tried to json.loads each input_json_delta fragment, which failed on the first partial chunk. Accumulating the partial JSON until content_block_stop fixed the parser on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Tool input arrived as partial JSON strings inside input_json_delta events, so no single delta parsed on its own.
Parsing the joined string at content_block_stop gave a complete object for every tool call in the test run.

context.task: Stream tool call arguments to a UI

method: Codex CLI in a Node streaming test. Subscribed to the raw stream events, first parsed each input_json_delta chunk on arrival and got parse errors, then buffered the partial string and parsed it at the block stop event.
limitations: Five scripted tool calls with short inputs; long nested arguments and parallel tool calls were not covered.

summary: Sandbox blocked outbound HTTPS to the API host, so every request timed out and the classifier never produced labels. The agent stopped after confirming that no request reached the network. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Requests hung for the full client timeout before raising a connection error, and the sandbox policy showed the outbound rule was off.
The timeout message did not mention the sandbox, so the first two retries looked like API slowness.

context.task: Label 300 texts from inside a sandbox

method: Devin in a sandbox with a default egress policy. Ran the labeling script with the Python SDK, watched four retried timeouts, then checked the network settings and stopped without changing the policy.
limitations: Single sandbox run; the egress policy was not changed, so no successful call from this environment exists.

summary: Turned a 1,200-row CSV of support call notes into a one-paragraph summary per product area in one pass. The output table had seven areas and no empty rows. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Rows were grouped by product area before sending, which kept each request small and avoided a single giant prompt.
A post-run check confirmed each area had a summary, and no area came back empty.

context.task: Summarize 1,200 support call notes by area

method: Windsurf with a Python script over an exported CSV. Grouped rows by product area with pandas, sent one request per group with the notes concatenated, and wrote the summaries to a markdown file.
limitations: One export of call notes with personal fields removed beforehand; redaction rules and long-tail areas were not tested.

summary: Test suite sets max_retries to zero so a mocked 429 surfaces on the first attempt instead of after backoff. The suite ran in under two minutes on 40 mocked calls. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Passing max_retries=0 on the test client made a mocked 429 raise on the first attempt, which made the assertion simple.
With retries left on, the same suite stalled for several minutes on the backoff sleeps.

context.task: Make a flaky-looking client test fail fast

method: Aider in a pytest suite with mocked HTTP responses. Added a fixture that builds the client with max_retries set to zero, then wrote one test for a 429 response and one for a 529 response.
limitations: Mocked transport only; no live API calls were made in the test run.

summary: Agent kept calling the model in a loop because it treated stop_reason end_turn as an error code. It stopped at the time budget after 60 near-identical calls. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The loop checked for any value other than tool_use as a failure, so a normal end_turn reply triggered another request.
No round limit was set in the script, and the agent noticed only after the time budget was spent.

context.task: Build a tool-use loop until the model stops

method: Custom Python agent built on the SDK. The loop called messages.create each round and branched on stop_reason, treating anything except tool_use as a retry trigger. Ran against one sample question with no round cap.
limitations: One sample question and no tools registered; the loop behavior with real tool results was not observed.

summary: Server action summarizes an inbox digest for a signed-in user using the TypeScript SDK on the server only. The digest rendered in the page within one request and no key reached the client bundle. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The client was created inside the server action, so ANTHROPIC_API_KEY never appeared in the client bundle.
The digest took about six seconds on a 20-message thread, which felt slow in the page until a loading state was added.

context.task: Summarize an inbox digest in a server action

method: Cursor in a Next.js App Router app. Wrote a server action that loads the current user's threads, builds one prompt per digest, calls messages.create on the server, and returns text to a client component.
limitations: Single signed-in test account with twenty messages; no large inbox or concurrency test was run.

summary: CI step sends a pull request diff to the API and posts up to five review comments as a PR comment. The comment appeared on the test pull request on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The prompt capped output at five comments, and the parser dropped anything past the fifth without failing the job.
Diffs over about 800 lines were skipped with a log note, which kept the request under the input window.

context.task: Post short review comments on a PR diff

method: Goose writing a Python script run from a GitHub Actions job on pull requests. Read the diff with git, sent it with a comment schema in the prompt, and posted the result through the REST comments endpoint with the workflow token.
limitations: Tested on one test pull request with a small Python diff; generated comments were not reviewed for accuracy beyond a glance.

summary: Node script printed a 401 because ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was undefined; the .env file was read from the wrong folder. Running it from the project root with dotenv pointed at the right path fixed the next run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: dotenv resolved .env relative to the shell working directory, which was a parent folder when the script was launched from a monorepo root.
An undefined key surfaced as an authentication_error at the first call, not at startup.

context.task: Run a summarizer script from a monorepo root

method: Claude Code running a Node script in a pnpm monorepo. First launched the script from the root and got a 401 on the first call; then moved the dotenv config to an explicit path next to the script and ran it again.
limitations: One script in one monorepo on a laptop; no CI runner or Docker image was tested.

summary: Question answering over 40 runbook pages with simple chunk retrieval before each call. The top-three chunk setup answered 18 of 20 test questions with the right section. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Pasting the three retrieved chunks above the question kept replies on the cited sections, and two misses came from chunk boundaries.
Asking for section titles in a fixed list made the answers easy to check against the source headings.

context.task: Answer questions over 40 runbook pages

method: Codex CLI in a Python repo with a folder of markdown runbooks. Split pages by heading, scored chunks by keyword overlap with the question, and sent the top three chunks plus the question to messages.create in each run.
limitations: Keyword retrieval only over one set of 40 pages; embeddings and multi-document questions were not tested.

summary: Replaced live API calls in the test suite with recorded fixtures, so CI stopped spending time on network calls. The suite passed on the first run with 34 tests. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Recorded responses were stored as JSON next to each test, and the replay layer matched requests by model and prompt hash.
The job time dropped sharply once the live calls were gone, and no test depended on a fresh model reply.

context.task: Remove live API calls from CI tests

method: Claude Code in a Python package with pytest. Added a recording fixture that saves SDK responses to JSON files on first run, configured CI to replay them, and kept one live smoke test behind an environment flag.
limitations: Recorded fixtures cover 34 tests on one package; the live smoke test was not executed in CI during this run.

summary: Import failed after the agent installed a package with a similar name by mistake. Reinstalling the official SDK by its documented name and rerunning the script fixed it on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A similarly named package installed without any warning, and the import error did not say which distribution was in the way.
The install line in the quickstart named the official package explicitly, which was the fix once the wrong install was removed.

context.task: Run a first Messages API call from a fresh venv

method: Goose in a new virtualenv. Ran pip install with a guessed package name, hit an import error, then uninstalled it and installed the official SDK from the quickstart line before running the first call again.
limitations: One fresh virtualenv on a laptop; no lockfile or private index was involved in this run.

summary: Large file reads in a coding agent are truncated to 200 lines before being sent as tool_result content, with a note saying more lines exist. The agent asked for the next window only when it needed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Sending a 4,000-line file in one tool_result inflated the input count, so the reader now returns windows of 200 lines.
Two follow-up window requests covered the rest of the file, and the final answer cited the right function names.

context.task: Let an agent read long source files through tools

method: Claude Code editing a Python agent with a read_file tool. Added offset and limit parameters to the tool schema, capped each tool_result at 200 lines, and tested on a 4,000-line module by asking for a function list.
limitations: Tested on one large Python module; binary files and minified bundles were not included in the test.

summary: Prefilled the assistant turn with an opening brace so the model continued straight into a JSON object for classification. All 25 sample replies parsed on the first pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Ending the message list with an assistant turn that began with an opening brace kept replies in JSON with no preamble text.
The closing brace came back in all 25 replies, and json.loads accepted each one on the first call.

context.task: Classify 25 sample tickets into JSON labels

method: Aider in a Python script with a classify function. Built a message list ending in an assistant turn that starts with an opening brace, called messages.create, then parsed the completed JSON object from the reply text.
limitations: Twenty-five sample tickets from one queue; the prefill approach was not compared against a tool-based schema.

summary: Transcribed 25 podcast clips from local files with the Python SDK in one script run. Every clip returned a completed transcript on the first attempt, and the script saved the text next to each source file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The SDK uploaded each local file before creating the transcript, so the script never needed a public link for the audio.
Each transcript reached the completed status after roughly a minute of processing, and the script blocked on the SDK call until then.
The plain text field held the full transcript with punctuation, which was enough for the search index without speaker data.

context.task: Transcribe podcast clips from local files into text

method: Claude Code in a Python project with one script. Set the API key on the SDK from an environment variable, looped over MP3 files in a folder, and called the transcriber with a default config for each file. Wrote each transcript text to a sibling file.
