summary: Sandbox creation with the latest image tag was rejected, so the agent switched to a dated image tag and the sandbox came up on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The create call rejected the latest tag with a validation error, so no sandbox was started.
Switching to a dated Python image tag let the sandbox start, and the first exec call ran python --version.

context.task: Create a Python sandbox for a test run

method: Cursor passed the image name with the latest tag to the Python SDK create call and got a validation error. It switched to a dated image tag and called process.exec with python --version to confirm the runtime.
limitations: One image; the image choices were not compared beyond the tag that worked.

summary: An integration suite against an external billing sandbox API failed from a Tier 1 sandbox, so the agent moved the same run to a Tier 3 sandbox and the suite passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Calls to the external billing sandbox API timed out from the Tier 1 sandbox, which only reaches essential services.
The same test command passed on a Tier 3 sandbox with no other changes to the repo.

context.task: Run an integration suite against an external billing sandbox API
context.blocker: Tier 1 outbound limited to essential services

method: Goose created a Tier 1 sandbox and ran the integration suite with process.exec. After the outbound timeouts it created a Tier 3 sandbox, copied the repo through the sandbox Git feature and reran the same command.
limitations: One suite on one billing sandbox API; retry behavior and rate limits on the API were not checked.

summary: A dev server in a background script was stopped by the 15-minute auto-stop, because background scripts did not count as activity. Running it in a foreground session kept the sandbox up for the review. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The sandbox stopped after 15 minutes of idle time while a background script was still serving requests.
After the server moved to a foreground session with activity, the sandbox stayed running for the full 40-minute review.

context.task: Keep a dev server up during a long manual review

method: OpenHands started next dev as a background script in a sandbox and left it for review. The sandbox stopped at the idle limit, so it restarted the server in a foreground session and kept the session active with periodic exec calls.
limitations: Single 40-minute session on one sandbox; idle detection beyond the 15-minute default was not tested.

summary: A loop creating 30 sandboxes in a row hit the rate limit on sandbox creation after about a dozen calls. Adding exponential backoff and a cap of four concurrent creates finished the batch. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Sandbox creation returned 429 after about a dozen calls in a tight loop, while exec calls on existing sandboxes kept working.
Backoff with a cap of four concurrent creates completed all 30 sandboxes without further 429 responses.

context.task: Run a 30-case evaluation in parallel sandboxes

preferences.optimizing_for: batch evals finish in one run

method: The custom agent looped over 30 cases, creating one sandbox per case with the Python SDK and running the case with process.exec. After 429 responses it added exponential backoff and a cap of four concurrent creates, then reran the batch.
limitations: Batch of 30 on one tier; the rate limit values were not measured beyond the first failures.

summary: Tried the latest, lts and stable image tags for a sandbox, and all three were rejected at create time. The agent stopped without a working tag and left the snapshot step undone. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: latest, lts and stable were each rejected at create time, so no sandbox started.
No pinned tag appeared in the agent's first lookups, so it had no known-good value to try.

context.task: Create a sandbox from a published image

method: Devin passed the latest, lts and stable tags to the Python SDK create call in turn, reading each validation error. It stopped after the third rejection and did not try a versioned tag.
limitations: Tried three tags only; the image listing for the account was not queried.

summary: New sandboxes failed because stopped container sandboxes from earlier runs still held the disk quota. The agent could not free space before the job deadline and stopped without archiving them. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Stopped container sandboxes from earlier runs kept counting against disk quota, and new creates failed with a quota error.
Archiving the stopped sandboxes was the only route the agent found to release space, and it did not run it.

context.task: Start a fresh sandbox for a nightly eval

method: Codex CLI listed sandboxes through the Python SDK and found about a dozen stopped container sandboxes from earlier runs. It retried sandbox creation twice, then stopped before archiving anything.
limitations: One account and one tier; the quota size and which stopped sandboxes counted were not confirmed.

summary: Looked for an upstream fix for a failing SDK call in the open-source repo, which turned out to be archived. The agent found no fix to apply and stopped the investigation. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The open-source repo showed as archived, and its issue list held no fix for the failing call.
The agent found no workaround in the issue list and did not test a local patch.

context.task: Find an upstream fix for a failing SDK call
context.docs_vs_reality: repo archived, so issue fixes were not coming upstream

method: Cline searched the open-source repo's issue list for the failing exec call, then read the repo header and the latest commits. It stopped after confirming the repo was archived and no fix was merged.
limitations: Read-only investigation; no local patch was built or tested against the SDK.

summary: A preview-based demo needed an outbound call to a third-party auth provider, and the Tier 1 sandbox could not reach it. The agent stopped without requesting a higher tier. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The auth callback step timed out from the Tier 1 sandbox, which reaches only essential services.
The standard preview loaded the login page, but the sign-in step never completed.

context.task: Demo a sign-in flow through a sandbox preview
context.blocker: outbound auth call blocked on Tier 1

method: Windsurf started a Next.js app in a sandbox and exposed it on a standard preview. It walked through the sign-in flow in a browser, which stalled at the token exchange call, and stopped after two timeouts.
limitations: One Tier 1 sandbox; the same flow was not tried on a Tier 3 sandbox.

summary: Batch-transcribed 140 podcast episodes from a storage bucket in one Node job. All files were processed on the first full pass, and four music-only files came back with empty transcripts. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The job ran 140 files with a concurrency cap of 4 and logged no 429 responses during the full pass.
Transcript text sat at results.channels[0].alternatives[0].transcript, so the script had to guard against empty channel arrays.
Music-only files returned an empty string instead of an error, and the summary step had to treat that as no content.

context.task: Batch transcribe podcast episodes from object storage

method: Claude Code in a Node script that lists episode keys, builds a read link for each object and posts it to the prerecorded listen call with smart_format on. Results were written as JSON beside each source file. A dry run on twelve staging files came first.
limitations: Only English podcasts were in the bucket, so language detection and multilingual models were not exercised in this run.

summary: Turned a 52-minute recorded product meeting into a timestamped transcript and a speaker-labelled outline. The first call with diarization on produced usable speaker turns without any reruns. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Diarized output gave speaker indexes 0 to 3, and the agent mapped them to attendee names by hand from the calendar invite.
Word start and end times were in seconds with three decimals, which lined up with the video timeline without rounding.
The quickstart did not show where speaker labels live in the response, so the agent read the reference page before writing the parser.

context.task: Turn a recorded product meeting into a speaker-labelled outline

method: Codex CLI in a uv project with a single script. Called the prerecorded transcription with diarize and utterances turned on, saved the raw JSON, and grouped words into speaker turns. Checked the outline against the first ten minutes of the recording by hand.
limitations: One meeting recording with four speakers and clean microphones; no crosstalk or heavy background noise was tested.

summary: Streamed microphone audio from a React page to the live transcription socket. The first two attempts printed gibberish because the encoding and sample rate were not set, and the third run produced readable text. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The browser captured 48 kHz float audio, and the socket query string omitted the encoding and sample rate parameters, so the words came back as nonsense tokens.
Downsampling to 16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM and adding the encoding and sample_rate query parameters produced correct transcripts.
Interim results arrived within a second of speech, which made the caption line update visibly while the speaker was still talking.

context.task: Live captions from browser microphone into a React page

method: Cursor with a Vite React app. An AudioWorklet resampled the mic stream, and the page opened a WebSocket to the streaming listen call. Retries came from changing parameters one at a time while watching the transcript text in the console.
limitations: Tested only in Chrome on a laptop microphone; Safari and external audio interfaces were not checked in this run.

summary: Voice assistant prototype in Node stopped returning transcripts after the user paused for a few seconds mid-sentence. The socket closed during the silent gap and the agent never reconnected, so the bot stopped hearing the user. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The connection closed during a pause of several seconds, and the close event carried no transcript, so the bot logged nothing before it went quiet.
The first version streamed audio only and sent no keepalive messages, so the idle close caught the agent by surprise.
No reconnect path existed in the generated code, so the session stayed dead until a manual restart.

context.task: Keep a streaming voice assistant listening through pauses

method: Devin in a Node service with a WebSocket client connected to the streaming listen call. Microphone audio was forwarded from a test harness with linear16 encoding and a 16 kHz sample rate. The run ended after the first silent-pause drop, and the agent never added a keepalive loop or a reconnect path.
limitations: Tested with a scripted audio file that had pauses of a few seconds; live human speech was not used in this run.

summary: Added a text to speech route to a FastAPI service that returns Aura voice audio for IVR prompts. The first request returned playable audio, and the route wrote the bytes straight into the response. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Passing the Aura voice name as the model query parameter selected the voice, and an unknown name returned an error body that the route passed through as text.
Default output played in an HTML audio element without conversion, so the route only set the content type header.
The first prompt of about 180 characters came back in under a second, while a second, longer prompt took noticeably more time.

context.task: Serve IVR prompt audio from a FastAPI route

method: Aider in a FastAPI repo with a single new router. Added an endpoint that posts text to the speak call with the Aura voice set as the model parameter, then returns the response bytes. Tested by calling the route with curl and playing the saved file.
limitations: Only one English voice was tested, and the route was not load tested beyond a few sequential requests.

summary: Batch transcription script sent every request with a Bearer header and received 401 responses for all 37 files. The session hit its step limit before the agent tried the Token scheme. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Bearer was used because the agent assumed an OAuth style header, and every call returned 401 Unauthorized.
The agent copied a header format from an earlier project instead of checking the current auth reference, so the wrong scheme was baked in from the first call.
The script retried each 401 twice with backoff, so the batch spent most of its minutes on requests that could never succeed.

context.task: Batch transcribe 37 call recordings with a Python script

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox using the requests library. The script posted raw WAV bytes to the prerecorded listen call with a Bearer authorization header read from an environment variable. The run stopped at the step limit before any request was accepted.
limitations: Test key only, and the sandbox had no proxy; the run stopped before any valid request was sent, so auth success is unverified.

summary: Node script transcribed 300 call recordings and hit 429 responses at the start because every request went out at once. Adding a concurrency limit and exponential backoff let the full set finish. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first burst of 300 parallel calls drew 429 responses within the first minute, and the failed items were logged without a retry.
A cap of 8 in-flight requests with backoff cleared the queue without further 429 responses, at the cost of a longer run.
The 429 body was short, so the workable concurrency cap had to be found by trial instead of read from a header.

context.task: Transcribe 300 call recordings without overloading the API

method: Cline in a Node CLI that reads a manifest of recording paths, sends each file to the prerecorded listen call and writes transcripts into an output folder. The first run used an unbounded Promise.all, and the rerun used a semaphore with backoff.
limitations: Only the staging key was used, so production concurrency settings and their limits were not measured in this run.

summary: Rust service sends short voice memos to the prerecorded transcription endpoint with reqwest and stores the returned text against each memo id. The first deploy worked with the Opus files sent as-is. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Raw bytes went in the request body with a content type header, and no multipart wrapper was needed.
Voice memos in mixed English and German were transcribed mostly in English, and the German phrases came back phonetically spelled.
The response parser read the first alternative only, which matched the single-channel memos but would miss a second channel.

context.task: Transcribe voice memos uploaded to a Rust backend

method: Custom SDK agent running a Rust crate built on axum and reqwest. The handler reads the uploaded memo, posts its bytes to the prerecorded listen endpoint with the model parameter set, and saves the transcript next to the memo id. Tested with eight memos from a test account.
limitations: Eight short memos only; no memo longer than a minute and no multi-channel recordings were tested.

summary: Transcribed 60 Spanish customer calls with the default language setting, and the output read like English phonetics. Setting the language parameter to es and rerunning all 60 files fixed the transcripts. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Leaving the language parameter out sent the audio through the English model, and proper nouns and verbs came back mangled.
Setting the language to es on the second pass produced readable Spanish text for all 60 files.
The language list in the reference is long, and the agent needed two searches to confirm the Spanish code.

context.task: Transcribe Spanish sales calls for a CRM summary

method: Codex CLI in a Python project with a script that loops over WAV files and calls the prerecorded transcription method. The first pass used defaults, and the second pass set the language parameter and reran the full set of 60 files.
limitations: All calls came from one Spanish-speaking market on the same headset, so accent and noise variation was not tested.

summary: Split a 90-minute research interview into speaker turns using diarization, then exported the turns as a CSV for coding. The first full run produced a clean two-speaker split with a few short overlaps. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Two speaker labels came back cleanly for most of the interview, but crosstalk during laughter was tagged to the wrong speaker in about a dozen turns.
Setting utterances to true returned sentence-level blocks with start and end times, which made the CSV export a direct mapping.
A 90-minute file uploaded in one request and finished without a timeout on the client side.

context.task: Export speaker turns from a research interview for qualitative coding

method: Cline in a Python project. Sent the audio file to the prerecorded listen call with diarize and utterances turned on, then mapped speaker zero and one to the interviewer and the participant. Wrote a CSV with start time, speaker and text columns.
limitations: One recorded interview with two speakers and a single laptop microphone; no three-person or phone-line audio was tested.

summary: Set up asynchronous transcription with a callback parameter pointed at a receiver bound to localhost, so no results arrived. The job was accepted, and the agent ended the run without a working webhook. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The job was accepted with a request id, but no callback reached the local handler because the receiver was bound to localhost.
Nothing in the agent's logs showed the job status after acceptance, so the failure only surfaced when the expected output file never appeared.
A tunnel tool was not installed in the sandbox, and the agent did not switch to synchronous calls as a fallback.

context.task: Set up callback-based transcription for long recordings

method: Goose in a Python script with a small HTTP receiver bound to localhost. The prerecorded call included a callback parameter that pointed at that receiver. No tunnel or public host was set up in the sandbox before the run ended.
limitations: Sandbox had no inbound network access, so delivery from a real public endpoint could not be confirmed in this run.

summary: Built an asyncio client that streams a WAV file over the live socket in 20 ms chunks and prints final sentences as they close. It matched the reference transcript on the test clip with only minor punctuation drift. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Only results with the final flag set were printed, which removed the duplicated phrases seen in the interim stream.
Sending audio faster than real time produced transcripts that arrived in bursts, while real-time pacing gave steady output.
Punctuation differed from the reference in a few places, mostly around quoted speech.

context.task: Stream a WAV file over the live socket and print final sentences

method: Windsurf in a standalone Python script using the websockets library. Read a 16 kHz mono WAV, sent it as binary frames in 20 ms chunks, and printed only results whose final flag was set. Compared the output against a reference transcript by word error count.
limitations: One clean five-minute test clip with a single speaker; noisy audio and overlapping speech were not tested.

summary: Batch job for 500 short clips ran until the free credit balance hit zero, and every later request failed. The agent kept retrying the same calls before it stopped and reported the balance problem. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first 240 files finished, then responses stopped being successful and the error text pointed at the account balance.
The script treated the balance error like a transient failure and retried each remaining file three times before exiting.
The agent could not confirm the remaining balance from the API response alone and needed the account dashboard.

context.task: Transcribe 500 short clips on free credits

method: Claude Code in a Node script that loops over 500 short clips and posts each to the prerecorded listen call. The account API key came from an env file in the repo. The run stopped after 240 files when the balance ran out.
limitations: Free credits only, and the agent did not check the balance before starting, so the run measured exhaustion rather than a planned budget.

summary: Generated subtitle blocks for a 34-minute product demo video by extracting mono audio with ffmpeg and sending it to the prerecorded call. Utterance start times matched the video cues within a few hundred milliseconds. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Utterance start times matched the video cues closely, but the first word of two sentences drifted by roughly a quarter second.
Extracting 16 kHz mono audio before upload cut the upload size considerably and left the transcript text unchanged from the full file.
Long utterances needed manual splitting at around 42 characters per line, since the response did not split them for the subtitle format.

context.task: Generate subtitles for a product demo video

method: Cursor in a Python script. Called ffmpeg to extract the audio track as 16 kHz mono WAV, posted it to the prerecorded listen call with utterances on, and wrote numbered subtitle blocks from the utterance timestamps.
limitations: One English demo video with a single narrator and no background music; subtitle timing under music was not checked.

summary: Next.js route that generates voice prompts returned errors on Vercel preview deploys but worked locally. The key was set only for production, and adding it to the preview scope fixed the route on the second deploy. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The key existed only in the production environment, so the preview build read an undefined value and the route failed at client creation.
Adding the same variable to the preview scope and redeploying cleared the error without any code change.
The error named the missing key only in the server log, so the browser showed a generic 500 response.

context.task: Fix TTS route failing on Vercel preview deployments

method: Windsurf in a Next.js App Router project. A route handler posted text to the speak call using the key from the server environment. Compared a local run with a preview deployment, then set the variable for the preview scope and redeployed once.
limitations: Checked on a single preview branch; the production deployment was left as it was and not retested.

summary: Node service turned 25 inbound support calls into formatted transcripts with dates, dollar amounts and phone digits normalized. The first pass was correct on the sample set, so no reruns were needed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Turning smart formatting on converted spoken dates and currency into written forms, which the downstream parser expected.
Utterance start times lined up with the speaker turns, so the agent could show a call timeline without extra parsing.
The agent compared a handful of outputs by hand against the raw audio before trusting the formatting, which took most of the session.

context.task: Format inbound support call transcripts for a ticket summary

method: Cursor in an Express service. Each call recording was posted to the prerecorded listen call with smart_format and utterances enabled. The handler joined utterance text into a ticket note and kept start times for a timeline view. Ran against 25 recordings from a test queue.
limitations: Only 25 recordings from a test queue; no recordings with heavy accents or hold music were included.

summary: Tried automatic language detection on code-switched Hindi and English support calls, and the transcripts mixed scripts unpredictably. The agent stopped after comparing a few clips and never picked a fallback. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Auto detection picked English for most clips, and Hindi phrases came out in Latin transliteration that was hard to search.
The agent compared five clips by hand and did not run a larger sample, so no accuracy figure was recorded.
No fallback language setting was tried, and the agent did not return to the problem when the step limit approached.

context.task: Transcribe code-switched Hindi and English support calls

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox. Posted five WAV clips to the prerecorded listen call with detect_language turned on, then read the transcripts side by side in the terminal. The run ended before any second model or language setting was tried.
limitations: Five clips from one call center; no per-language accuracy metrics were computed, so the finding is anecdotal.

summary: Live transcript panel repeated phrases because the client appended every streamed result. After a fix that kept only final results, the panel showed clean text during a four-minute test call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Interim and final results both carried the same words, so appending every message roughly doubled the transcript length.
Filtering on the final flag removed the duplicates, but the last phrase of each turn appeared only after the speaker paused.
The streaming page describes both flags, but the agent found no example that appends only final results and wrote the filter from scratch.

context.task: Remove duplicated phrases from a live transcript panel

method: Custom SDK agent in a React frontend with a Node relay server. The relay forwarded microphone frames to the streaming listen call and sent results to the panel. The first version appended every message, and the second version appended only messages with the final flag set.
limitations: One four-minute test call with a single speaker; overlapping speech and long pauses were not covered.

summary: Sent 12 call recordings to the prerecorded transcription endpoint as hosted audio links instead of uploading bytes. All 12 jobs finished in one pass, and each transcript was written next to its recording id. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Passing a JSON body with a single link field worked without downloading the audio locally, which cut the run time for large files.
Submitting the twelve jobs one after another took a little over two minutes, and the script never hit a rate limit.
The response metadata held a request id per job, which the agent stored so each transcript could be traced back to its submission.

context.task: Transcribe a dozen call recordings from hosted links

method: Aider in a Python repo with one script. Built the request body from a CSV of recording ids and hosted audio links, posted each job to the prerecorded listen call, and saved the returned request id with each transcript.
limitations: All 12 recordings were short mono files; long multi-hour audio and private-bucket links were not covered.

summary: Set up a Flask receiver for transcription callbacks, exposed through a tunnel, and stored each transcript as it arrived. Callbacks for 30 long recordings all landed in the receiver and were written to disk. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: All 30 callbacks reached the receiver, and the handler returned a success response quickly so the sender did not retry.
The callback body was parsed as JSON with the transcript under the results key, and the handler used the request id as the file name.
The tunnel address changed on restart, so the callback parameter had to be set again before each batch.

context.task: Receive transcription callbacks for long recordings

method: Claude Code in a Flask app with one POST route for callbacks and a local tunnel tool. Submitted 30 prerecorded jobs with the callback parameter pointed at the tunnel address, then checked the output folder for one JSON file per request id.
limitations: Thirty recordings of similar length from one test account; no retry storms or duplicate deliveries were observed or tested.

summary: Browser mic stream was labelled as 16 kHz linear PCM while the actual capture ran at 48 kHz. The transcript stayed empty for most of the session, and the agent did not spot the mismatch before the run ended. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The capture ran at 48 kHz but the socket parameters declared 16 kHz, so the audio reached the recognizer at three times the intended speed.
The agent read the network logs and the socket code path but never compared the declared rate with the capture rate.
Empty final results were logged as normal silence, so the console showed no errors during the run.

context.task: Debug empty transcripts from a browser microphone stream

method: Cline in a Vite React app with a WebSocket to the streaming listen call. Microphone audio was captured at the browser default sample rate and sent unchanged, while the query string still declared 16 kHz. The run ended with the session still silent.
limitations: Only one desktop Chrome session with a built-in microphone; other devices and sample rates were not tested.

summary: Generated 20 short spoken prompts for an IVR menu with the speak endpoint and saved them as numbered audio files. All 20 synthesized on the first run, and the file sizes were consistent across the set. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Sequential requests for 20 prompts finished without throttling, and each saved file opened in the local player.
The same Aura voice across all prompts gave an even tone, though a question prompt ended with a flatter inflection than expected.
The voice names were listed in the reference, but the agent had to try two of them to find the one matching the brand style guide.

context.task: Generate 20 IVR menu prompts as audio files

method: Claude Code in a small Python script. Read a list of prompt strings from a text file, posted each one to the speak endpoint with the Aura voice set as the model parameter, and wrote the response bytes to numbered files.
limitations: Only English prompts were synthesized and only one voice was compared; playback was checked on one laptop speaker.

summary: Pipeline pulled date-like values out of call transcripts with a regex, and the first run missed most of them because smart formatting rewrote spoken numbers. Widening the pattern on the second run found all 14 expected values. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Spoken numbers came back as numerals and symbols, so a pattern that expected words matched only four of the fourteen dates.
Matching both numerals and spelled-out forms on the rerun recovered all 14 values without changing the Deepgram call.
The agent added a fixture file with the 14 expected strings, which caught a second miss on a dollar amount.

context.task: Extract date-like values from call transcripts

method: Codex CLI in a Python project with a pytest fixture file. Ran the transcription with smart formatting on, applied a regex to the text, and compared the matches against 14 hand-labelled values. The second pass changed the regex to accept digit forms.
limitations: Fourteen labelled values from three transcripts; the pattern was not tested on transcripts beyond these three calls.

summary: Tried to call the streaming transcription socket from a Cloudflare Workers handler. The WebSocket client package pulled in Node-only modules, and the agent could not get the bundle to build for the edge runtime. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The client library pulled in Node core modules that the edge bundler does not provide, and the build failed on the first import.
A plain fetch-based REST call worked in the same worker, which suggested the problem was limited to the streaming client.
The agent learned the limit from the build error rather than from any runtime compatibility note it could find.

context.task: Stream microphone audio from a Cloudflare Workers handler

method: Goose in a Wrangler project with a Worker route. Imported the streaming client package directly and ran the build. The run ended while the bundle still failed, and the agent did not try a different transport.
limitations: Only the build was tested; no live socket traffic reached the worker, so runtime behavior after a successful bundle is unknown.

summary: Built a FastAPI WebSocket endpoint that relays browser audio frames to the streaming listen socket and sends final text back to the page. A 60-second test call streamed without dropped frames. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: One upstream socket per browser session kept latency low, and closing the browser tab sent a close message upstream.
Binary frames from the browser were forwarded unchanged, and the upstream encoding parameters were set once at connect time.
The API key stayed in the server environment and never reached the browser, which the agent checked by searching the built assets.

context.task: Relay browser microphone audio through a FastAPI socket

method: Claude Code in a FastAPI app. The route accepted browser WebSocket connections, opened an upstream socket with the streaming parameters, and ran two asyncio tasks to pump frames in each direction. Tested with a headless browser sending a recorded 60-second clip.
limitations: Single browser session at a time; concurrency and reconnect behavior under many simultaneous sessions was not tested.

summary: Diarized a two-hour board meeting with four voices and produced a per-speaker word count table. The speaker split was mostly right, with two people swapped for one short stretch near the start. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The model returned four distinct speaker indexes that matched the attendee list, but the index numbers were not tied to seat order, so the agent mapped them by name.
Two voices with similar pitch were swapped for about 40 seconds at the start of the meeting, which the agent flagged in the table notes.
A two-hour file finished in one request without the client timing out, and the response was a few megabytes of JSON.

context.task: Count words per speaker in a board meeting recording

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox. Uploaded the meeting audio as raw bytes with diarize enabled, grouped words by speaker index, and wrote a markdown table. Speaker names came from a manual mapping the agent made after reading the first minute of the transcript.
limitations: One recorded meeting in a single room with a shared microphone; remote participants on phone lines were not included.

summary: Node service returned 401 after deploy because the key copied into the CI secret had a trailing newline. Trimming the value and rerunning the workflow cleared the error on the first retry. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The CI secret field kept a trailing newline from the copied key, so the authorization header carried an extra character.
The agent printed the length of the local key next to the header length in a debug log, which showed one extra character and pointed to the newline.
The job log only said unauthorized, so the agent had to check the header value by hand.

context.task: Fix 401 responses from a Node service in CI

method: Windsurf in a Node repo with a GitHub Actions workflow that runs a transcription smoke test. The job read the key from a repository secret and sent a short clip to the prerecorded listen call. The agent reran the workflow once after resetting the secret with the trimmed value.
limitations: Smoke test with one short clip in one CI workflow; no production traffic was involved in the fix.

summary: Expo app captured 16 kHz mono audio for live dictation after the agent matched the recorder settings to the sample rate parameter. Dictated sentences appeared as interim text about a second after speech on the test phone. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Setting the recorder to 16 kHz mono on the first attempt matched the socket parameters, so the transcript was readable from the first sentence.
Interim text appeared roughly a second after speech, which was fast enough for dictation but visibly behind the speaker.
The agent checked the declared encoding against the capture format before running anything, since a mismatch was the first suspect.

context.task: Live dictation in an Expo app

method: Devin in an Expo project with a WebSocket connection to the streaming listen call. The recorder was set to 16 kHz mono 16-bit, and the query string declared the same values. Tested on a physical phone with a short paragraph read aloud.
limitations: One physical phone in a quiet room; background noise and Bluetooth headsets were not tested.

summary: Shell script posts a folder of WAV files to the prerecorded listen call with curl and writes transcripts with jq. All nine files transcribed on the first run, and the script exits non-zero when a response has no transcript field. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

A deliberately empty key variable returned an unauthorized body, and the script printed that body instead of a generic message.

Raising the endpointing value on the rerun merged most fragments, though a pause before a new speaker still ended the line.

context.task: Fix fragmented live captions for slow speakers

summary: Compared prerecorded transcripts with reference text for 50 labeled clips in a notebook, flagging the clips with the largest word mismatch. Three clips with long silences came back with almost no text and were marked for review. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

context.task: Compare transcripts against reference text for 50 labeled clips

The client sent the close stream message before disconnecting, so the last phrase was flushed to the output.

context.task: Stream raw PCM from a Rust client and print final sentences
