pip freeze inside the sandbox matched the pinned versions in requirements.txt for all 23 entries.

context.task: Set up a pinned Python environment for a data validation job

method: Windsurf in a validation repo using the Python SDK. Uploaded requirements.txt with files.write, ran pip install -r requirements.txt through commands.run, retried after the 429, then compared pip freeze output against the pinned file.
limitations: Single environment with 23 pinned packages; no private index or hashed requirements were tested.

summary: Shift scheduling model solved with OR-Tools inside the code interpreter returned a feasible roster for 14 staff on the first execution. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ortools installed through the cell's pip step, and the CP-SAT solver returned OPTIMAL for the small instance within the time limit.
A 60-person instance hit the time limit without a proven optimum, so the agent kept the 14-person run as the reference case.
The fixed solver time limit in the cell kept the wall time predictable across the two instance sizes the agent tried.

context.task: Draft a shift roster that satisfies coverage constraints

method: Goose in a scheduling repo using the code-interpreter Python SDK. The cell installed ortools, built a CP-SAT model from a JSON file of shift requests, solved it with a fixed time limit, and printed the assignment table in the execution logs.
limitations: Synthetic shift requests only; no union rules or overtime caps from a real labor agreement were modeled.

summary: Edge route that created a sandbox per request failed at build time because the JavaScript SDK pulled in Node-only modules that the edge target could not bundle. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build reported a Node built-in module that was unavailable for the edge target, so the route could not be bundled for that runtime.

context.task: Create a sandbox per request from an API route

method: Custom agent with an LLM loop in a Next.js App Router project. Wrote an edge route file that imported the JavaScript SDK and called Sandbox.create per request, then ran the next build with config tweaks until the stop condition fired.
limitations: Build-only test with no deploy; runtime behavior after a successful build was never reached.

summary: An upload saved as Report.csv was read back as report.csv, and Linux treated the two names as different files until the agent fixed the path. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Linux paths are case sensitive, so files.read on report.csv raised not found while Report.csv sat in the same folder.
A quick ls inside the sandbox showed the exact filename, and the agent used that spelling in every read call after that.

context.task: Read an uploaded CSV inside a sandbox script

method: Claude Code in a Python analysis repo using the Python SDK. Uploaded Report.csv with files.write under a capitalized name, but the reader script asked for report.csv, and after a files.read failure the agent listed the folder and fixed the path.
limitations: One small CSV upload; the folder held no other files, so the listing did not reveal any name collisions.

summary: Generated narration for eight onboarding lessons with one stock voice through the Python SDK. Each lesson produced an mp3 on the first call, and the files played back at matching loudness. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Default mp3 output played in the course player without conversion, so the script only set the file extension.
Using the same voice id and settings for all lessons kept the delivery even, though one long lesson sounded faster near its end.
Playback levels varied slightly between lessons, and the agent normalized them with ffmpeg after generation.

context.task: Narrate eight onboarding lessons with a stock voice

method: Claude Code in a Python script using the Python SDK. Read the lesson scripts from a folder, requested each one with a fixed voice id and the multilingual model, and saved the mp3 bytes beside the lesson file. Loudness was normalized with ffmpeg afterwards.
limitations: Eight lessons of English text from one stock voice; no cloned or designed voices were compared in this run.

summary: Shell script called the text to speech endpoint with curl to make a six-second greeting. The first request returned a playable mp3, and the script printed the file size when it finished. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The key went in the xi-api-key header, and the request failed without it, which was the first thing the agent checked.
The JSON body needed only the text and a model id, and the voice settings fell back to defaults when they were omitted.
Writing the curl output straight to a file produced an mp3 that opened in the default player.

context.task: Generate a short spoken greeting from a shell script

method: Codex CLI in a terminal with a bash script. Called the text to speech endpoint with curl, sent the key in the xi-api-key header from an environment variable, and wrote the response to an mp3 file. Checked the file size with ls.
limitations: One short greeting on one account; no streaming output or long text was requested.

summary: Next.js route streamed speech from the service, but it first collected the full response before returning it, so playback waited several seconds. Passing the stream through directly on the second deploy started audio within about a second. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Reading the whole body into memory before responding delayed the first audio chunk until the entire clip had been generated.
Returning the response body as a stream let the browser start playback while later chunks were still arriving.
The agent's first version followed an older non-streaming example, which had no stream handling at all.

context.task: Stream generated speech to a browser audio element in Next.js

method: Cursor in a Next.js App Router project. The route handler posted text to the streaming text to speech endpoint with the key from the server environment. The first version awaited the full body. The second version returned the body stream and the client attached it to an audio element.
limitations: Tested in Chrome on one desktop with one short paragraph; mobile browsers and very long text were not checked.

summary: Speech script sent requests with an empty key because the environment variable name in the code did not match the one set in the sandbox. Every call returned 401, and the agent spent its remaining steps on retries instead of checking the variable name. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The xi-api-key header was built from an undefined variable, so each request went out with an empty value and returned 401.
The agent retried each request twice with backoff, which added minutes and produced no new information.
The sandbox had the key under a different variable name, and the agent did not print the variable list before it started retrying.

context.task: Generate spoken lines for a 12-line script in a sandbox
context.blocker: empty key from wrong variable name

method: Devin in a Node sandbox calling the text to speech endpoint over plain HTTP. The request builder read the key from an environment variable with a different name than the sandbox defined. The run stopped at the step limit with all twelve lines still unsynthesized.
limitations: Sandbox with a test key; the sandbox environment was reset afterward, so the variable listing could not be checked again.

summary: Rendered one audiobook chapter twice with different stability settings and kept the version the team preferred. The lower stability setting gave more expressive reads, and the two files differed in length by about four seconds. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Stability was set on the request's voice settings object, and the lower value produced visibly wider pitch swings in the same passage.
The agent listened to two excerpts through the player and recorded its choice in the project notes, which was a manual step.
Splitting the chapter by paragraph kept each request short, and the joined audio had no audible seams.

context.task: Compare two voice settings for an audiobook chapter

method: Aider in a Python repo with one render script. Split chapter 4 into paragraphs, sent each paragraph with stability set to two values, and concatenated the mp3 parts with the standard library. Kept the variant the team picked in a notes file.
limitations: One chapter read by one voice; the comparison was made by one listener on laptop speakers.

summary: Generated a 20-second podcast intro for a weekly show in a Node script and wrote the mp3 to the publishing folder. The first render matched the approved script, and the agent confirmed the duration with ffprobe. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The intro text was short enough for a single request, and the output came back in one response with no chunking.
The chosen voice sounded slightly formal for the show's style, so the agent kept it and flagged the tone in the summary.
The output file name came from the episode number, which let the publishing step pick up the right file without a manual rename.

context.task: Generate a short podcast intro from an approved script

method: Cline in a Node project with the JavaScript SDK. Read the approved intro text, requested audio with a fixed voice and the multilingual model, and saved the result as an mp3 named by episode number. Checked the duration with ffprobe.
limitations: One intro in English with a single voice; the show's full episode audio and mixing were not part of this run.

summary: Script requested raw PCM output but saved the bytes with an mp3 extension, so the players rejected the file. Rerunning with mp3 output and a matching extension produced playable audio on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The request asked for a PCM format, but the save step wrote the bytes with an mp3 extension, which no player would open.
Matching the output format to the extension on the rerun gave playable files, and the agent checked one by duration in ffprobe.
The agent had copied the format string from an earlier example, so the mismatch was not caught at write time.

context.task: Save generated speech as playable audio files

method: Windsurf in a Python script with the Python SDK. Requested an output format from the PCM options and wrote the response to a file path ending in mp3. The second run requested mp3 output and kept the same path logic.
limitations: Checked on two sample lines only; the other output formats were not tested in this run.

summary: PHP service generates spoken appointment reminders through plain HTTP calls and stores the mp3 next to each reminder record. Each reminder rendered on the first request, and the stored files played in the admin page. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The built-in HTTP client in PHP posted JSON and read the binary body without a helper library, and the content type header was set explicitly.
Names with accents were spoken correctly in the test set, though one surname was stressed on the wrong syllable.
Saving the bytes under a hash of the text and voice let repeated reminders reuse the same file.

context.task: Render spoken appointment reminders from a PHP service

method: Custom SDK agent in a PHP service. For each reminder, the service sent the text and voice id as JSON to the text to speech endpoint, saved the response under a hash of both, and returned the file path to the admin page. Tested with twelve reminder texts.
limitations: Twelve short test reminders with English names; no live appointment data or peak load was tested.

summary: Batch of 300 audiobook lines ran on a free plan and stopped when the monthly character allowance ran out partway through. The agent kept submitting the remaining lines, each returning a quota error, until the step limit ended the run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Once the allowance was used up, every request returned a quota error with no partial audio.
The script logged quota errors as warnings and did not stop the batch, so each remaining line was submitted and failed in turn.
The agent did not estimate total characters before starting, so the run could not tell whether the batch would fit.

context.task: Render 300 audiobook lines on a free plan

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox using the Python SDK. Looped over 300 lines and requested mp3 audio for each with a fixed voice. The run stopped at the step limit after the allowance ran out at about line 180.
limitations: Free plan on one sandbox key; the allowance size and reset timing were not checked in the dashboard during the run.

summary: Generated narration for a product changelog video with two voices, one for the host and one for the feature walkthrough. The clips were ready in a single pass and aligned to the storyboard timings within half a second. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Switching voice ids between segments kept the host and walkthrough voices distinct without changing any other settings.
Clip lengths came back slightly longer than the storyboard estimate, so the agent trimmed silence from the end of each file.
The multilingual model read the product names without respelling them, which was the main concern in the script review.

context.task: Narrate a changelog video with two voices

method: Codex CLI in a Node project with the JavaScript SDK. Read the storyboard JSON, requested each segment with the voice id assigned to its speaker role, and wrote one mp3 per segment. Trimmed trailing silence with ffmpeg.
limitations: Six segments from one short changelog; long-form pacing and music mixing were not part of the test.

summary: Copied a voice id from the public voice library into the script, and every request failed because the voice was not in the account. The agent did not find the add-to-account step and ended the run with the feature demo unrendered. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The service rejected each request for the library voice id, and the error text pointed to the voice rather than to the key.
A library voice had to be added to the account before the API would accept its id, and the agent looked only at the API reference.
The agent retried the same request several times without listing the account's voices, which would have shown the available ids.

context.task: Render a feature demo narration with a library voice
context.blocker: library voice not added to account

method: Cline in a Node script with the JavaScript SDK. Requested three lines using a voice id copied from the public library page. The run ended after several retries with the demo narration still missing.
limitations: Three lines on one account; no other library voices were tried, so the add step is inferred from the error pattern.

summary: Uploaded a voicemail as multipart form data to the speech-to-text endpoint and got a text transcript back on the first try. The shell script printed the text and the detected language. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The audio went in a multipart form field named file with a model id beside it, and the endpoint returned JSON with the text.
The response included a language code, which the script printed next to the text for the voicemail log.
Background hiss was transcribed as a short word at the start of the clip, which the agent noted in the log.

context.task: Transcribe a voicemail file from a shell script

method: Goose in a terminal session. Posted a 40-second WAV voicemail with curl as multipart form data, set the model id field, and parsed the text and language fields with jq.
limitations: One voicemail with a single caller; no accented speech or overlapping audio was transcribed in this run.

summary: Generated 40 narration lines in parallel and got rate limit errors on about a third of the requests. Adding a semaphore that capped concurrent requests and retrying the failed lines finished the set on the second pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Launching all forty requests at once triggered errors on roughly a third of them, and the successful ones kept their audio.
Capping concurrent requests at a small fixed number cleared the errors on the second pass without changing the voice settings.
The retry wrapper waited a few seconds between attempts, which kept the second pass inside the active limit.

context.task: Generate 40 narration lines without hitting concurrency errors

method: Claude Code in a Python asyncio script. The first version used gather over all forty requests. The second version wrapped calls in a semaphore, retried failed lines after a short wait, and wrote the mp3 files as they completed.
limitations: Forty short lines on one account; behavior under higher concurrency tiers or at sustained load was not measured.

summary: Wrote a script that lists available voices and filters them by accent and gender labels so the team can pick a narrator. The listing returned results on the first call, and the filter matched the labels shown in the dashboard. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each voice carried a labels map with accent, gender and use case entries, which made the filter a simple dictionary check.
The script printed a short table of name, id and accent, which was enough for the team to choose without opening the dashboard.
The agent generated one preview line per shortlisted voice and saved them for the team to listen to.

context.task: List and filter voices by accent for a narrator pick

method: Cursor in a Python script with the Python SDK. Called the voice listing, filtered entries by the accent and gender labels, and wrote a table with name, id and accent. Generated a one-line preview per shortlisted voice.
limitations: One filter run on one account; the shortlist was judged by ear by one person.

summary: Radio spot generator requested 16-bit PCM from the service and converted the result to a WAV with ffmpeg in the same Node script. The first spot played correctly on the first run, and the converted files matched the expected sample rate. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Asking for raw 16 kHz PCM skipped the decoding step, and ffmpeg wrapped the bytes into a WAV container.
The converted files reported the sample rate the script asked for, which the agent checked with ffprobe.
Joining the lines with short silences was done in ffmpeg rather than in the request, which kept the API calls simple.

context.task: Generate radio spot audio as WAV files

method: Windsurf in a Node script with the JavaScript SDK. Requested the 16 kHz PCM output format for each spot line, collected the bytes, and piped them through ffmpeg with the raw input flags to produce one WAV per spot. Checked the header with ffprobe.
limitations: Three spots with one voice on one laptop; no broadcast loudness standard was checked.

summary: Node script wrote the response from the speech endpoint with a text encoding, so the saved mp3 files were corrupted and would not play. Writing the buffer as binary on the second run produced files that played in the player. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Decoding the response body as text before saving corrupted the bytes, and the file size came out about a third smaller than expected.
The agent compared the file header with a known mp3 pattern and found it did not start with the expected bytes.
Writing the raw buffer on the second run produced playable files, and the durations matched the expected length of each line.

context.task: Save speech responses as playable mp3 files

method: Devin in a Node script using plain HTTP calls to the text to speech endpoint. The first version read the response with a text decoder and wrote the string to disk. The second version wrote the array buffer directly.
limitations: Two sample lines checked in a sandbox; playback was verified with a headless player, not on a phone.

summary: Passed the voice's display name where the script expected a voice id, and every request came back not found. The agent kept changing the model field and never listed voices to check the id. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The display name looked like an identifier, so the script sent it unchanged, and each request returned a not-found error.
The agent changed the model id three times while the error stayed the same, which pointed away from the real cause.
The voice listing call was never run, so the agent did not see the id field that the request needed.

context.task: Render a product intro with a named voice
context.blocker: display name used as voice id

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox with the Python SDK. Set the voice argument to the display name copied from the dashboard and requested three test lines. The run ended after the step limit with no audio produced.
limitations: Three test lines in one sandbox; the dashboard view was not compared with the API response for the same voice.

summary: Transcribed a 70-minute meeting recording with word timestamps and generated chapter markers from silence gaps and topic words. The chapter list was written in one pass, and the marks lined up with the recording when spot-checked. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Word timestamps were returned for every token, so the chapter script could find pauses longer than a set threshold.
Speaker tags were not used in this pass, so chapter labels came from keyword matches instead of speaker changes.
Three chapter marks were checked against the audio, and each landed within a few seconds of the topic change.

context.task: Generate chapter markers for a long meeting recording

method: Custom SDK agent in a Python service. Sent the meeting audio to the speech-to-text endpoint with word timestamps on, scanned for gaps longer than the threshold, and wrote chapter markers to a JSON file with start times and a keyword label.
limitations: One recorded meeting with two speakers; chapter quality on multi-hour or noisy audio was not evaluated.

summary: Node server streamed generated speech to a file as chunks arrived and reported the byte count when the stream ended. Three test paragraphs saved in full, and the byte totals matched the stream lengths. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Writing each chunk to the file stream as it arrived kept memory flat, and the script closed the file on the end event.
A partial file from a forced abort was removed by the error handler, which the agent tested by aborting one request.
The first chunk arrived within about a second of the request, while the full paragraph took several seconds to finish.

context.task: Stream speech to a file from a Node server

method: Cursor in a Node script with the JavaScript SDK. Called the streaming text to speech method, piped the response into a write stream, and removed partial files on error. Tested with three paragraphs of different lengths.
limitations: Three test paragraphs in English; the server was not run under concurrent streams or behind a proxy.

summary: Long article narration was sent as one request, and the script's own length cap cut the text mid-sentence. Splitting at sentence boundaries and rerunning produced continuous audio on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A hard character cap in the script cut the article at a random word, and the audio ended in the middle of a sentence.
Splitting on sentence punctuation kept each request under the cap, and the joined audio had no abrupt jumps in pitch.
The second run took about the same time as the first, so the chunking added no meaningful overhead.

context.task: Narrate a long article in full

method: Aider in a Python repo. The first script sent the whole article in one request after a character slice. The second version split the text on sentence ends, requested each chunk separately, and concatenated the mp3 parts in order.
limitations: One article of about two thousand words in English; other languages and very long documents were not tested.

summary: Wrote a cron-friendly health check that requests one short line of speech and fails if the response is empty or late. The check passed on the first run and was scheduled on the team's runner. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The check exits non-zero for an empty body or a non-200 response, so the scheduler reports failures without parsing output.
A single short line returned in about half a second on the test runner, which set the timeout threshold in the script.
The check sends one fixed phrase per run, so its daily usage stays small and predictable.

context.task: Monitor the speech API with a scheduled check

method: Codex CLI wrote a bash script that calls the text to speech endpoint with curl and a fixed short phrase. It checks the HTTP status and the byte count of the response, then exits. The check runs from a cron entry on the team's runner.
limitations: Tested only from one runner in one region; the scheduled run itself was not observed over several days.

summary: Game tutorial hints were rendered with a stability value of 1.5 copied from a forum post, and every request was rejected. The agent treated the rejection as a network problem and never checked the valid range. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The voice settings object accepted only values inside the documented range, and the out-of-range stability value failed validation on every call.
The client retried on any non-200 response, so each hint was attempted up to three times before the run gave up.
The agent looked at connection timeouts and DNS settings first, which were unrelated to the validation error text.

context.task: Render tutorial hint audio for a game

method: Claude Code in a Node script with plain HTTP calls to the text to speech endpoint. Five tutorial hint lines were requested with a voice settings object that set stability above the valid range. The run stopped after the retry wrapper gave up on each line.
limitations: Five short hints on one test key; the valid range was not confirmed in the reference during this run.

summary: Generated localization review clips in four languages with one multilingual model and the same voice id. Each clip rendered on the first attempt, and the reviewers received a folder sorted by language code. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Sending each line in its target language with the multilingual model produced clips the reviewers could follow without reruns.
Folders were named by language code, which the review tool read without extra mapping.
The English-accented voice read the Spanish clip with a slight accent, which the reviewers flagged as acceptable for a demo.

context.task: Render localization review clips in four languages

method: Goose in a Node project with the JavaScript SDK. Read a CSV of strings per language, requested each line with the multilingual model and one voice id, and wrote mp3 files into per-language folders.
limitations: Four languages with about thirty lines each; reviewers were not asked to rate pronunciation beyond a quick listen.

summary: Streaming speech route on a serverless function timed out on long paragraphs, and the client received a partial audio file. The agent raised the timeout setting but did not split the text, so the failure came back on each long input. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Requests for paragraphs longer than a few sentences ran past the function time limit and returned a partial body.
Raising the function timeout helped only for medium-length text, which the agent counted as success before testing longer input.
The agent did not split the text into sentence chunks, which would have kept each request short enough for the function.

context.task: Stream narration from a serverless function

method: Cline in a Next.js project deployed to a serverless host. The route streamed speech for the posted paragraph with plain HTTP. Tests used three paragraphs; the run ended after the longest one timed out on the final attempt.
limitations: Three test paragraphs and one function configuration; behavior on other hosts or with the platform's streaming options was not examined.

summary: Built a 3-minute explainer voiceover by generating each script section separately and placing the clips at timestamps taken from a storyboard file. The sections lined up with the cut points on the first render. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Generating each section as its own file made it simple to re-render one line without touching the rest of the voiceover.
Some sections ran longer than the storyboard slots, so the agent shortened two lines of script instead of speeding up the audio.
Placing clips at fixed offsets with a small assembler script avoided a video editor for this pass.

context.task: Build a timed voiceover for a product explainer

method: Devin in a Python repository. Read the storyboard JSON for section start times, generated each section through the Python SDK, and used ffmpeg to place the mp3 clips at their offsets in one track. Re-rendered two sections after timing checks.
limitations: One three-minute explainer in English with a single voice; mixing with music and sound effects was not part of this run.

summary: Voice output sounded flatter than the dashboard preview until the agent passed voice settings explicitly in the request. After that change, the API output matched the preview on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The request used the service defaults for the voice settings, which differed from the dashboard preview the team had approved.
Passing stability and similarity values explicitly on the second run brought the API output in line with the approved preview.
Nothing in the response indicated which settings were applied, so the agent compared audio by ear.

context.task: Match API speech output to an approved dashboard preview

method: Windsurf in a TypeScript script with the JavaScript SDK. The first run omitted the voice settings object. The second run passed stability and similarity values taken from the dashboard, then rendered the same line for a side-by-side listen.
limitations: One approved preview line; the comparison covered one voice and one line only.

summary: Converted 22 help articles into audio versions for an accessibility page, one mp3 per article with a short intro line. The batch completed in one run, and the page links resolved to the right files. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Long articles were split into sections below the length the script enforced, and the section files were joined in order.
Markdown headings were read as plain text, so the script removed the symbols and read the heading words only.
File names came from article slugs, so the page builder linked each audio file without a lookup table.

context.task: Generate audio versions of help articles for accessibility

method: Codex CLI in a Python project. Read each article's markdown, stripped formatting into plain sentences, split long sections, requested audio per section with one voice, and joined the parts into one mp3 per article.
limitations: Twenty-two articles in English with simple markup; tables and code blocks were skipped rather than read aloud.

summary: Sent a Spanish call recording to the speech-to-text endpoint with the language field set, and the transcript came back in Spanish with accents intact. Four files completed on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Setting the language field explicitly kept the accents and special characters in the transcript, which matched the spot check.
The response did not include speaker separation in this call, so the summary treated each file as one speaker.
A four-file batch finished in a few minutes, mostly waiting on processing rather than upload.

context.task: Transcribe Spanish call recordings with accents preserved

method: Devin in a Python script using plain HTTP calls to the speech-to-text endpoint. Uploaded four recordings as multipart form data with the language field set to Spanish, and grouped the returned text into paragraphs for the summary.
limitations: Four Spanish recordings from one caller set; the check on accents was made by reading the text, not by listening.

summary: Voiced a dashboard walkthrough for a sales video, with short pauses inserted between steps through the script text. The first render was kept with no changes to the voice settings, and the same voice ran across all eleven steps. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Pauses written as ellipses and periods in the script text gave short gaps, and no special markup was needed.
Reusing one voice across eleven steps kept the delivery steady, and the agent did not compare alternative voices.
The team listened to the full walkthrough once and asked for one step to be re-rendered with a corrected product name.

context.task: Voice a dashboard walkthrough for a sales video

method: Claude Code in a Node project with the JavaScript SDK. Wrote eleven step lines with pauses as punctuation, requested them with one voice id and the multilingual model, and saved one mp3 per step for the video editor.
limitations: Eleven steps in English with one voice; the walkthrough was not timed against screen recordings in this run.

summary: Nightly job renders audio for new changelog entries and skips entries that already have an mp3. The first run rendered the four new entries and skipped the older ones without any errors. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Checking for an existing mp3 by slug kept reruns cheap, since older entries never reached the API.
A failed render leaves no partial file, because the script writes to a temp name and renames on success.
The job runs from the team's scheduler and posts the file list to the release folder for review.

context.task: Render audio for new changelog entries on a nightly schedule

method: Goose in a repository with a Python script and a scheduled workflow file. The script lists changelog entries, skips slugs that already have an mp3, renders the rest through the Python SDK, and writes to a temp file before renaming.
limitations: Four new entries on one manual run; the scheduled run was not observed firing.

summary: Requests for long paragraphs hit the client's default timeout on the first run, and two lines failed. Raising the timeout and adding one retry let all lines finish on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The default client timeout was shorter than the render time for the longest paragraphs, so those requests were abandoned.
A single retry with the longer timeout completed both failed lines without changing the text or voice.
The script logged the elapsed time per line, which made the slow lines easy to pick out in the output.

context.task: Render paragraph audio without client timeouts

method: Aider in a Python script. The first run used the client's default timeout. The second run set a longer timeout for each request and retried any line that failed once, then wrote the mp3 files for all paragraphs.
limitations: Forty paragraphs from one document; timeouts on very long single requests were not characterized beyond these cases.

summary: Go worker renders short alert voice messages from a queue and uploads the mp3 files to object storage. Messages rendered on the first try, and the queue consumer acknowledged each job only after the upload finished. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Acknowledging the queue message only after the upload finished meant a crash mid-render left the job for another try.
The worker read the full response into a byte slice and checked the content type before uploading, which caught an empty body early.
The test queue held twenty messages, and they rendered one at a time, so no concurrency settings were exercised.

context.task: Render queued alert voice messages to object storage

method: Custom SDK agent in a Go worker using net/http. Pulled a message from a queue, posted the text to the speech endpoint, checked the content type, uploaded the mp3 to object storage, and acknowledged the message only after the upload returned.
limitations: Twenty test messages on one queue; crash recovery was reasoned about in code but not forced during the run.

summary: Picked the first voice from the voice list, which turned out to be unavailable on the account's plan, and every render returned a permission error. The agent switched the model three times instead of choosing a different voice from the same list. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first listed voice was not available on the current plan, so each render returned a permission error that named the voice.
Changing the model three times left the error unchanged, which the agent read as a model problem.
The agent picked the first entry in the list without reading any of the voice details first.

context.task: Render narration with the first available voice

method: Cline in a Node script that calls the JavaScript SDK. Fetched the voice list, picked the first entry, and requested four lines with three different model ids. The run ended with no audio rendered at the step limit.
limitations: One account and four lines; other voices in the list were not tested, so plan access for them is unknown.

summary: Speech-to-text on a French meeting came back in English-looking text on the first run, because the language field was left out. Setting the language on the rerun gave readable French transcripts for the same file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Leaving the language field empty let the default model guess, and the guess produced English-looking text for French audio.
Setting the language on the rerun gave readable French output with accents preserved on the same file.
The agent compared the first paragraph against the audio by ear to confirm the fix rather than trusting the output length.

context.task: Transcribe a French meeting recording

method: OpenHands in a Python sandbox, calling the speech-to-text method of the Python SDK. Posted one French recording to speech-to-text with no language field, read the output, then reran the same file with the language field set to French.
limitations: One French meeting recording; other French regional accents and multi-speaker overlap were not checked.

summary: Batch render of tutorial clips hit a server-side error response on two requests that the script did not recognize as retryable, so the batch stopped at the first one. Adding retries for those responses let the rest of the batch finish on the second run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script treated any non-200 response as fatal, so the first failed request stopped the batch before the remaining clips were sent.
Retrying with backoff on server-side error codes let both failed clips render, and the remaining clips finished without further errors.
The batch wrote a progress file after each clip, which let the rerun skip the clips that had already rendered.

context.task: Render 35 tutorial clips in one batch

method: Claude Code in a Python script with the Python SDK. The first run treated every non-200 response as fatal and stopped. The second run retried server-side error codes with backoff and resumed from a progress file that listed finished clips.
limitations: Thirty-five clips in one batch on one account; long batches spanning several days were not tested.

summary: Claude Code wrote a script that pulls five recent papers per topic for a reading list, and the first run returned clean titles and links. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The Python snippet ran after exporting the key, with no setup beyond the install step.
Each hit carried title, url and publishedDate, so the agent filtered by year without a second request.

context.task: Pull recent papers on retrieval evaluation into a markdown reading list

method: Claude Code generated a short script with exa-py, searched three topics with a start date and five results each, and wrote the titles into a reading list file. Key read from EXA_API_KEY in a local env file.
limitations: Three topics on one laptop; result quality was checked by reading the titles only.

summary: Cursor scaffolded an App Router route that searches three news domains and returns JSON to a client component, and the local production build served results without edits. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The JS README constructor took the key as an argument, which matched the snippet the agent wrote on the first pass.
Text for five results made the JSON response heavy, so the agent trimmed each excerpt before returning it to the browser.

context.task: Startup news digest page with a server-side search route

method: Cursor added a route handler in a Next.js app, called search from the server with an include filter for three sites, and rendered results in a client component. Tested with the dev server and a local production build.
limitations: Ran only on localhost with a development key; the route was never deployed to a preview environment.

summary: Codex CLI filled a 50-row company list with one-line descriptions by searching each domain's About page, and 40 rows matched on the first pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Ten rows returned no About page text, so the agent left those cells blank instead of guessing a description.
Median call time stayed under a second across the batch, and no call hit a rate limit during the run.

context.task: Enrich a 50-row company CSV with one-line descriptions

method: Codex CLI read a CSV of domains, ran one search per row with a domain filter and text contents, and wrote the first sentence of each match into a new column. Run from a Linux shell in a venv.
limitations: One 50-row CSV; the ten blank rows were not checked by hand against the company sites.

summary: Devin set up a nightly search for launch posts from three competitors, and the first manual run returned seven links from the past week. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A start date seven days back returned posts from the right window, though two results were older reposts.
The agent read the key from the sandbox secret store at runtime, so it stayed out of the script file.
The first search call came back in under two seconds, and new links were appended to the log without duplicates.

context.task: Nightly watch for competitor launch posts

method: Devin wrote a Python job with exa-py that searches three competitor names with a seven-day start date and appends new links to a log file. Ran it by hand twice in its sandbox to confirm the output.
limitations: Ran by hand twice in one sandbox; the cron schedule itself never fired during the session.

summary: A custom TypeScript agent calls the search tool, gets ranked results, and cites the links it used in its reply; the first product question came back with two sources. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The top two hits matched the product question closely, and the third hit was an unrelated changelog that the model left out of its answer.
Median search call took about 640 ms, which left plenty of room inside a one-minute reply budget.

context.task: Answer product questions with cited web sources

method: Custom agent in TypeScript with a tool-calling loop. The search tool wraps the JS client with numResults 5 and returns title, url and text, and the model writes its answer with bracketed citations. Run from a local script.
limitations: About a dozen questions, spot-checked by hand; no load test and no measurement of citation accuracy.

summary: Windsurf used Exa to confirm release dates for six changelog pages; four pages returned a publish date that matched the heading and two returned none. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Four of six pages carried a publishedDate that matched the changelog heading, while the other two returned no date at all.
Each page needed its own query built from the page title, and the whole check took eleven tool calls.

context.task: Verify release dates on a changelog page

method: Windsurf read six changelog entries from a markdown table, called search with each page title as the query and the page domain as a filter, then compared publishedDate to the heading dates. Output was a checked table.
limitations: Six pages from one vendor; date coverage on other sources may differ and was not measured.

summary: Cline added a research route to a notes app and tested it locally with curl; the first request returned ranked links in under two seconds. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first curl call returned five results with titles and urls, and the response matched the route's JSON shape.
The deploy target could not be reached from the sandbox, so the route only ran on the dev server.

context.task: Research endpoint for a notes app

method: Cline added an Express route that forwards the query to search with contents enabled and returns trimmed JSON. Tested with curl against the local server on port 3000; nothing was deployed.
limitations: Local server only; the deploy target was unreachable from the sandbox that day.

summary: Codex CLI built a Flask endpoint that answers vendor questions with links, and the first POST returned three hits with titles and short excerpts. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A missing key raised a clear client error at startup, which made the empty env var easy to spot.

context.task: Flask endpoint for vendor question lookup

method: Codex CLI generated app.py with exa-py, read the key from the environment, and added one POST route that returns title, url and an excerpt per hit. Tested with curl against the local Flask server.
limitations: Local Flask server only; the endpoint had no auth in front of it during this run.

summary: Cursor wrote a bash helper that posts a neural search body with numResults 10, and the curl output parsed cleanly through jq on the first try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A JSON body with type neural and numResults 10 returned a results array on the first attempt, with no schema errors.
The REST section pairs the x-api-key header with the request body example, which was all the agent needed.

context.task: Shell helper for quick topic lookups

method: Cursor drafted a bash function that builds the JSON body from its arguments, sends it with curl and the x-api-key header, and pipes results through jq for titles and links. Run from a macOS terminal.
limitations: Used on public topic queries only; non-English queries were not tried.

summary: Claude Code added a list-recent command to a Node CLI and ran it on three seed topics; each run printed dated links without any error. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each topic printed up to five links with a date column, which the author said was enough for a daily skim.
A niche topic returned only two hits, and the CLI printed them without a warning about the short list.

context.task: Node CLI to list recent posts on a topic

method: Claude Code added a command that calls the JS client with a seven-day start date and prints title, date and url for each hit. Tested against three seed topics in a local terminal.
limitations: Three English topics on one machine; long-tail queries were not tried.

summary: Devin pulled About page text for twelve vendors and filled a one-liner table; eleven returned usable paragraphs, and one returned only a cookie banner. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Eleven vendors returned real paragraphs, but one vendor page returned only a cookie banner and a consent prompt.
The batch used about 41000 tokens across the twelve summaries, most of it in the page text passed to the model.

context.task: Vendor one-liner table for a procurement review

method: Devin ran a Python loop over twelve vendor domains, called search with each domain as a filter and text contents enabled, and wrote the first paragraph of each result into a CSV. Ran once in its sandbox.
limitations: One procurement batch; the cookie-banner vendor was left in the table with a manual note.

summary: OpenHands tested a similar-page lookup on ten seed posts and kept the top three matches per post for a related-reading widget in a static blog. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Most top-three matches shared the post topic, but two seeds pulled in a job board page that the author removed by hand.
Median lookup time stayed near 610 ms, so building the widget at site build time added under a minute.
The widget partial rendered with no empty slots, because the build script skipped any post with fewer than three matches.

context.task: Related-reading widget for a static blog

method: OpenHands wrote a build step in Python that takes each post's URL, calls the similar-page lookup with a result count of three, and writes the links into a template partial. Run as part of a local site build.
limitations: Ten seed posts from one blog; match quality was judged by one reader in a single pass.

summary: aider wrapped Exa in a Bun script with a five-second timeout for a weekly ops report, and the first run finished the query list in about a minute. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The five-second timeout never fired on this run, and the slowest single query finished in about 2 seconds.
Bun ran the TypeScript file without a build step, which kept the report job to one command.
The markdown list needed one manual fix because a few titles contained pipe characters that broke the table.

context.task: Timeboxed lookup script for a weekly ops report

method: aider generated a Bun script that loops through eight queries, calls the JS client inside a timeout wrapper, and prints a markdown list. Run once from a terminal on a home network.
limitations: Single run from a home network; latency numbers do not reflect a deployed region.

summary: Windsurf pulled sources newer than a fixed cutoff for a policy brief and cited four of them with dates; the brief header records the cutoff used. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Four cited sources carried publish dates after the cutoff, and the agent dropped two older hits that had matched on keywords alone.
Some hits had no author line, so the citation format needed a manual fill for those sources.

context.task: Policy brief with dated sources

method: Windsurf ran several topic searches through exa-py with a start date set to the cutoff, deduplicated the hits by url, and wrote the brief with a header listing the date filter. Run on a Windows laptop.
limitations: One brief on a single policy topic; source selection was reviewed by the same person who ran the agent.

summary: Cline ran a sixty-query retrieval check on a Free plan key and finished without errors, staying inside the plan allowance. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The run stayed inside the free allowance, and the agent kept its own call counter to make sure it did not exceed it.
Median call time was about 890 ms across the sixty queries, with no timeouts.

context.task: Retrieval check on a small question set

method: Cline wrote a loop over sixty questions with the Python client, saved the top five urls per question, and tallied calls against its own counter. Run on a Linux dev box with a Free plan key.
limitations: Free plan key only; no paid plan was tested, so limits on other plans were not compared.

summary: Claude Code added Exa as the source for a related-articles list on a news page; eight of ten pages returned body text and two came back with titles only. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Eight pages returned body text the widget could show, and two returned only a title and url.
Hits were mostly from the last two weeks, which fit the widget's purpose of showing recent coverage.

context.task: Related-articles list for a news page

method: Claude Code wired a FastAPI endpoint to search with a fourteen-day start date and contents enabled, then rendered the first five hits in the page template. Tested against ten article URLs in a local run.
limitations: Ten pages from one news domain; body text coverage on other domains is untested.

summary: A custom Go service calls search over plain HTTP, stores the id and text of each hit, and serves cached answers for repeated support questions. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each result came back with an id and a text field, and the service stored both next to its question hash.
Nothing in the test set expired, so the eviction path was never exercised before the run ended.

context.task: Retrieval cache for a support bot

method: A Go service posts a JSON body with an include filter and text enabled through net/http, parses the results array, and keeps each answer in memory under a hash of the question. Ran a fifty-question test from a shell loop.
limitations: Fifty questions in one process; eviction, stale-data handling and concurrency were not tested.

summary: Goose checked the empty-state path for a search widget by sending a date range that matched nothing, and the component showed its fallback message without errors. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A date range with no matches returned an empty results list, and the component rendered its fallback text.
The agent tested only that one empty case and did not try a query that failed on the network.

context.task: Empty-state handling for a search widget

method: Goose sent a real query with a start date later than the newest page, got an empty list back, and checked the fallback text in the browser. Vite dev server, React component, one page load.
limitations: Only one empty case tested; no check on slow or failed network calls.

summary: Goose built a weekly markdown digest on vector database releases from six search hits, and the file came out with dates and links on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Six hits were enough for the digest, so the agent did not need a second topic query to fill the list.
Two hits were release notes for unrelated database products that shared a name fragment with the query.

context.task: Weekly digest on vector database releases

method: Goose wrote a Python script that runs one query with six results and a start date seven days back, then writes a markdown file with title, date and link per hit. Run once from a terminal.
limitations: Single digest run; quality was judged only by the agent reading its own output.

summary: Cursor's first script run returned 401 because the key was read from a misspelled variable; after renaming it in the env file, the five-source pull returned results. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first call failed with 401, which pointed at credentials rather than the query code.
The env file had a misspelled name, so the script read an empty key and the first request failed authentication.

context.task: Script to pull five product-review sources per query

method: Cursor wrote a Python script with exa-py that reads the key from a local env file, runs five queries, and prints one source line per hit. First run on a laptop, second run after the rename.
limitations: The fix was a renamed env variable on one machine; CI with the same secret name was not checked.

summary: A docs-site search box sent numResults as a string from a form field and got a 400 until the value was cast to a number; the retry returned results for the typed query. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A string value in numResults produced a 400 response, so the agent logged the request body to find the bad field.
Casting the form value to an integer before the call fixed the request on the first retry.

context.task: Search box for a docs site

method: Codex CLI wired a React search input to a server route that calls the JS client with numResults taken from the query string. Tested with the Vite dev server and three typed queries.
limitations: Tested on one form with three fields; other numeric inputs on the site were not checked.

summary: aider's batch of 120 startup-page lookups hit 429 responses after about forty calls; a sleep between requests and a backoff retry let the rest of the batch finish. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Three 429 responses came back in a row once the loop ran without pauses, and the retries succeeded after the backoff delay.
All 120 rows finished in the second pass, and the output file had one sector label per row.

context.task: Batch sector labels for 120 startup pages

method: aider generated a Python loop that calls search for each startup domain, sleeps between calls, and retries 429 responses with exponential backoff. Output went to a CSV with one sector per row. Ran on a Linux dev box.
limitations: One batch on a personal key; the delay was tuned by hand and not measured against documented limits.

summary: Devin's nightly hiring-post job returned an empty list because cron did not load the key; reading it from the secret store at runtime made the next test run return hits. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The shell profile had the key, but cron does not source it, so the job ran with an empty key and returned nothing.
The job exited with status zero on the empty run, so the failure only showed up in the log file.

context.task: Nightly search for hiring posts in three cities

summary: Goose's first fetch of three pages timed out in a sandbox with restricted outbound access; the same script returned summaries when run from a laptop terminal. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Calls from the sandbox failed with ETIMEDOUT before any HTTP status came back, so the failure sat on the network path.
The unchanged script returned results for all three URLs on the laptop, which pointed at the sandbox as the cause.

context.task: Fetch and summarize three pages for a briefing

limitations: Sandbox behavior was not confirmed beyond this run; the laptop result may not carry over to CI.

summary: OpenHands sent a US-style date in the start date field and got a 400, then sent an ISO date and pulled the framework release posts from the quarter. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A 400 response came back for the US-style date string, and the ISO form in the same field worked on the next call.
The agent guessed a US format for the date field before checking how the date was supposed to look.

context.task: Pull posts about a framework release from one quarter

method: OpenHands built a curl request with a JSON body that carries a start date and a result count, retried with an ISO timestamp after the 400, and saved the hits to a text file. Run from a Linux terminal.
limitations: One date range checked; other date formats were not tried after the first fix.

summary: A custom agent passed full https addresses in its domain filter and got empty results; stripping the scheme from each entry restored hits from the vendor doc sites. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Entries with a scheme returned zero results and no error, so the agent first suspected the query text.
Plain hostnames in the same filter returned hits from the vendor doc sites on the next call.

limitations: Two domain filters tested; the empty-result case was not reproduced on purpose after the fix.

summary: Windsurf's first similar-page call passed a page title instead of the page url and returned nothing; swapping in the full url gave six matches for the competitor post. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The similar-page call returned an empty list when given a title string, and it returned six hits once the agent passed the url.
Three of the six similar pages were tutorials on other tools, which the author judged off-topic.

context.task: Find pages similar to a competitor blog post

limitations: One seed url tested; similarity results were rated only by the person who ran the script.

summary: Cursor's production deploy of a search route returned 500 because EXA_API_KEY was not set in the Vercel project; adding the variable and redeploying the same commit cleared it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The local dev server worked with the key from the env file, but the Vercel production environment had no value for it.
The route returned a bare 500 and gave no hint about the missing key, so the agent read the function logs to find it.

context.task: Deploy a search route to production

method: Cursor added a Next.js route handler that calls the JS client, pushed to a Vercel project, and read the production logs after the 500. Added the variable in the project dashboard and redeployed the same commit.
limitations: Single production deploy; preview deployments were not checked for the same missing variable.

summary: Devin's daily source scan for a research memo failed on every request because the sandbox could not open outbound connections; it stopped after its third retry and wrote a note. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: All three requests failed with connection errors before any HTTP status came back, so no response body was ever received.
Backoff retries added about a minute of waiting per request and did not change the outcome.
The note in the repo listed the blocked calls and the time of each attempt, which made the failure easy to hand off.

context.task: Daily source scan for a research memo

method: Devin ran a Python script with exa-py inside its sandbox, sent three search requests with exponential backoff, and then wrote a note in the repo describing the failed connections. No retry from another network.
limitations: Sandbox egress blocked all calls, so the search path itself was never exercised in this run.

summary: OpenHands used keyword mode for a conceptual question about a licensing change; the results were off-topic and the run ended without switching search modes. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Keyword mode returned pages that shared one literal term with the question, and none covered the licensing change itself.
The agent read the titles from each attempt, marked the question unanswerable, and stopped after nine tool calls.
The curl requests returned valid JSON on every call, so the problem was the query mode rather than the request.

context.task: Find primary sources on a licensing question

method: OpenHands sent several curl requests with the type field set to keyword and the question as a full sentence, read the returned titles, and stopped. No neural or auto query was tried in this run.
limitations: One question tested; the failure reflects a query mode choice in this run, not a general result.

summary: Claude Code's calls to the search API failed certificate checks behind a corporate proxy on every attempt, and the market scan ended before any results were pulled. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Every request failed certificate verification at the proxy, so the client never got a response from the search endpoint.
The agent's first attempt to point the client at a CA bundle path did not take effect, and the error stayed the same.

context.task: Pull sources for a weekly market scan

method: Claude Code ran a Python script with exa-py from a work laptop on a managed network. Five retries reused the same client config with a cert path set through an environment variable, and nothing changed.
limitations: Only the managed work laptop was tried; a personal network was not used for comparison.

summary: Cursor called the search API from a React client component on a marketing page, and the browser blocked each response with a CORS error; the run stopped before a server route was added. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

The agent kept editing the component for several reload cycles instead of moving the call to a server route.

context.task: Live search box on a marketing page

summary: aider's 300-page sector batch hit 429 responses on a Free plan key partway through, and the remaining queries kept failing until the run was stopped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Goose installed a similarly named PyPI package instead of the Exa client, hit ModuleNotFoundError twice, and stopped with the sales-research script still unbuilt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Windsurf's Windows scheduled news digest returned 401 on every run because the key was set only in the session and did not survive a restart; the task stopped at the scheduler timeout. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Python client scraped a long API reference page into markdown with the main-content setting on, and the headings matched the page outline on the first call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

Fenced code blocks came through intact, but two tab-switched examples appeared only in their default tab.

summary: Crawl of a docs subsite with a 50-page limit started as a job, and the job returned 48 markdown pages once its status reported completed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: crawl returned a job id straight away, and the loop checked status every few seconds until the state changed to completed.
Forty-eight pages came back against a limit of 50, because two URLs redirected to pages already in the set.

context.task: Crawl a docs subsite into a markdown folder

limitations: One docs subsite of about 60 pages; sites with heavy client-side rendering were not part of this crawl.

summary: Scrape of a client-rendered dashboard page returned empty markdown on the first call, and adding a wait time before capture fixed it on the second. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

Setting a wait time of two seconds before capture returned the table rows, and the second response had the full list of 31 items.

limitations: One status page with 31 rows; other single-page apps with infinite scroll were not checked.

summary: Crawl of a large documentation site stopped at about 40 percent when the account's credit balance ran out, and the restart could not finish the rest of the list. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

The restart requested the full site again instead of the unfinished pages, so the remaining balance was spent before the new job reached new pages.

context.task: Crawl a large documentation site into a local index

limitations: One site of about 1,200 pages; the plan's credit allowance was not checked before the run began.

summary: Map call listed 212 URLs on a docs site, and filtering the results to the API path prefix left 96 pages for the next scrape step. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: map returned URLs without fetching page bodies, so the listing finished in a few seconds even for the full site.
