summary: OpenHands wired a Go service with pgx v5 to a Neon branch, ran golang-migrate up, and the health endpoint returned 200 after the first deploy. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: golang-migrate applied two up migrations to the branch host and recorded the version in schema_migrations.
pgxpool max connections was set to 5 for the smoke test, and the service handled the 20 concurrent smoke requests without pool timeouts.

context.task: Add a reports table and a health endpoint to a Go service

method: OpenHands agent on a Linux workstation with Go 1.23 and the golang-migrate CLI. Migrations in db/migrations run against the branch host, and the smoke test uses hey with 20 concurrent connections.
limitations: Smoke test only, no sustained load, and the branch was left running afterward.

summary: A custom SDK agent on Node 20 used the serverless Pool, got a WebSocket not defined error, and passed the ws package as webSocketConstructor on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

limitations: Batch size of 500 rows tested only, with one worker and no concurrency.

summary: Claude Code added a GitHub Actions step that creates a Neon branch per pull request with neonctl and deletes it when the PR closes. The cleanup job ran on the next close event. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The closed-event job removed the branch in about 4 s, and the next pull request created a fresh one from main.
The workflow listens on opened, synchronize, and closed events, so each pull request gets exactly one branch.

summary: Cline tried to restore a local pg_dump into a fresh Neon database. The plain SQL stopped on ALTER OWNER lines that named a local role, and the run was abandoned. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ALTER OWNER statements pointed at a local superuser role that does not exist on Neon, and psql stopped on the first one.
The second psql run failed on the same ALTER OWNER line, and no retry with --no-owner was attempted before the agent stopped.

context.task: Import a local pg_dump of an app database into Neon
context.blocker: dump contains owner statements for a local role

The 240 seed rows went in one transaction and the unique slug column raised no conflicts.

summary: Cursor added a row-level security policy to a tenant-scoped notes table and confirmed that a non-owner role saw only its own tenant rows. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

The table owner still saw every row, which the agent noted as expected without FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY.

context.task: Enable RLS on a multi-tenant notes table

method: Cursor agent in a macOS terminal with psql against a Neon branch on the direct host. Ran ALTER TABLE ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY, CREATE POLICY keyed on current_setting, then SET ROLE to a non-owner role for the checks.
limitations: Checks ran on a branch with synthetic tenants, and no load was applied to the policy.

summary: Devin created a read-only role for a BI tool, limited it to the reporting schema, and confirmed that a query against the auth schema was denied. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: GRANT SELECT covered the reporting schema only, and the auth schema query returned a permission denied error as planned.
New tables added later to reporting will need their own grants, because the default privileges were not changed in this run.

Batches of 500 rows committed at a steady pace once the wrapper was in place, with no duplicate rows found afterward.

summary: Windsurf ran drizzle-kit migrate with the app role and got a permission error on the public schema. It reran with the owner role for migrations and kept the app role for runtime. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

A single module-scoped pool per function instance stopped the errors in the second run, though requests queued behind it.

summary: OpenHands generated an Alembic revision that adds a nullable column, applied it to a Neon branch, and backfilled 3,000 rows in batches. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Claude Code added a materialized view for daily signups, scheduled REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY from a cron route, and the refresh finished in 3.2 s. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

context.task: Prune preview branches that no open pull request still uses

method: OpenHands agent with a bash script calling neonctl branches list as JSON, filtering by created_at and the keep- name prefix, then neonctl branches delete for each remaining match.
limitations: Dry run and one real pass on a sandbox project, with no scheduled runs tested.

summary: Aider tried to run prisma generate in a sandbox where binary downloads were blocked. The engine fetch failed, and the migration step never started. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: prisma generate could not fetch the query engine binary because outbound requests to the download host were blocked in the sandbox.
Two reruns hit the same blocked request, and the agent stopped before trying a bundled engine path.

context.task: Generate the Prisma client and run migrations inside an agent sandbox

method: Aider in a restricted sandbox with Node 22 and Prisma 6. Ran npx prisma generate and prisma migrate deploy with DATABASE_URL set to a Neon branch host, then reran twice after the engine error.
limitations: Single sandbox run, and the egress rules were not changed for this test.

summary: Claude Code added a PL/pgSQL trigger that writes an audit row on every update to the accounts table. Two test updates produced two audit entries with old and new values. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The trigger fired once per UPDATE statement, and the audit row stored the old and new values as jsonb.
Only two test updates were run, so bulk updates and concurrent writes were not exercised.

context.task: Record field-level changes on an accounts table

method: Claude Code in a terminal writing a migration with CREATE FUNCTION and an AFTER UPDATE trigger, applied via psql on a Neon branch. Verified with two UPDATE statements and a SELECT on the audit table.
limitations: Two test updates only, with no concurrency or bulk-update test.

summary: Devin rotated the owner role password in Neon, but a preview deployment still held the old value. Authentication failed until the variable was replaced on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The old password stopped working at once, and the preview build logged password authentication failed until the new value was saved.
Production picked up the new value on redeploy, and the preview environment needed a separate update in the Vercel project.

context.task: Rotate the owner password and update every deployment

method: Devin in a cloud sandbox ran neonctl roles reset-password for the owner role, then vercel env rm and vercel env add for DATABASE_URL in preview and production, followed by redeploys of both environments.
limitations: Two environments in one Vercel project, with no other services checked for the old value.

summary: Windsurf set a SQLAlchemy pool size of 5 per worker for a uvicorn app with four workers, and the smoke test ran without connection errors. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The smoke test held 50 requests per second for two minutes on the pooled host with no connection errors.
Four workers with five connections each meant at most twenty open sessions at peak.

context.task: Size connection pools for a multi-worker FastAPI app

method: Windsurf agent on Ubuntu with uvicorn --workers 4, SQLAlchemy create_engine with pool_size 5, and hey as the load tool against the items route.
limitations: Two minutes of smoke load, with no sustained traffic pattern tested.

summary: A custom SDK agent added a generated tsvector column and a GIN index to a 20,000-row articles table, and the ranked search returned in about 14 ms. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: CREATE INDEX on the tsvector column took 2.4 s, and the EXPLAIN plan switched to a bitmap scan on the GIN index.
websearch_to_tsquery with ts_rank handled quoted phrases from the sample queries without extra parsing code.

context.task: Add keyword search to an articles table

method: Custom SDK agent running SQL through the pg client against a Neon branch. The migration adds a generated column with to_tsvector and a GIN index, and the query uses websearch_to_tsquery with ts_rank.
limitations: Synthetic article text with English stemming only, on one branch.

summary: OpenHands kept connecting to a preview branch host that the cleanup job had already deleted. After repeated lookup errors, the run was abandoned. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The DNS lookup for the branch host failed on every attempt after the branch was removed, so the agent never reached the query step.
The hostname came from an older pull request comment, and the agent did not check the branch list before connecting.

context.task: Run a data check against a preview branch
context.blocker: branch deleted before the job ran

method: OpenHands on Linux with psql and a hostname copied from an earlier pull request comment. Ran the check query in a loop with a 10 second wait between attempts.
limitations: Single run with a stale host, and the cleanup schedule was not inspected.

summary: Codex CLI added a wait-for-db Makefile target that polls the branch host with pg_isready until it accepts connections. The check passed after six polls. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The wait loop returned ready after six 2 second polls, which covered a short compute resume on the branch.
The target is set to fail after 30 attempts, so a stuck branch fails the job instead of hanging.

context.task: Block CI tests until the branch accepts connections

method: Codex CLI edited a Makefile on Linux. The target loops pg_isready -h with the direct hostname, sleeps 2 seconds between polls, and exits non-zero after 30 attempts.
limitations: One branch in one region, and the failure path was not exercised.

summary: Cursor measured a median of 181 ms from a Frankfurt VM to a us-east-2 database, then created a project in eu-central. The first seed run timed out, and the second run passed with smaller batches. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Round trips from the Frankfurt VM had a median of 181 ms to the existing project, which the agent treated as the reason to move.
The first seed run hit a client timeout on the long link, and the second run with 200-row batches finished without errors.

context.task: Move a database closer to the app region

method: Cursor agent with Node 22 and pg. Measured SELECT 1 round trips from a Frankfurt VM to the existing project, created a new project in the eu-central region with neonctl, then reran the seed script with 200-row batches.
limitations: Round trips measured from one VM, with only two regions compared.

summary: Windsurf ran ALTER TABLE from a Vercel build step. The statement waited on a lock held by an idle session, and the build was cancelled before the migration finished. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: ALTER TABLE blocked for the whole build timeout because a leftover idle transaction held a lock on the table.
The migration sat inside the build command, so the build timeout was the only limit on how long it could wait.

context.task: Run schema changes as part of the Vercel build
context.blocker: lock wait on an idle transaction

method: Windsurf agent added a prebuild step to package.json that runs drizzle-kit migrate against the pooled host. The build ran on Vercel with the production DATABASE_URL.
limitations: One failed production build attempt, with no retry over a direct connection.

summary: Claude Code queried pg_available_extensions on a fresh branch, confirmed citext was listed, and the first migration ran clean. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The query returned a row for citext, so the migration could create the column type without a manual install step.
The check ran before the migration was generated, so a missing extension would have shown up earlier.

context.task: Check extension availability before writing a migration

method: Claude Code ran SELECT name, default_version FROM pg_available_extensions WHERE name = 'citext' through psql on the direct host, then wrote the create extension line into the migration.
limitations: One branch checked, and the extension list was read from a single project.

summary: Devin tried to install neonctl in a sandbox with restricted registry access. The npm install failed on every mirror it tried, and the task stopped before any database call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: npm returned ETIMEDOUT for the registry host three times, and the agent never reached a neonctl command.
A configured mirror timed out the same way, so the agent stopped without trying an offline package archive.

context.task: Automate a Neon branch setup from a sandbox
context.blocker: registry access blocked in the sandbox

method: Devin in a cloud sandbox with Node 22 and npm. Tried npm install -g neonctl, then npx neonctl with the default registry, then with a configured mirror. No database calls were made.
limitations: Sandbox network policy blocked the registry, so the database steps were never tested.

summary: OpenHands mocked the Neon client for unit tests in a Next.js project, and all 27 tests passed without a database connection on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The mock covered query and transaction calls, so the suite finished in about 4 s on a laptop.
Because the SQL never ran, typos in raw queries would not show up in this suite.

context.task: Run unit tests without a live database

method: OpenHands agent on Linux with Vitest and vi.mock on the module that exports the database client. Tests import the service layer only, and npm test runs the suite.
limitations: Mocks only, so SQL correctness was not exercised by this suite.

summary: Claude Code's parallel tests raced on a unique email insert. One worker hit a unique violation, and the seed switched to ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING before the second run passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Two workers inserted the same email at once, and one hit a unique violation that failed a single spec on the first run.
ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING removed the race, and the rerun passed the full suite of 61 specs.

context.task: Make parallel test seeding safe on a shared branch

method: Claude Code in a macOS terminal running Vitest with four workers against one Neon branch. Changed the seed insert to ON CONFLICT (email) DO NOTHING and reran the suite.
limitations: Four workers on one branch, and no run with a higher worker count.

summary: Aider converted a text status column to a Postgres enum through a Drizzle migration. The migration applied to a branch with a USING clause, and the counts per value matched. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The migration used a USING clause from the start, so the existing text values cast into the four enum labels.
A GROUP BY count per status matched the pre-migration counts for all four values.

context.task: Convert a status column to a Postgres enum

method: Aider edited a Drizzle schema file and generated a migration with drizzle-kit generate. Applied it to a Neon branch with drizzle-kit migrate on the direct URL, then ran a GROUP BY count per status.
limitations: One table of 8,000 rows, with the enum fixed at four labels.

summary: Cline wrote a COPY TO STDOUT export for a 500,000-row table. The file finished in 22 s with the header row, and the line count matched the source. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: COPY streamed rows to the output file, so the script never held the full result in memory.
wc -l on the output matched the row count from a SELECT count query, with the header line accounted for.

context.task: Export a large table to CSV for a data handoff

method: Cline in VS Code writing a Python script with psycopg 3 and copy() over COPY table TO STDOUT WITH CSV HEADER on the direct host. Row count checked with wc -l and a count query.
limitations: Export from one table on one branch, with the file kept local and not uploaded.

summary: Goose ran db push against main and then started the app on a preview branch, so Prisma raised P2021 for a missing table. Pointing the env file at the right branch fixed it on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Prisma raised P2021 because db push targeted the main branch host while the app read DATABASE_URL from the preview branch.
The DIRECT_URL and DATABASE_URL pair had been copied from two different branches, which was easy to miss in .env.local.

context.task: Run db push and start the app on a preview branch

method: Goose agent in a local shell with Prisma 6. Ran prisma db push with DIRECT_URL, then started next dev with DATABASE_URL, where the two variables pointed at different branches. Fixed .env.local and reran.
limitations: Local run only, and the same mismatch was not tried in a CI environment.

summary: Codex CLI generated a seed file of 300 product rows and loaded it with psql in one pass, after checking that the table was empty. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: psql -f applied the file in about 3 s, and the row count query returned 300.
A SELECT count before the load returned zero, so the ON_ERROR_STOP flag never had to abort anything.

context.task: Load a product catalog seed into a dev branch

method: Codex CLI generated seed.sql with INSERT statements, then ran psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f seed.sql against the direct host of a dev branch, followed by a count query.
limitations: Dev branch only, with a synthetic catalog of 300 products.

summary: Claude Code tried to reach the Neon host on port 5432 from a sandbox that blocks outbound database ports. Every connect timed out, and the task was stopped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: psql reported a connection timeout on every attempt, including the pooled hostname, so no query ran at all.
Swapping the pooled and direct hostnames changed nothing, which pointed the agent at the network rule rather than the URL.

context.task: Run a schema check against Neon from a restricted CI sandbox
context.blocker: outbound port 5432 blocked by the sandbox

method: Claude Code in a locked-down sandbox with psql and a direct connection string. Each attempt used a 10 second connect timeout, and the agent retried three times with the pooled and direct hostnames before stopping.
limitations: One sandbox tested, and no allow-list change was requested during the run.

summary: Drizzle-kit introspect ran against a Neon branch from a custom SDK agent, and the typecheck passed on the first run. Generated schema files needed no manual edits. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Introspection generated 14 table definitions, and the typecheck passed without manual edits to the output.
The run used only SELECT on catalog tables, so the branch schema was left unchanged.

context.task: Generate typed schema files from an existing Neon database

method: Custom SDK agent running drizzle-kit introspect with the direct URL against a Neon branch, then tsc --noEmit. Generated output written under src/db/.
limitations: Read-only introspection on one branch, with no comparison to the migration history.

summary: Deployed a Vite single-page app from a Git push and the site loaded at the root path. Refreshing a nested route returned a 404 until a SPA fallback rule was added. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A direct load of a nested route returned 404 because no fallback rule existed in netlify.toml.
The push to main triggered a build and the site went live without any manual step.

context.task: Deploy a Vite single-page app and fix refresh on nested routes

method: Claude Code in a macOS terminal set the build command and publish directory in netlify.toml, pushed to main, then tested a nested route in the browser. Added a catch-all redirect to index.html with status 200.
limitations: One Vite app with three routes; no server-side rendering and no custom domain attached during this run.

summary: Wired a contact form with the data-netlify attribute and submitted it twice; the second submission appeared in the Forms tab. The first submit was missed because the form was rendered by JavaScript. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The JavaScript-rendered form was not detected at deploy time, so the hidden form-name input was needed for the second version.
Submissions were listed with their fields in the Forms tab without extra configuration.

context.task: Collect contact form submissions on a static marketing site

method: Cursor agent added a plain HTML form with the data-netlify attribute, deployed with a git push, then submitted the form from the live site. Rewrote the form as static markup after the first submission was not recorded.
limitations: Static Astro site only; spam filtering and notification emails were not configured or tested.

summary: Ran a Netlify Function locally with netlify dev and called it from the front end on a second terminal. The function returned the expected JSON on the first request. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: netlify dev served the static site and the functions on one port, so the front end call needed no CORS change.

context.task: Add a JSON endpoint as a Netlify Function and test it locally

method: Codex CLI ran netlify dev from the project root, then fetched the function path with curl. The handler lived in netlify/functions and exported a plain handler function.
limitations: Local run only; the function was not deployed and no production environment variables were loaded.

summary: Pointed a custom subdomain at a Netlify site through a CNAME record. The site showed a certificate pending state for roughly twenty minutes before HTTPS worked. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The domain page listed the CNAME target to use, and the agent copied it from there without changing the DNS zone otherwise.
The certificate stayed pending while DNS was still resolving the old record, and it issued on its own after the change spread.

context.task: Attach a subdomain to a Netlify site with HTTPS

method: Devin created a CNAME record in the DNS provider for the subdomain, added the domain in the site settings, then polled the site with curl until the certificate was active. No apex domain was changed.
limitations: A single subdomain on one DNS provider; apex domains and redirects between domains were not tested.

summary: Ran the production deploy with the CLI and the command deployed to a draft URL instead of the live site. Rerunning with the prod flag published it to the main domain. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A plain deploy command created a draft deploy with its own address, and the live site was unchanged until the prod flag was passed.
The CLI printed both the draft URL and the production URL, which made the difference easy to check.

context.task: Publish a static docs site to the production domain from the CLI

method: Aider ran the CLI deploy command in the build output folder, read the draft address it printed, then ran the same command again with the prod flag. Checked the production address with curl.
limitations: One static site, no branch deploy in use; the run did not cover rollback.

summary: Stuck on a build failure because the site used Node 16 by default and the dependency needed a newer runtime. Setting NODE_VERSION in the site settings fixed the next build. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build log showed the default Node version, and the install step failed on an engines mismatch before any code ran.
Adding NODE_VERSION to the build environment was the only change needed, and the next build passed.

context.task: Fix a failing Netlify build for a Node project

method: Cline read the build log in the Netlify UI, then set NODE_VERSION in the site environment settings and triggered a new deploy from the Deploys tab. The repository had no .nvmrc file.
limitations: Only one site on the Free plan; the chosen Node version was not checked against the full dependency tree.

summary: Built an edge function to rewrite the language path before the page loaded, and the redirect returned the localized page on the first request. Cold reads of the origin were skipped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The function file in netlify/edge-functions ran on the request path and returned the rewritten response without a separate deploy step.

context.task: Rewrite localized paths at the edge for a marketing site

method: Windsurf created an edge function under netlify/edge-functions, registered its path in netlify.toml, deployed a draft, and requested three localized paths with curl. Latency was measured from a single client.
limitations: Three paths from one client location; no load test and no comparison with a non-edge rewrite.

summary: Used Netlify Blobs from a function to store a counter, and the value persisted across two cold starts. The first write failed because the function had no site context in local dev. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Under netlify dev the store call threw a missing-context error, and the counter only worked after the call ran through a deployed site.
The stored value was still there after both cold starts and the read returned the last written number.

context.task: Persist a hit counter across function invocations
context.blocker: missing site context in local dev

method: Goose added @netlify/blobs to a function, wrote and read a counter key, then deployed and called the function repeatedly. Compared the value after a pause to confirm it held.
limitations: A single counter key with a few hundred writes; no concurrent write test and no data-size checks.

summary: Opened a pull request and the deploy preview came up with its own address within a few minutes. The preview showed the new hero section while production stayed on the old one. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The preview link appeared as a comment on the pull request once the build completed.

context.task: Review a hero section change through a deploy preview

method: Claude Code pushed a feature branch and opened a pull request on GitHub, then waited for the deploy preview comment and opened the link. Confirmed the production address still served the old hero.
limitations: A single visual change reviewed in one browser; the preview was not checked on mobile widths.

summary: Set an environment variable in the UI for the runtime scope only, and the build step read it as empty. Moving the variable to the all-contexts scope fixed the build output. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The variable was saved without a warning, but the build log showed it as unset until the scope was widened.
The scope selector sat under an advanced panel, which made the difference hard to see at first.

context.task: Pass a public site key into a static build

method: Aider set the variable in the site environment settings, triggered a build, read the build log, then changed the scope and redeployed. Used the public key only, no secret values were involved.
limitations: Static Hugo site only; the scope behaviour was checked on one variable and not on functions.

summary: Migrated a Gatsby site to the new Netlify build plugin setup and the first deploy failed on a missing publish directory. Correcting the path in netlify.toml let the second deploy pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The deploy failed with a not-found error on the publish path, and the path in the UI differed from the one in netlify.toml.
The plugin list in the UI matched the config file, and no other plugin needed changes.

context.task: Move a Gatsby site to the current build settings

method: Devin compared the UI build settings against netlify.toml, corrected the publish directory, and ran a deploy from the main branch. Diffed the build output folder against the previous deploy.
limitations: One Gatsby site; the build plugin list was not changed, only the publish path.

summary: Tried to deploy a Next.js site with server rendering on the Free plan and the deploy stalled after the build with a runtime error. The agent stopped after the second attempt without a working page. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build finished, but the first server-rendered page returned a 500 that the logs described only as a generic function error.
The function log had the stack trace but no link to the framework setting that controlled the runtime.

context.task: Deploy a server-rendered Next.js site with dynamic routes

method: OpenHands agent connected a Git repository, ran the default build, then opened the function log for the failing dynamic route. Two configuration tweaks were tried before the agent stopped.
limitations: Free plan with one dynamic route; the run did not test the framework adapter with other route patterns.

summary: Moved the site from a manual drag-and-drop folder upload to git-based deploys, and the first push built a new version within a few minutes. The old drop deploy stayed in the history. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Linking the repository required granting the Git provider app access, and the agent did that from the site settings page.
The deploy history listed the manual upload next to the git builds, which made the switch easy to confirm.

context.task: Switch a site from manual uploads to git-based deploys

method: Cline linked the repository in the site settings, confirmed the branch and build command, then pushed a one-line text change to the main branch. Checked the new deploy in the Deploys list.
limitations: One repository and one branch; the run did not cover branch deploys or deploy previews.

summary: A sandboxed agent could not run netlify deploy because the CLI needed a login step and the sandbox had no browser to complete it. The run ended at the auth prompt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The login command opened a device flow that required a browser, which the sandbox could not open.

context.task: Deploy a static build from a sandboxed agent

method: Custom SDK agent in a Linux sandbox ran the CLI build, then the deploy command, which asked for login. The agent did not have a token and the run stopped there.
limitations: Sandbox with no browser and no stored credentials; a run on a machine with a logged-in CLI was not attempted.

summary: Added a scheduled function for a nightly cleanup and the first scheduled run fired at the expected hour. The function logged the number of records it removed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The schedule was declared in the function file and appeared in the functions list after the deploy.
The cron expression was read in UTC, and the agent had to convert the expected local hour before writing it.

context.task: Run a nightly cleanup job as a scheduled function

method: Goose added a schedule to the function config with a cron expression, deployed it, then waited for the first run and read the function log. The cleanup targeted a test blob store only.
limitations: A single scheduled run was observed; retries after a failed run and overlapping runs were not checked.

summary: Created a branch deploy for a feature branch and its URL returned the staging copy within a few minutes of the push. The production site stayed unchanged during the test. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The branch deploy showed up in the Deploys list under its branch name, and the address followed the branch.

context.task: Share a feature branch on a staging address before merging

method: Claude Code pushed a feature branch, checked the Deploys list for the branch entry, and opened the branch address in a browser. Compared the header text with the production site.
limitations: One branch and one static change; branch deploy access controls were not reviewed.

summary: Set up a split test between two landing page variants and the traffic split took effect after the second deploy. The first deploy kept all traffic on the original page. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The split was set in the site settings, but the first deploy did not apply it until a second deploy ran.
Repeated requests showed both variants in roughly the configured ratio after the second deploy.

context.task: Run an A/B test on two landing pages

method: Windsurf built two variants into separate branches, deployed them as branch deploys, set the split in the site settings, and sent 200 requests with curl to check the ratio.
limitations: A single test with one set of requests; no statistical significance check and no conversion data.

summary: Added a redirect file for renamed blog posts and the old paths returned 301 responses on the next deploy. One legacy path still returned 404 because its pattern was misspelled. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The rules in the redirects file were applied on deploy, and the 301 status was visible in the response headers.
A misspelled pattern in one rule quietly matched nothing, and the 404 only showed up when the agent checked every old path.

context.task: Map old blog paths to new ones with permanent redirects

method: Aider wrote 40 rules in the redirects file, deployed, then requested every old path with curl and checked the status code. Fixed the one pattern that returned 404 and redeployed.
limitations: Forty paths from one site; the check covered status codes only, not the final page content.

summary: Ran a build with CI set to true and the build failed on warnings that were not errors on a local run. Setting the flag off for the build let the deploy finish. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The CI variable made the bundler treat warnings as errors, and the log listed unused variable warnings as the failure.

context.task: Get a React app build through the Netlify pipeline

method: OpenHands agent read the build log, reproduced the warnings locally with the CI flag set, removed the unused imports, and redeployed. Kept the flag on after the fix.
limitations: One React project with a handful of warnings; a larger codebase might surface more failures under the same flag.

summary: Connected a Netlify site to a Git repo and the first deploy failed with a missing publish folder because the build wrote to dist. Adding the publish path to netlify.toml fixed the next build. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build finished with a success status while the publish step found no files, so the deploy page showed an empty site first.

context.task: First git-based deploy of a Vite site

method: Cline connected the repo, accepted the default build command, and then set the publish directory to dist in netlify.toml after seeing the empty deploy. Triggered a new deploy from the Deploys tab.
limitations: A single Vite site with the default build command; custom plugins and headers were not configured.

summary: Set custom response headers for security in netlify.toml and the headers appeared on the next deploy for every path. The agent checked them with a header dump from the local terminal. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The header block matched all paths, and the content security policy was applied to the static assets as well as the pages.

context.task: Add response headers to a static site

method: Claude Code edited the headers block in netlify.toml, deployed a draft, and fetched the home page and one asset with curl and printed the response headers.
limitations: Two requests checked; the policy was not tested against live scripts or third-party embeds.

summary: Rebuilt an old site that had a stale cache, and the purge from the UI removed the old asset but the browser kept an old copy until a hard reload. The new hash appeared in the HTML after the redeploy. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The HTML referenced the new hashed file name, while the browser still requested the old one from a local cache.

context.task: Confirm a redeployed site serves fresh hashed assets

method: Devin redeployed the Vue build, compared the script tag in the served HTML with the build manifest, then loaded the page in a fresh browser profile to confirm the new file.
limitations: A single page checked in one browser; the purge behaviour on other clients was not measured.

summary: Tested a function that calls an upstream service every minute and the run stalled at the first call because the request had no timeout. The deploy was rolled back by the agent before the test could finish. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The upstream request hung for longer than the test window, and the function never returned a response in the log.

context.task: Poll an upstream status endpoint from a scheduled function

method: Goose added a fetch call with no timeout to a scheduled function, deployed, and waited for the first run in the function log. Stopped after the log showed no response and rolled back the deploy.
limitations: A single upstream endpoint on the Free plan; the run did not try an abort signal or a retry wrapper.

summary: Used a deploy hook from a CMS to trigger a rebuild, and the hook call returned 200 but the site showed old content for about three minutes. The second hook call after an edit showed the new text. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The hook responded with a 200 status right away, and the build started in the Deploys list after a short delay.
The old text stayed visible until the build finished, so the agent waited before checking the page.

context.task: Trigger a Netlify rebuild from a CMS publish event

method: Aider created a build hook in the site settings and called it with curl from a CMS webhook test, then polled the page until the new text appeared. Checked the Deploys list for the triggered build.
limitations: A single webhook call path; the hook was not tested under bursts of content edits.

summary: The sandbox blocked outbound traffic, so a build step that downloaded a font pack failed and the deploy never started. The agent recorded the failure and ended the run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build step exited when its download request was refused, and the local dev server still rendered the page.

context.task: Build and deploy a site that fetches remote fonts at build time

method: OpenHands agent in a sandboxed Linux shell ran the build command that pulled remote fonts, then stopped at the download step. Deploy was not attempted because the build never produced an output folder.
limitations: Sandbox with no outbound network; the deploy step was not reached, so the deploy path is untested in this run.

summary: Added one rule to the redirects file for a moved docs section and the old path answered with a 301 on the first deploy. The check used curl on both paths. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

method: Claude Code wrote Vitest specs on Node 22 with pnpm that replace global fetch with fixtures for a streamed reply, a 429 response, and an empty choices list.

summary: A long generation timed out at the client default, and raising the timeout and lowering max tokens let the second attempt finish the report. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The timeout error appeared only on the longest prompts, and the agent first suspected the proxy.
Setting the timeout once on the client covered every call in the job without per-request overrides.

context.task: Draft a long report from a structured outline

method: Aider changed a Python 3.11 report script to set a longer client timeout and a lower max_tokens cap, then reran the longest outline on its own after the first timeout.
limitations: Only the longest outline was rerun; the chosen timeout was not tested against slow providers.

summary: Compared a summarizer prompt across three providers serving the same model family, and the agent logged latency, token counts and a rubric score for each run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Latency differed by provider for the same family, while rubric scores stayed within two points of each other.
Logging the provider field per call was what made the latency split visible in the final table.

context.task: Pick a provider for a summarizer

method: Claude Code wrote a Python 3.12 harness that runs 50 documents through three provider routes for one model family, logs timings and usage from each response, and scores outputs against a rubric.
limitations: Fifty documents from one corpus; scores came from a single rubric prompt and were not double-checked.

summary: A 180k-token document was sent to a model with a shorter context window, the 400 error came back, and the agent's truncation cut the wrong section and the run was abandoned. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 400 reported the input as too long, but the truncation kept the table of contents and dropped the body, so the summaries were useless.

context.task: Summarize a long technical manual in one call

method: OpenHands sent a full manual to a model slug chosen from the listing without checking its context length field, then truncated the input by character count and reran twice.
limitations: One manual and one model; chunking by section was not attempted in this session.

summary: Built a FastAPI endpoint that takes the model slug as a query parameter with a fixed allowlist, and requests to unknown slugs get a 400 before any upstream call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The allowlist was a short tuple in config, so adding a model meant editing one line and redeploying.
Rejecting unknown slugs locally kept bad slugs from reaching the upstream API and cluttering the error logs.

context.task: Expose a model choice safely in a FastAPI endpoint

method: Claude Code added a FastAPI route on Python 3.12 that checks the model query parameter against a tuple of allowed slugs, returns 400 for anything else, and forwards the rest to chat.completions.create.
limitations: Tested with pytest and TestClient only; the allowlist was not checked against the live listing.

summary: Behind a corporate proxy the Python client failed TLS verification with a certificate error, and the agent pointed the client at the company CA bundle before the run completed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The SSL error named the certificate chain but not the proxy, so the agent first suspected an expired key.
Setting the CA bundle path through an environment variable worked for the SDK's HTTP client without code changes.

context.task: Run a summarizer from an office network

method: Goose ran a Python 3.12 summarizer on Windows 11 from an office network, got an SSL verification error, then set the CA bundle environment variable to the company certificate file and reran.
limitations: One office network and one laptop; no other proxy setups or Linux hosts were tested.

summary: Paddle.js overlay checkout opened in a React page after the agent set the client token and switched the environment to sandbox. The first open showed the test product and closed cleanly after a sandbox purchase. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The sandbox switch had to run before initialize, otherwise the overlay requested the live catalog and listed no products for the test token.
The checkout completed callback fired with the transaction id, which the page used to show a confirmation line.

context.task: Open an overlay checkout from a pricing page

method: Claude Code in a Vite React app. Added the Paddle.js script, initialized it with a client-side token and the sandbox environment, and opened the overlay with a price id from the test catalog. Completed a sandbox purchase in the browser.
limitations: Only one test price was purchased in the sandbox; the flow for multiple line items and discount codes was not tested.

summary: Node Express webhook route rejected every Paddle event with a signature mismatch. The body had already been parsed by the global JSON parser, so the HMAC was computed over re-serialized bytes. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Verification failed on each delivery until the route used express.raw for the webhook path and read the Paddle-Signature header.
The header carries a timestamp and a hash, and the agent split them on the semicolon before building the signed payload.

context.task: Verify subscription webhooks in an Express service

method: Codex CLI in an Express 4 server. Moved the webhook route above the JSON middleware, switched it to raw body parsing, and replayed a signed subscription.updated event from a local script after each change.
limitations: Only the subscription events were replayed locally; the timestamp tolerance window was not tested with delayed deliveries.

summary: Node script created a transaction through the API for one price with custom data attached. The response returned a checkout URL on the first call, and the agent saved the transaction id to a local file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Passing a single item with a price id and quantity was enough, and the call returned the transaction with its status draft.
Custom data came back on the transaction object as sent, which made it easy to store the internal order key alongside.

context.task: Create a transaction for a quote from a backend job

method: Goose in a Node script. Installed the official Node SDK, set the sandbox API key from the environment, and created a transaction with one item and custom data, then printed the returned id.
limitations: Covered one item and one currency in the sandbox; multi-item carts and tax handling were not part of this run.

summary: Overlay checkout button on a marketing page never opened the checkout. The default payment link was unset in checkout settings, and the agent stopped after four attempts with the same silent failure. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The overlay needed a default payment link configured in the dashboard, and nothing in the console error named that setting.
The initialize call succeeded and the open call returned without an error, so the page looked healthy while no overlay appeared.

context.task: Open an overlay checkout from a landing page button

method: Cursor editing a static HTML page with Paddle.js included from the script tag. Ran the page in a local browser, clicked the button, and read the console output after each change to the initialize options.
limitations: The dashboard checkout settings were not inspected by the agent, so the fix path was never confirmed in this run.

summary: Flask service listed prices for a pricing page and cached the response for an hour. The first call returned the test catalog, and the cache key included the environment name so sandbox and live data stayed apart. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The list call paginated results, and the agent followed the next cursor until the catalog was complete.
Keying the cache only on the product id would have mixed sandbox and live prices, so the agent added the environment to the key.

context.task: Show current prices on a server-rendered page

method: Aider in a Flask app. Wrote a helper that lists prices with the Python SDK, follows the pagination cursor, and stores the result in a dict cache keyed by environment and product id. Checked the page output against the sandbox dashboard.
limitations: The catalog had about a dozen test prices; the cache eviction behavior under many products was not measured.

summary: Next.js route handler called the API with a sandbox key while the environment variable pointed at production. Every request returned an authentication error until the base URL and key were changed together. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The error said the key was not valid for the requested environment, which pointed the agent at the base URL setting.
The project had two variables with similar names, and the agent had read the wrong one from the deployment config.

context.task: Create transactions from a Next.js API route

method: Claude Code in a Next.js app deployed to Vercel. Read the environment variables for the route, set the sandbox key and environment name in a preview deployment, and called the transaction endpoint from a test request.
limitations: Only the preview environment was checked; production variables were left as they were and not called during the run.

summary: Plan change on a subscription was built with a proration setting and tested in the sandbox. The preview showed a credit and a charge line, and the agent matched both to the expected amounts in minor units. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The preview endpoint returned the recurring and immediate totals separately, which made the credit line easy to label in the UI.
Totals came back as strings in minor units, and the first formatter treated them as numbers and rounded the cents away.

context.task: Preview the cost of switching a subscription to a higher plan

method: Cursor in a React and Node project. Added a preview route that calls the subscription preview endpoint with the target price, then a formatter that parses the minor unit strings. Covered the formatter with unit tests.
limitations: Tested with one monthly subscription in a single currency; annual billing and mid-cycle changes with multiple items were not checked.

summary: Laravel app pointed its HTTP client at a classic billing endpoint while the keys were issued for the newer billing product. The first call returned a not-found response and the agent switched the base path to the current API. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The two Paddle products use different keys and paths, and the not-found error gave no hint that the key belonged to the other product.
The official PHP package installed cleanly and the agent used its client class rather than raw HTTP calls after the path fix.

context.task: Create a checkout from a Laravel controller

method: Claude Code in a Laravel project. Installed the PHP SDK with composer, replaced a hand-written HTTP call with the client class, and created a transaction in the sandbox to check the response shape.
limitations: Only the sandbox was used, and the controller was tested through a local artisan serve session without a queue worker.

summary: Vue storefront passed an internal cart id through custom data into the overlay checkout. The completed purchase came back to the page with the same id, which the agent used to clear the cart on success. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The custom data object was echoed in the checkout completed event, so the cart id was available without a server lookup.
The cart was cleared only on the completed event, and a closed overlay left the cart intact as the agent intended.

context.task: Tie a storefront cart to an overlay purchase

method: Cline in a Vue 3 storefront. Passed the cart id as custom data when opening the overlay, handled the checkout completed event to clear local state, and tested a sandbox purchase and a closed overlay.
limitations: Only a single-item cart was tested; server-side reconciliation of the purchase was not part of this run.

summary: Rails controller tried to verify webhooks with a hand-written HMAC helper and compared against the wrong header. The helper never matched, and the agent ended the run without switching to the official verifier. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The hand-written helper hashed the parsed params hash instead of the raw request body, so no delivery ever matched.

context.task: Verify billing webhooks in a Rails app

method: Claude Code in a Rails app with no Paddle SDK installed. Wrote a verification method with OpenSSL HMAC, replayed three sandbox deliveries, and compared the computed digest with the header value on each attempt.
limitations: Only sandbox deliveries were checked; the agent did not install a maintained client and the run did not test one.

summary: Angular component mounted the overlay checkout inside a modal and opened it from a plan card. The modal closed on the completed event, and the agent reloaded the subscription list to show the new plan. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The overlay rendered above the modal backdrop without a z-index change, so the agent left the component markup as it was.
The subscription list did not update until the page re-fetched, because the webhook had not yet been processed.

context.task: Let users switch plans from an in-app modal

method: Claude Code in an Angular 18 app. Wrapped the Paddle.js open call in a service, bound it to the plan card button, and tested a sandbox purchase from the modal followed by a list refresh.
limitations: Only the upgrade path was tested in the sandbox; downgrade and cancellation from the modal were not built.

summary: Fastify service deduplicated incoming Paddle events by event id in Redis. Two deliveries of the same event arrived during a replay, and the second one was acknowledged without a second write after a Redis key expired too early. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The dedupe key had a 60 second expiry, and the replay tool sent a retry after 90 seconds, so the second write went through.
The event id field was stable across retries, which made it a sound dedupe key once the expiry was longer.

context.task: Process Paddle events once even when they are redelivered

method: Codex CLI in a Fastify service with Redis. Added a set-if-not-exists check on the event id with a 24 hour expiry, then replayed one event twice with a 90 second gap and counted the database rows.
limitations: Tested the dedupe with a single local Redis instance; eviction under memory pressure and cluster failover were not covered.

summary: Symfony command verified stored Paddle deliveries using the official PHP SDK's verifier. The command rejected a single tampered payload, and the agent confirmed the valid ones passed on the same run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The verifier took the raw payload and the header value, and returned a boolean the command used to skip bad rows.
The stored rows had been saved as decoded JSON, so the agent changed the table to keep the raw text column for verification.

context.task: Audit stored webhook payloads for tampering

method: Aider in a Symfony console command. Read stored deliveries, passed raw text and the signature header to the SDK verifier, and printed a count of valid and invalid rows for a set of sandbox samples.
limitations: Covered about thirty sandbox samples; the migration to the raw text column on an existing production table was not run.

summary: Sandboxed agent tried to call the sandbox API from an isolated container to create a test transaction. Outbound requests to the API host were refused, so the run ended with no transaction returned. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The SDK surfaced a connection refused error from the sandbox proxy, which looked identical to a bad base URL on the first pass.

context.task: Create a sandbox transaction from a worker

method: Devin in a sandboxed Node project with the official SDK installed. Set the sandbox key and called the transaction create method, then tested basic connectivity with a plain request to the same host.
limitations: The sandbox had no outbound route to the API host, so transaction behavior was never observed in this run.

summary: FastAPI route verified webhooks with the Python SDK's helper and returned 200 after the verifier passed. A delivery sent with a stale timestamp was rejected as expected, which the agent checked against the replay window. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A delivery older than the tolerance was rejected, and the agent confirmed the window by sending one event with an old timestamp.
The route read the body with request.body() before parsing, so the verifier received the bytes it signed.

context.task: Accept subscription events in a FastAPI service

method: Claude Code in a FastAPI project. Added a route that reads the raw body and the signature header, passed them to the SDK verifier, and sent one valid and one stale event from a local script.
limitations: Tested the verifier with two events in a local process; the production secret handling and deployment were outside this run.

summary: Duplicate checkout completed events arrived from the browser and the webhook, and the order was created twice. The agent moved the write to the webhook and kept the browser event as a read-only refresh. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The browser callback and the webhook both reported the same transaction, and the first version created an order from each one.
Keying the order on the transaction id stopped the second insert, and the browser path now only reads the order status.

context.task: Create exactly one order per paid transaction

method: Claude Code in a Next.js app. Removed the order insert from the client callback, added a unique index on the transaction id, and replayed a completed event followed by the browser callback to count rows.
limitations: Only one order table was tested with a single database; concurrent webhook deliveries from separate workers were not simulated.

summary: Next.js server action opened a customer portal session for the signed-in customer and redirected to the returned link. The redirect worked after one correction to the customer id lookup, which had used the email instead. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The portal session needs the Paddle customer id, and the agent first passed the email address stored on the user row.
The returned session contained a link that opened the self-service page with subscription management enabled.

context.task: Let customers manage their subscription in a hosted portal

method: Windsurf in a Next.js project. Added a server action that reads the Paddle customer id from the user record, creates a portal session, and redirects. Tested with one sandbox customer who had an active subscription.
limitations: Tested with one sandbox customer and one active subscription; customers without a subscription were not covered.

summary: Discount code was applied to a transaction preview and the total dropped by the expected amount on the first try. The agent checked the discount object's status before showing the price, since an expired code still returned a preview. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: An expired discount still produced a preview with no reduction, so the UI would have shown the full price without any warning.
The discount applied as a percentage to the recurring total only, which matched the expected figure in the sandbox.

context.task: Show a discounted price before checkout

method: A custom SDK agent in a Hono service on Bun. Wrote a route that fetches the discount, checks its status, and only then calls the transaction preview with the code, then compared the totals for two sandbox codes.
limitations: Only percentage discounts were tested in one currency; fixed-amount codes and stacked discounts were not covered.

summary: Expo app tried to open the Paddle checkout inside a WebView by injecting the browser script. The WebView loaded the page, but the overlay never rendered, and the agent stopped after two approaches. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The injected script ran, but the overlay depended on a page origin the WebView did not present, so no checkout frame appeared.

context.task: Show hosted checkout inside a mobile app

method: Claude Code in an Expo app using a WebView component. Injected the Paddle.js script through the source html and called the open method from a message handler, then checked the simulator logs for the frame load.
limitations: Only an iOS simulator was used and the native checkout route was not tried, so the mobile checkout path is untested here.

summary: Spring Boot service read the product catalog from the API once at startup and cached it in memory. The catalog call returned all active prices, and a refresh endpoint reloaded the cache after a price change in the sandbox. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The startup load took under a second in the sandbox, and the cache held the price ids used by the pricing controller.
Prices changed in the dashboard were not visible until the refresh endpoint was called, which the team had not expected.

context.task: Serve current price ids from memory

method: Windsurf in a Spring Boot service. Added a catalog client that lists prices at startup, stored them in a concurrent map, and exposed a refresh route. Tested the refresh after editing a sandbox price in the dashboard.
limitations: The catalog held a few dozen test prices; cache size and refresh timing at larger catalogs were not measured.

summary: Bun script exported last month's transactions to a JSON lines file by following the pagination cursor. The file held every transaction in the range, and the agent checked the count against the dashboard report. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The list call returned a next cursor on each page, and the script stopped when the cursor was empty instead of counting pages.
The created_at filter took ISO timestamps, and a date without a time was treated as the start of that day in UTC.

context.task: Export monthly transactions for bookkeeping

method: Goose in a Bun script. Used the list transactions call with a created_at range for one month, followed the cursor, and wrote one JSON object per line to a file in the working directory.
limitations: Covered one sandbox month of a small account; very large date ranges and rate limiting on long exports were not tested.

summary: Overlay checkout on a Svelte page failed to open because the site's content security policy blocked the inline init call. The agent could not change the header in the sandbox preview, so the run ended on the console error. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The console listed the blocked inline script and the Paddle host, and the agent could not confirm the header change without a deploy.

context.task: Open a checkout overlay on a Svelte landing page

method: Cline in a SvelteKit project. Moved the initialize call into a module script, opened the overlay from a button, and read the console in a headless browser before and after each change to the policy meta tag.
limitations: The policy was set by a meta tag in the sandbox only; the deployed server header and its precedence were not checked.

summary: Django admin page listed subscription status changes from webhook records and filtered them by customer. The page loaded in the first test, and the agent added an index on the event type column for the filter query. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The changelist filter on the event type column ran a full scan until the agent added the index in a migration.
Storing the event type as a plain string made the admin filter simple, and the agent avoided an extra lookup table.

context.task: Review subscription status history in the admin

method: Claude Code in a Django project with a PostgreSQL test database. Registered a ModelAdmin for stored webhook events, added list filters and a migration with an index, then loaded a set of sample rows to check the page.
limitations: Loaded a few thousand synthetic rows; query plans under real event volume and the admin permissions model were not reviewed.

summary: Node CLI read a YAML file of tiers and created the matching products and prices in the sandbox. Re-running the script with the same file left the existing prices alone after the agent added a lookup by external id. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script created each product first and stored its id in a local map, so the price entries could reference the product by name.
Without the lookup the second run created duplicate prices, which the agent saw as extra rows in the sandbox listing.

context.task: Sync a pricing table from a config file

method: Goose in a Node CLI. Parsed a YAML file of three tiers, created products and prices through the SDK, and ran the command twice to confirm the second pass made no new prices.
limitations: Only three tiers in one currency were seeded; archiving prices removed from the file was not implemented in this run.

summary: Webhook handler received a subscription event before the matching customer event had been stored. The first handler call threw on the missing customer, and the retry after a short delay succeeded. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Subscription and customer events arrived in either order during a replay, so the handler needed to tolerate a missing customer row.
Returning a non-2xx code on the missing row let the delivery retry later, which fixed the ordering without extra storage.

context.task: Handle subscription events that arrive before customer events

method: Claude Code in an Express webhook service. Added a check for the customer row that returns a 500 when it is missing, then replayed the two events in reverse order with a local script to watch the retry path.
limitations: Used a local script to replay reversed events; the real delivery retry schedule on the provider side was not observed.

summary: Rails app moved webhook processing into an ActiveJob queue so the controller returned quickly. The job ran in the test queue adapter, and the agent confirmed the transaction row was updated after the job finished. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The controller verified the signature inline and enqueued the payload, so the response came back before any database work started.
Passing the raw payload as a string kept the signed bytes intact for the job's own verification step.

context.task: Process billing webhooks without slow responses

method: Codex CLI in a Rails 7 app with ActiveJob. Added a controller action that verifies the signature and enqueues a job, then ran the job inline in the test environment and checked the row afterward.
limitations: Tested with the inline test adapter only; a real queue backend and its retry settings were not configured in this run.

summary: Agent tried to create sandbox transactions in a EUR-only test workspace from a Python script. Every request was refused because the workspace had no default currency configured, and the run ended without a transaction. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The refusal message named the currency rule in general terms, and the agent could not change the workspace setting from the API.

context.task: Create a EUR transaction in the sandbox

method: OpenHands in a Python venv with the official SDK. Created a transaction with a EUR price, read the error object, and listed the workspace settings through the API to look for the currency field.
limitations: The agent only read settings exposed by the API and did not check the dashboard, so the configuration fix is unconfirmed.

summary: Python script generated transaction previews for each pricing tier to fill a comparison table. Three tiers returned totals on the first pass, and the agent wrote the results as a markdown table for review. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each preview call took one price id and returned the line items, so the script could loop over tiers without state.
Totals came back in minor units, and the script divided by one hundred for display, which matched the sandbox amounts.

context.task: Compare plan totals for a pricing page

method: Aider wrote a short script that loops over three price ids, calls the preview endpoint for each, and prints a markdown table. Ran it against the sandbox and compared the output to the dashboard totals.
limitations: Three tiers in one currency were compared; tiers with add-ons or regional tax lines were not included in this run.

summary: Bulk price update script hit HTTP 429 after about two hundred requests in the sandbox. The agent added a backoff that reads the retry-after header, and the remaining updates completed on the second pass. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 429 responses came without a clear limit name, so the agent only knew to wait from the retry-after value.
A fixed one second pause between calls reduced the throttling to a single retry during the second run.

context.task: Update prices on several hundred entries

method: A custom SDK agent running a Node batch script against the sandbox. Looped over price updates with a fixed pause, caught 429 responses, read retry-after, slept, and retried each failed call up to three times.
limitations: Batch of about four hundred sandbox updates; production limits and their behavior at larger batch sizes were not measured.

summary: Astro page prerendered prices during the build and opened the overlay on click with the stored price id. The static output had no secret keys, and the overlay opened on the first try in the preview deployment. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build step fetched the prices with the server key and wrote only the public ids into the page, which kept the secret out of the output.
The client-side token was passed as a public environment variable, and the agent confirmed it was the sandbox token.

context.task: Open checkout from a static pricing page

method: Claude Code in an Astro project. Added a build script that reads price ids from the API and writes them into the page, then wired a button to open the overlay with the id. Checked the built HTML for any key strings.
limitations: Only one preview deployment was tested with sandbox data; the production token rotation and cache headers were not checked.

summary: TypeScript project added strict types for the webhook payloads it reads, using the SDK's exported event types. The compiler caught two places where the code read a field that is optional on subscription events. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The SDK's event union narrowed on event_type, so the switch statement gave the right payload type in each branch.
Two accesses on subscription events needed null checks, which the agent added rather than casting the object.

context.task: Type-check incoming billing events

method: Claude Code in a TypeScript service. Replaced loose event typing with the SDK's exported union, updated the switch branches, and ran the type checker plus a short test that feeds sample payloads.
limitations: Checked types against sample payloads from one sandbox account; event types not present in the sample set were not exercised.

summary: Python worker synced customers into a CRM table from the customer list endpoint and recorded the last cursor after each batch. A crash in the middle of a run resumed from the stored cursor without duplicating rows. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Writing the cursor after each committed batch meant a restart picked up the next page, which the agent verified by killing the process mid-run.
Upserting on the customer id made the rerun idempotent, and the CRM row count matched the sandbox customer list.

context.task: Mirror customers into a CRM table

method: A custom SDK agent in a Python worker. Paginated the customer list with the SDK, upserted each page into SQLite inside a transaction, saved the cursor, and killed the process after the second batch to test the resume path.
limitations: Tested with a few hundred sandbox customers in SQLite; the production database and larger pagination volumes were not covered.

summary: Node CLI replayed saved webhook payloads from a folder into a local handler to check branch coverage for each event type. The replay stopped at one payload with an unknown event type, and the handler logged it without failing. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The CLI read each saved file, signed it with the local secret, and posted it to the handler, so the replay exercised the real verifier.
The handler's default branch logged the unknown type and returned 200, which kept the replay moving through the rest of the folder.

context.task: Smoke test every webhook event type locally

method: Goose in a Node project. Wrote a replay command that reads JSON files from a fixtures folder, signs each body with the test secret, and posts it to the local handler, then counted the logged branches.
limitations: Covered the fixtures committed in the repo only; events that the sandbox had not produced yet were not represented.

summary: Go service called the API with a client-side token meant for the browser. Every call came back forbidden, and the agent stopped after reading the token type in the docs and finding no matching server key. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The browser token and the server API key look alike in the dashboard, and the agent had copied the wrong one into the environment file.

context.task: Fetch transactions from a Go backend

method: Claude Code in a Go service. Read the environment file, wired a transaction list call with the token from it, and compared the request header format against the server key format in the docs.
limitations: Only the sandbox credentials were checked; the agent did not generate a fresh server key, so the working setup was not reached.

summary: Flask endpoint that builds a checkout for a plan passed a product id where the API expected a price id. The first two requests returned validation errors, and the third used the id from the price list and succeeded. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The product id and the price id were both in the same dashboard table, and the agent had read the wrong column for the checkout items.
The error named the item field but not the id type, so the agent compared the two values by hand against the listing output.

context.task: Create a checkout for a selected plan

method: Claude Code in a Flask app with the Python SDK. Listed prices and products through the SDK, matched the plan name to a price id, and sent one sandbox checkout request per candidate id until the validation error stopped.
limitations: Covered one plan with a single price in the sandbox; plans with several prices per product were not tested.

summary: Claude Code set relationMode to prisma in a Next.js schema for PlanetScale, ran prisma db push against a development branch, and the migration applied on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: relationMode was set to prisma in the datasource block, since the branch had no foreign key constraints on the new tables.
prisma db push finished in 11 s against the development branch and reported no drift.

context.task: Add a projects and members schema to a Next.js app on PlanetScale

method: Claude Code on macOS editing schema.prisma and running prisma db push with DATABASE_URL pointed at a development branch, using a password created with pscale password create. Next.js route reads projects through the Prisma client.
limitations: One development branch, and the deploy request to main was not opened in this run.

summary: Cursor added a nullable column through a development branch, opened a deploy request against main, and merged it after reviewing the schema diff. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The schema diff in the deploy request listed one added column and no dropped indexes, which the agent checked before merging.

context.task: Run a Vite dev server from the Playwright config
context.blocker: port held by a stale process

Leaving the reuse option on let an already running dev server serve the local run without a second process.

observations.observation: Waiting for the download after the click left a gap where the event fired before the listener was attached.
Starting the download wait and the click together inside Promise.all removed the race and the file name matched.

summary: Goose wrote a keyboard navigation test for the site menu that tabs through the items and checks focus order. The run passed on the first attempt, and the agent noted that the search field had no visible focus outline. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

The visible focus outline was checked by eye in a screenshot, since no computed style assertion was added.

context.task: Test keyboard focus order in the site menu

summary: Custom SDK agent tried to install Playwright browsers in a locked-down sandbox. The browser download host was unreachable, so no test ran, and the run was stopped after the install retries used up the budget. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Claude Code added a mobile project to the Playwright config using a device descriptor for a phone-sized viewport. The navigation spec ran on both desktop and mobile projects and passed, with the mobile menu opened by its button. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

The mobile menu needed a click on the toggle before the links were visible, so the spec opens the menu first.

context.task: Run navigation tests on a phone-sized viewport

method: Inside a Next.js repo with an existing Playwright config, Claude Code added a project that spreads a built-in phone device descriptor, opened the menu before the link assertions in the navigation spec, then ran both projects.

summary: OpenHands ran the suite with four workers, and two specs changed the same test account's profile at once. Creating one account per worker stopped the collisions, and the next full run passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

summary: Goose added API checks with the request fixture to the same suite as the UI tests. The health endpoint and the items list returned the expected status codes, and the checks ran in the same job. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

Asserting the status and the content type on each response kept the checks short and readable.

method: Goose added a spec file that uses the request fixture to call the health and items routes on a local API server, checks status codes and content types, and runs in the same project as the UI specs.
limitations: Two routes on a local server; authenticated endpoints and error payloads were not covered.

summary: Codex CLI upgraded the Playwright package in one workspace but left a second copy of the browser library pinned to an older version. Browser launches failed with a mismatch, and the agent stopped after it could not get a single install tree. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

Installing with system dependencies first kept the first WebKit run clean on the Linux runner.

observations.observation: Events were queued in memory when the function returned, and the process froze before the batch was sent.
Awaiting shutdown before the response made each event appear in the live view within seconds of the request.
The client gave no error on the empty runs, so the missing events were only visible in the project after waiting.

context.task: Send server-side events from Express route handlers

Remote evaluation worked for each request, but the agent wanted local evaluation to avoid per-request calls and did not switch back.
The 401 message did not name which key type was expected, so the agent read the docs twice before trying a second key.

context.task: Evaluate feature flags server-side in FastAPI
context.blocker: project key used for local evaluation

A rewrite on the app domain routed the SDK traffic through the same origin, and the second test sent the pageview normally.
Two browser setups were tested, so other blocker lists were not covered.

Capture calls ran inline in the request, and the agent measured a small per-call cost in a local loop.

context.task: Capture server-side events in a FastAPI backend

preferences.optimizing_for: server and client on one person

summary: Claude Code turned on session replay for a Next.js signup page and confirmed the recording showed the form layout with input values masked. The first recording appeared in the replay list about ten minutes after the test signup. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]
