observations.observation: The audit endpoint received one callback after the final retry failed and logged the original destination and message ID.
The gaps between attempts grew with each retry, so the full retry sequence for the test took several minutes rather than seconds.

context.task: Capture exhausted retries

method: Windsurf added failureCallback to the publish call, pointed it at a SvelteKit endpoint that writes a log line, wired a test route that returns 500, published one message with retries set to 2, and waited for the callback.
limitations: One failing route with a fixed 500; the callback path was not tested with a timeout or a 4xx response.

summary: The publish script threw 401 because QSTASH_TOKEN was not set in its local environment. Adding the variable to the env file and loading it before client creation let the next publish return 200. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The client raised an authorization error on the first publish, and the error text did not name the missing variable.
The env file was read after the client was created in the first version, so the client never saw the variable even after it existed on disk.

context.task: Publish nightly export jobs

method: Codex CLI ran the publish script, read the authorization error, added QSTASH_TOKEN to .env, moved dotenv loading above client creation, then reran the script with one test row.
limitations: One local script run with a single test row; the production secrets store was not checked.

summary: Relayed incoming vendor webhooks through QStash into a Remix action, so the action handled retries instead of the sender. All 40 test deliveries were verified and processed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: All 40 test deliveries passed signature verification with the current signing key, and the action wrote 40 rows to the test table.
The replay used a noticeable share of the free plan message allowance, so the agent capped the test at 40 messages.

context.task: Relay vendor webhooks through QStash

method: Devin added a Remix action that reads the raw body, verifies it with Receiver using the current signing key, inserts a row and returns 200, then replayed 40 recorded payloads through publishJSON from a script.
limitations: Replayed recorded payloads only, against a test table; the vendor side was not connected during the run.

summary: A Bun script listed all QStash schedules and deleted the 14 that pointed at a retired staging host. The remaining schedules were left as they were. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Listing returned 23 schedules, the filter matched 14 with the retired host, and a second listing showed the other 9 unchanged.
The list call returned results in pages, and the script kept requesting pages until the last one came back.

context.task: Remove stale schedules

method: Goose wrote scripts/prune-schedules.ts for Bun, read the token from the environment, paged through the schedule list until the last page, then deleted each schedule whose destination contained the retired host.
limitations: Staging project only with 23 schedules; the script ran once and was not scheduled itself.

summary: Publish calls from the sandbox could not reach the QStash API, so no message was queued during the run. The agent recorded the connection errors and stopped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each publish call failed with a connection error after the default client timeout, and the 30 attempts produced no delivery entries.
The SDK error said fetch failed without the host or status code, so the egress block was only inferred from the repeated timeouts.

context.task: Queue test messages from sandbox

method: Cursor wrote a script that calls publishJSON 30 times with a small payload from a sandboxed Linux VM, captured the error from each call, and compared the failure timing with a curl request to the same API host.
limitations: Outbound access from the sandbox was blocked, so the run never reached the queue and no later stage was tested.

summary: A 5,000 message fan-out test on the free plan stopped when publish calls began failing at about 2,600 messages. The remaining messages were not sent. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Publish calls began returning an error after about 2,600 messages, and the error text pointed at the plan's message quota.
The test plan set 5,000 messages without reading the plan limits first, so the agent had to stop the run partway.

context.task: Fan-out load test

method: Codex CLI generated a Node script that publishes 5,000 messages in batches of 100 to a URL group on the free plan, watched the error output, and stopped the script after the quota errors repeated.
limitations: One script from one machine; the run stopped before the planned total, so no delivery rate figures were produced.

summary: Publishing a 3 MB JSON body returned errors from the publish call, and the agent abandoned the approach. The worker never received the payload. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 3 MB publish call returned an error on each of four tries, and the error did not state whether the body size was the cause.
The agent judged a queue message the wrong place for a payload that size and switched to passing an object key instead.

context.task: Send generated report via queue

method: Windsurf built a 3 MB JSON report in memory, called publishJSON four times with retries set to 0 and read each error response, then dropped that approach and went back to passing object keys.
limitations: One synthetic 3 MB report from one machine; no attempt at compressed or chunked bodies.

summary: A Hono route on Cloudflare Workers received QStash deliveries, verified them, and wrote each message to KV. Publish-to-log latency stayed under a second in the test. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Verification passed inside wrangler dev on the first try once the body was read as text, and the Worker wrote the expected key to KV.
Publish-to-log latency averaged 640 ms across 20 deliveries, with the slowest at 910 ms.

context.task: Process deliveries on Workers

method: Claude Code wrote a Hono handler that reads c.req.text(), verifies with the Receiver from the Upstash package, writes to KV, then published 20 messages with a loop and read the Worker logs with wrangler tail.
limitations: Local wrangler dev through a tunnel; the deployed Worker and its KV namespace were not used.

summary: Image resize jobs went through QStash to a worker route that returned 200 after writing thumbnails. Twelve uploads were processed and each job finished on its first delivery. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: All twelve jobs returned 200 on the first delivery, and the thumbnails appeared in storage under matching keys.
Passing only the object key in the body kept messages small, and the worker fetched the original from storage on its own.

context.task: Generate thumbnails from uploads

method: Cursor added a route that publishes the object key after each upload, a worker route that downloads the original and writes three sizes, then uploaded twelve test images from a script and compared the thumbnail keys.
limitations: Twelve small test images from one machine; no large files and no concurrent upload burst.

summary: publishJSON received a body that was already a JSON string, so the worker got a quoted string instead of an object. Passing the object directly fixed the handler. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The worker's JSON.parse produced a string instead of an object, and the handler failed its schema check on the first delivery.
Passing the object into publishJSON produced a body the schema accepted on the next three deliveries.

context.task: Send order sync payloads

method: Windsurf called JSON.stringify before publishJSON in the sync job, read the schema failure in the worker log, removed the stringify call, and published three test payloads to confirm the handler accepted them.
limitations: Three synthetic payloads on one route; no check of nested objects or large arrays.

summary: Rotated the signing keys by moving the old current key into the next slot and the new key into current. Deliveries made before the swap still verified during the overlap window. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Deliveries signed before the swap still returned 200 because the verifier was given both keys, and fresh publishes after the swap also passed.
The rotation needed edits in two places, the environment file and the deploy settings, and the agent checked both before calling it done.

context.task: Rotate QStash signing keys

method: Codex CLI updated QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY and QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY in the local env file, restarted the server, published a message before and after the swap, and checked that both deliveries returned 200.
limitations: Local server only; the deploy-side key update was checked by reading settings, not by a live deploy.

summary: Replaced a custom setTimeout retry loop around a webhook call with QStash retries set to five. The webhook sender now makes one publish call and the in-process loop was removed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A test endpoint that failed twice and then returned 200 received three attempts in total, and the publisher made only the one publish call.
Deleting the retry loop removed about 60 lines and two timer helpers from the sender module.

context.task: Replace custom retry loop

method: Aider deleted the withRetry helper, passed retries: 5 to publishJSON in the webhook sender, pointed a test route at an endpoint that returned 500 twice, and counted attempts in the endpoint log.
limitations: Single test endpoint with a scripted failure pattern; the production sender was not switched over in this run.

summary: A Python script published 200 messages from a nightly export to a Next.js route in about 40 seconds. Every publish call returned a message ID on the first attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 200 publish calls finished in about 40 seconds from a single process, and the route logged 200 distinct message IDs.
No publish call returned an error, and the script wrote each message ID from the response into the audit file.

context.task: Push nightly export records

method: Cline wrote export_push.py with the Python SDK client, looped over 200 rows from a CSV file calling publish_json with the Next.js route as destination, then compared the logged IDs against the file.
limitations: One process on a Linux VM with 200 rows; no test of the route under concurrent exports.

summary: The worker ran longer than the endpoint timeout, so QStash retried and the same order row was written twice. An idempotency check on the order id stopped the duplicate. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Handler work ran for about 11 seconds, so the delivery timed out and was retried, which produced a second insert for the same order id.
A lookup on the order id before insert stopped the second write, and the retried delivery returned 200 without changing the table.

context.task: Stop duplicate order writes

method: Devin ran the order handler against a slow test database, observed duplicate rows after a timed out delivery, added a lookup on the order id before insert, then replayed the same message twice to confirm one row.
limitations: A single slow-database test with synthetic orders; the check reads before inserting rather than using a unique constraint.

summary: Passed each webhook event id as the QStash deduplication id, so a second publish of the same event was not delivered to the handler. The handler ran once per event in the test. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The second publish with the same deduplication id was not delivered, and the handler log showed one entry for event evt-8810.
The agent could not find the deduplication retention period in the quickstart and wrote a note asking the team to confirm it.

context.task: Deduplicate webhook replays

method: Windsurf set deduplicationId from the event id in publishJSON, sent one event twice with a script, and read the handler log to count runs.
limitations: One event sent twice from a script; behaviour after a longer gap between the two publishes was not measured.

summary: After rotating the signing keys, the verifier was built with only the current key, so deliveries signed under the previous key failed for about two minutes. Adding the second key to the verifier cleared it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Deliveries queued before the rotation failed verification for about two minutes, and the retries succeeded once the second key was added to the verifier.
Leaving one key out of the verifier constructor was not flagged by the type checker or by the startup logs.

context.task: Rotate signing keys

method: OpenHands rotated QSTASH_CURRENT_SIGNING_KEY and QSTASH_NEXT_SIGNING_KEY in the environment, built the Receiver with only the current key, read the 401 failures in the worker log, then added the next key and waited for the retries to land.
limitations: One worker in a staging project with a small queue, so the retry timing reflects that single queue.

summary: Deliveries signed with the rotated key were rejected by the verifier, and the agent stopped before adding the other key. The worker kept returning 401 until someone changed the config. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Every delivery after the rotation returned 401, and the queue backed up while the agent waited on a config change it was not allowed to make.
The agent stayed inside the repository and did not edit deployment settings, which left the rotation incomplete.

context.task: Rotate QStash signing keys

method: Devin changed the verifier to read the new signing key from the environment, ran a test delivery while deploy settings still held the old value, collected the 401 responses and stopped without editing deployment settings.
limitations: No access to deployment settings, so the key state there was inferred from the 401 responses alone.

summary: Publishes a status re-check for an order ten minutes after checkout, with the delay set on the publish call. The re-check route returned 200 at the expected time. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The re-check arrived 10 minutes and 9 seconds after publish, in line with the delay setting plus queue overhead.
A ten minute wait made iteration slow, so the agent used a 20 second delay in development behind an environment flag.

context.task: Re-check order status after checkout

method: Claude Code added a publishJSON call with a delay option inside the checkout route, used a 20 second delay in development behind an environment flag, then timed the delivery against the log timestamp.
limitations: One order flow in a preview deployment; no test of checkout failures or duplicate checkouts.

summary: Schedule creation ran on every server start, so each deploy added another copy of the same cron job. A test expecting one schedule failed with four, and a list-by-destination check before create fixed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: After four deploys the schedule list held four entries for the same destination and cron, and each one fired the job in the same minute.
The fix lists existing schedules by destination before creating, and the test passed after two simulated restarts with no new entries.

context.task: Make schedule setup idempotent

method: Aider moved schedules.create into an instrumentation hook that runs at boot, ran vitest which expected one schedule after two restarts and read four, then added a list-by-destination check before create and reran the test.
limitations: Test ran against a development project with mocked server restarts; real deploy timing was not reproduced.

summary: Published a job from a Vercel Edge route through the HTTP client, since the Edge runtime has no Node sockets. The worker received the message and returned 200. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The publish call succeeded from the Edge route, and the worker log showed the body unchanged after the round trip.
The agent did not need a Node-only dependency, because the client sends plain fetch requests and runs unchanged in the Edge runtime.

context.task: Publish jobs from Edge routes

method: Goose added a route handler with the edge runtime that calls the QStash client publish method with the worker URL, deployed a preview build, then sent five requests and read the worker logs.
limitations: Preview deployment only with five requests; the production alias and its routing were not checked.

summary: Deliveries returned 404 because the destination path said api/task instead of api/tasks. The agent corrected the publish constant, and the next delivery returned 200. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each attempt returned 404 from the worker, and the delivery log showed a path one letter shorter than the route folder.
The delivery log listed the attempted destination, which made the one-letter difference visible after the first failure.

context.task: Deliver agent tasks to worker

method: A custom TypeScript agent published tasks to a worker route through a path constant, read the 404 entries in the delivery log, fixed the publish constant to match the route folder, then reran three tasks with curl.
limitations: Three tasks in one local test with a single worker; no check of other publish paths in the codebase.

summary: A custom agent queued each tool task on QStash with a deduplication id derived from the task hash, so a replayed planning step did not run the same task twice. Forty tasks ran once each. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Replaying the planning step produced the same deduplication id, and QStash did not deliver the duplicate task to the worker.
Tasks came back out of submission order when two workers were active, so the agent stored a sequence number in the message body.

context.task: Queue agent tool tasks durably

method: A TypeScript agent loop hashed each tool call, published it with publishJSON and that hash as the deduplication id, ran two local workers, then replayed the planning step to confirm the duplicate was dropped.
limitations: Forty synthetic tasks on one machine with two local workers; no failure injection on the worker.

summary: Tried publishing from a client component in the browser, which needs the server-side token. The build failed, and the agent moved the call to a server action before the session ended. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The client component imported a shared QStash helper, and the build failed on a server-only import pulled into the browser bundle.
The quickstart showed a server example without saying the token must stay out of client bundles.

context.task: Publish jobs from a button click

method: Aider imported a shared qstash helper into a client component, ran next build, read the bundler error, moved the publish into a server action, and stopped when the session time limit was reached.
limitations: Only the build step was checked; the server action path was not exercised before the run ended.

summary: Ran a tunnel so QStash could reach a development endpoint, then published three test jobs that all came back with 200. The tunnel address was updated in the publish script for each run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Three test deliveries reached the local handler through the tunnel within a few seconds, and each returned 200 on the first try.
The tunnel address changes on every restart, so the publish script read it from a dev env file that the agent rewrote before each run.

context.task: Test deliveries against local handler

method: OpenHands started a tunnel to the local port, wrote the tunnel address into a dev env file, published three jobs with publishJSON from a Node script, and tailed the local server log to confirm each 200.
limitations: Single developer machine with a tunnel; no test of a longer local outage or a restart during delivery.

summary: A daily job was set for 09:00 on the assumption that cron used local time, but the first run landed at 09:00 UTC. The expression was shifted to the intended local hour and the schedule view was rechecked. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The schedule view showed only UTC, so the 09:00 local target was entered without conversion and the first run came in several hours early.
Shifting the expression by the offset and putting UTC in the schedule name made the schedule view show the intended local hour.

context.task: Set a daily morning job

method: Goose created the schedule through the REST endpoint with a daily cron, compared the first run time in the logs with the local clock, then updated the cron to the offset value and reread the schedule entry.
limitations: One schedule in a staging project and one time zone; daylight saving changes were not tested.

summary: Mounted express.raw on the QStash route before the verifier, so the signature check ran on the original bytes. A tampered test body returned 401 and the valid one returned 200. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The route used express.raw directly, so the verifier received the exact bytes QStash signed, and valid deliveries passed on the first run.
A body with one changed character returned 401, and the handler side effect did not run for that request.

context.task: Verify deliveries in Express

method: OpenHands mounted express.raw on the job route, passed the buffer to Receiver.verify with the Upstash-Signature header, and ran vitest with a valid request and a request with one character changed.
limitations: Vitest with supertest against a local app; no real QStash delivery from the public internet was observed.

summary: Added a sliding-window limiter to the comments route with @upstash/ratelimit. The 11th request inside one minute returned 429 as configured. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Requests 1 through 10 passed and request 11 returned HTTP 429 with a reset header, matching the 10-per-60-second config.
The quickstart showed the limiter constructor but did not say the Redis instance must read the same environment variables as the rest of the app.

context.task: Rate limit comment submissions per IP

method: Claude Code edited app/api/comments/route.ts, installed @upstash/redis and @upstash/ratelimit with pnpm, read credentials through Redis.fromEnv(), then ran curl loops against the local dev server to check the 429 boundary.
limitations: Only one development database and one local dev server; no load test and no concurrent-IP scenario.

summary: The first run of Redis.fromEnv threw a missing variable error because the project only had REDIS_URL set. Adding the REST URL and token to .env.local fixed it on the next run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The thrown error named UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL as missing, while the project file held a rediss connection string under REDIS_URL.
The fix took one edit and one server restart, and the rate limit route returned 200 on the first request afterwards.

context.task: Wire rate limiter in Next.js route

method: Claude Code ran next dev after adding Redis.fromEnv() to lib/redis.ts, read the missing variable error, copied the REST URL and token from the console into .env.local, restarted the server and resent the request with curl.
limitations: Only the local development environment was checked; production environment variables were not compared.

summary: Cached catalog JSON for 300 seconds inside a Remix loader and timed the hit path against the uncached query. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Cache hits answered in about 41 ms from the client region, while the uncached catalog query took roughly 190 ms.
The SDK docs listed ex as an option key on set, and the agent used it as written without any typing or runtime error.

context.task: Cache catalog reads in a Remix loader

method: Cursor edited app/routes/catalog.tsx and a small cache helper, installed @upstash/redis, read the client with Redis.fromEnv(), set entries with the ex option, then timed 50 requests with autocannon against a preview build.
limitations: Timed against one preview build in a single region; no cache invalidation path was exercised.

summary: Tried ioredis inside Next.js edge middleware for a per-IP counter. The edge runtime could not open the TCP socket ioredis needs, so the agent stopped that path. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The middleware failed on the first redis command with a socket error, before any counter was read or written.
The client setup section did not mention that ioredis needs the Node.js runtime, and the runtime note sat on a separate page.

context.task: Per-IP counter in edge middleware

method: Cline added ioredis to package.json, created a client from REDIS_URL in middleware.ts, ran next dev and requested the protected page, then read the runtime error and stopped without switching clients.
limitations: Only the local dev server was run; no preview deployment was tried in this session.

summary: Built an idempotency-key guard for a FastAPI order endpoint with the Python Redis client, using set with nx and ex. A replayed POST returned the stored response. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A second POST with the same Idempotency-Key header got the stored 201 body back, and the handler ran only once according to the test log.
The first version set the key without an expiry, which the agent caught in review and fixed by passing a 24 hour ex value.

context.task: Idempotency keys for order creation

method: Codex CLI wrote app/idempotency.py on top of the upstash-redis client, ran pytest against a development database, then replayed one POST twice with httpie and compared the stored response body.
limitations: One endpoint and a development database; concurrent duplicate requests were not raced against each other.

summary: Batched 200 HINCRBY writes into one pipeline in a Node ingest script instead of awaiting each call. The batch finished in 6 s instead of 41 s. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Sequential awaits took 41 s for 200 writes from a laptop, and the pipelined version finished in 6 s with identical final hash values.
Results came back in command order, and the agent confirmed it by checking the returned array length against 200.

context.task: Speed up counter ingestion

method: Aider rewrote scripts/ingest.ts to call redis.pipeline() and exec once per 200 command batch, then ran the script under time against 1,000 synthetic events from a laptop on a home connection.
limitations: One laptop on a residential connection; no measurements from the production region.

summary: The cache read threw a SyntaxError because the code ran JSON.parse on a value the SDK had already parsed. Removing the extra parse fixed the account settings route. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: get returned a plain object for a value written with set, and the second JSON.parse call threw on the first cache hit.
After removing the extra parse, two cache hits in a row returned identical objects and the unit test passed.

context.task: Serve cached account settings

method: Cursor added a cache wrapper in app/lib/settings-cache.ts using set and get, ran the Remix dev server, reloaded the settings page twice, then removed a leftover JSON.parse call that the first version had carried over from another file.
limitations: Verified only the settings route with one test account; other cached routes were not reloaded after the change.

summary: Built a top-10 leaderboard for a Hono app on Cloudflare Workers with sorted sets. The HTTP-based client ran inside the Worker with no extra bundler setup. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The client imported cleanly under wrangler dev, and reads and writes from the Worker route worked without changes to the build config.
Two players with equal scores came back in lexical member order, which the spec did not cover, so the agent added a tiebreak note in the handler.

context.task: Top-10 leaderboard endpoint

method: Cline generated src/index.ts for a Hono app, wrote a leaderboard helper around zadd and a top-10 range read, ran wrangler dev locally, then posted five scores with curl and checked the returned ordering.
limitations: Local wrangler dev only; the Worker was not deployed, and just five players were seeded.

summary: A Node.js node-redis client inside a Cloudflare Worker failed the bundle step because the TCP client imports Node built-ins that the Workers build does not provide. No request reached the Worker. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Wrangler stopped with a missing module error for a Node built-in pulled in by the TCP client, before any request was made.
The agent did not switch to the HTTP-based client during the session, so the Worker had no working data path at the end.

context.task: Connect Worker to Redis

method: Claude Code installed the node-redis package, wrote a Worker entry that connects with createClient to a rediss URL, ran wrangler dev, then wrangler deploy with a dry run, reading the bundler output after each attempt.
limitations: Only the bundling stage was attempted; no request reached a Worker, so runtime behaviour is untested.

summary: Stored Express session JSON in Upstash with a one hour expiry so two app instances behind one balancer shared logins. Both instances read the same session after one login. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A login on instance A was readable from instance B within the same second, and logout deleted the key so both instances saw the session end.
The SDK returned the stored session as a parsed object, so the store adapter needed no serializer of its own.

context.task: Shared session store across two instances
context.deploy_target: two instances behind a load balancer

method: Windsurf added a RedisStore adapter using set with ex 3600 and del on logout, wired it into express-session, then logged in on one local instance and checked the same session id on the other with curl.
limitations: Two local processes on one machine; restarts and a real load balancer were not tested.

summary: Changing the window to 10s failed the TypeScript build because the duration type expects a space before the unit. Changing it to '10 s' got the build through. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The compile error pointed at the window argument, and the package example used a number and unit separated by a space.
The second build compiled in 14 seconds, and the limiter returned 429 on the 11th request in the smoke test.

context.task: Add sliding window limiter

method: Codex CLI wrote the limiter in middleware, ran tsc, read the error on the window argument, changed the string, reran tsc, then started a local server and sent 11 requests with curl.
limitations: One route and a local server; the limiter was not checked across several app instances.

summary: Cached the account feature flags in a SvelteKit server hook with a 30 second TTL to cut reads against the flag service. Cache hits served 18 of 20 reloads inside the window. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: 18 of 20 page reloads inside the window were served from Redis, and the two misses lined up with the 30 second expiry.
A flag switched off in the admin page stayed on for up to 30 seconds on the storefront, which the agent wrote into the PR description instead of shortening the TTL.

context.task: Reduce feature flag reads

method: Devin added src/hooks.server.ts that reads flags through redis.get, falls back to the flag service on a miss and writes back with set plus ex 30, then reloaded the storefront page 20 times from a shell loop and counted hits in the logs.
limitations: One storefront route was tested, and flag changes were made by hand in a single admin session.

summary: Wrote a Bun script that deletes every key with a given prefix by walking scan in batches of 500 rather than calling keys. It removed 12,430 keys from a staging database. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The scan loop removed 12,430 keys with the prefix session:stale in about 40 seconds and left the other 3,116 keys untouched.
The agent avoided keys because it walks the whole keyspace in one call, and the staging database held about 80,000 keys.

context.task: Delete stale session keys in staging

method: Goose created scripts/clear-prefix.ts for Bun, loaded credentials through Redis.fromEnv(), looped scan with a match pattern and count 500, deleted matches in chunks, then ran a second scan to confirm zero matches remained.
limitations: Staging database with no live traffic during the cleanup, so concurrent writes were not a factor.

summary: The latency script could not reach the database endpoint from the sandbox, and every call timed out after 10 seconds. No benchmark numbers were produced. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: All 40 connection attempts timed out, and a curl to the same host from the sandbox hung without any response.
The SDK surfaced only a generic request failure, so the timeout reason was not visible in the stack trace.

context.task: Benchmark REST latency

method: Cursor wrote a Python script with the upstash-redis client that ran 40 get calls with a 10 second timeout inside a sandboxed Linux VM, then tried curl against the same endpoint and watched it hang.
limitations: Outbound network from the sandbox was blocked, so the benchmark was not repeated from an unrestricted machine.

summary: A 10,000 write load test on the free plan hit the command quota at about 4,300 writes, and the agent abandoned the run. Partial results were not kept. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Writes stopped succeeding after roughly 4,300 calls, and the errors named the command limit for the plan.
The test plan did not check the plan's command allowance before starting, so the limit was found in the middle of the run.

context.task: Load test session writes

method: Codex CLI generated a Node script that issued 10,000 set calls with random keys in one loop, ran it against a free plan database, watched the error output and stopped the process once the errors repeated.
limitations: One process on one machine; the run stopped before the planned 10,000 writes, so later-stage numbers do not exist.

summary: Stored 2 MB JSON snapshots as single Redis values to skip an object storage hop, and the test runner stalled on each write. The agent dropped the approach. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each 2 MB set took between 3 and 5 seconds from the test runner, so a 50 snapshot test took about four minutes.
The agent concluded Redis suits short-lived small values better and left the snapshots out of the cache design.

context.task: Cache dashboard snapshots

method: Aider wrote a helper that serialized dashboard snapshots as JSON and called set on each one with a 2 MB payload, ran a pytest module that wrote 50 of them, timed the run and reverted the helper afterwards.
limitations: Synthetic 2 MB payloads from one laptop; a larger test set was not tried.

summary: Cached the user profile hashes behind a Next.js profile page. Server time fell from 310 ms to 58 ms once the cache was warm. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Server time for the profile page fell from 310 ms to 58 ms on the second visit, measured from the Next.js timing output.
Profile edits call hdel on only the changed fields, which kept writes small but needed a separate test for renamed keys.

context.task: Speed up profile page

method: Claude Code added lib/profile-cache.ts with hset and hgetall helpers, wired them into the profile server component, and warmed the cache by loading the page twice in a local production build.
limitations: Measured on a local production build with one test account; no traffic from the real user region.

summary: Used a Redis list as a lightweight job queue, with lpush in the web handler and rpop in a Node worker loop. The worker drained 50 queued thumbnail jobs in order. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Pairing lpush with rpop gave first-in first-out order, and the test confirmed it by checking job IDs 1 through 50 in sequence.
The worker slept 500 ms whenever rpop returned null, so an empty queue did not turn into a busy loop during the test.

context.task: Background job queue for thumbnails

method: Cursor added enqueue in an Express route using lpush and a worker script using rpop with a 500 ms sleep on empty, then enqueued 50 jobs with a loop and compared the worker log order.
limitations: One worker process and 50 jobs; the queue had no crash recovery or retry path in this run.

summary: Writes to the counter key returned a permission error because the environment file held the read-only token. A new token with write access in .env.local cleared it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Writes failed with a permission error while reads from the same client succeeded, which pointed at the read-only token in the environment file.
The console listed the read-only token beside the main one, and the copy step was easy to skip on the first pass.

context.task: Increment page counters

method: Windsurf ran a Nuxt server route that calls incr, read the permission errors in the server log, compared the token prefix in .env.local with the console entries, created a token with write access and restarted the dev server.
limitations: Only the dev server was retested with the new token; token rotation and revocation were not checked.

summary: Added a fixed window of 100 requests per minute to a webhook receiver through the rate limit package. The load script saw request 101 blocked. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Request 101 in the same minute returned 429, and the counter reset at the next minute boundary as a fixed window does.
A burst of 200 requests straddling a minute boundary was allowed in full, roughly twice the per-minute limit, which is the known tradeoff of fixed windows.

context.task: Limit webhook receiver traffic

method: Codex CLI installed @upstash/ratelimit, created a fixedWindow limiter at 100 requests per 60 s, mounted it on the webhook route, then sent 101 requests in one minute and a 200 request burst across a boundary.
limitations: Tested locally with one client IP; the limiter key came from a header the test set by hand.

summary: Replaced an ioredis client in Next.js middleware with the HTTP-based Upstash client. The edge build compiled, and five requests returned 200 from the preview. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The edge build failed on the ioredis import before the change and compiled cleanly once the middleware used the HTTP client.
The old call set a key and then ran a separate expire, while the new client takes the expiry as an option on set.

context.task: Make middleware edge-compatible

method: Aider replaced the ioredis import in middleware.ts with Redis.fromEnv(), moved expiry into set options, ran next build, then sent five curl requests to a rate-counted route on a preview deployment.
limitations: Checked only the middleware path on one preview build; other routes that still used ioredis were left as they were.

summary: Connected a go-redis client over TLS to an Upstash endpoint and trimmed login attempts per IP with a sorted set. Trimming took about 3 ms per call in the test harness. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The rediss connection string worked with the stock go-redis client, and the agent used the database password from the console rather than the REST token.
ZREMRANGEBYSCORE removed attempts older than 15 minutes in one call, and ZCARD matched the expected count in all 40 table cases.

context.task: Login throttling by IP

method: Claude Code wrote auth/throttle.go with go-redis, opened a TLS connection from the rediss URL in environment config, added ZADD, ZREMRANGEBYSCORE and ZCARD calls, then ran go test with a 40 case table against a development database.
limitations: One development database and a single test process, so concurrent writers were not exercised.

summary: Tool results were written to Redis without an expiry, and an audit script that checks for a positive TTL flagged 14,000 keys. A default expiry in the write helper and a rerun cleared the audit. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Tool result writes had no ex option, so the first audit counted 14,000 keys with a TTL of -1 on a staging database.
The audit exited non-zero on its first run, and it passed after the helper began setting a 3600 second default expiry.

context.task: Tool result cache hygiene

method: A Python agent loop wrote tool outputs with the upstash-redis client, ran an audit script asserting a positive TTL on every key, added ex 3600 to the write helper after the failure, and reran the audit on staging.
limitations: Audit ran against staging only, with about 14,000 keys and no production traffic.

summary: Devin tried to rotate a cache key with the production environment token, but that token was read-only, so every write was refused. It stopped and logged the failure for the team. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Every SET call returned a permission error while GET calls on the same key succeeded, so the rotation never started.
The agent had no console access, so it could not confirm the token scope and did not try other tokens from the environment.

context.task: Rotate production cache keys

method: Devin read the deploy config to find the Redis environment names, ran a rotation script that wrote one test key with the environment token, collected the permission errors, and stopped without changing any values.
limitations: No console access was available, so token scope was inferred from the error responses alone.

summary: Caching LLM summaries for a docs search tool with keys built from a SHA-256 hash of the normalized prompt. Repeat questions returned the stored answer without a model call. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Keys came from a SHA-256 of the normalized prompt, so the same question with extra spaces hit the same entry in the test run.
Entries expired after 24 hours, a window the agent picked to limit stale answers once the source docs change.

context.task: Cache repeated docs questions

method: Goose wrapped the summary call in a helper that hashed the prompt with node:crypto, read with redis.get, wrote with set and ex 86400, then asked the same three questions twice and counted hits in the log.
limitations: Only three test questions; the cache was not checked against a docs corpus that changes during a run.

summary: Counted page views per route with incr in an Express middleware and read the totals with mget. The counters matched a manual tally of 60 test requests. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The counters for the four test routes summed to 60, the same total as the manual tally kept in the test script.
The incr call added about 9 ms to each request on the local network, which the agent judged acceptable for analytics.

context.task: Count route views

method: OpenHands added a middleware that calls redis.incr on a day-scoped key, read the four counters with mget, and ran a bash loop of 60 requests against the local server before comparing the totals.
limitations: Local server only, with no real user traffic and no check of counter behaviour across midnight UTC.

summary: Deduplicated incoming webhook events by storing each event ID with set nx and a 600 second expiry. A redelivered event was acknowledged and skipped. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The redelivered event returned 200 without running the handler, and the log line read already processed for event 7781.
The agent assumed the sender retries within ten minutes and set the key lifetime to match, noting that a longer retry window would need a longer expiry.

context.task: Ignore duplicate webhook deliveries

method: Windsurf added a dedupe helper in src/webhooks.ts that calls set with nx and ex 600 keyed on the event id, returns early when the set does not apply, then replays one signed payload twice with curl.
limitations: Only one event type was replayed, and signature verification was stubbed in the local test server.

summary: Pipeline results were read by the wrong index, so the first version of the batch test failed its assertion. Mapping results by command position fixed it, and the 200 writes checked out. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The test expected the hgetall result at index 0, but the array started with the hincrby return values, so the first assertion failed.
Mapping each result by its command position fixed the test, and the batch of 200 writes was rechecked against the final hash totals.

context.task: Batch hash writes in ingest

method: Aider updated scripts/ingest.ts to use pipeline with hincrby, ran vitest, read the failed assertion on index 0, changed the reader to map results by command position, then reran the ingest on 200 synthetic events.
limitations: Synthetic events only, and the check compared hash totals rather than every field value.

summary: A cleanup script using keys timed out on a staging database with about 72,000 keys. A scan cursor loop finished the delete in roughly two minutes. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first keys call on the staging database did not return before the client timeout, and the process was killed.
The cursor loop with count 1000 removed 9,870 matching tmp:export keys and left every other key in place.

context.task: Clean up staging export keys

method: Goose ran a Bun script that called redis.keys with the tmp:export pattern, hit the client timeout, rewrote the loop to use scan with count 1000, deleted matches in batches and checked the remaining total with dbsize.
limitations: Staging database with no concurrent writes; the export prefix was unique to this job and no other service used it.

summary: Guarded a nightly reconciliation route with a lock taken through set nx px. A second concurrent call got a 409 while the first run held the lock. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The second concurrent call returned 409 while the first held the lock, and the key expired on its own after the 60 second timeout.
Release compares the stored owner value before deleting, which the agent added after reasoning through the case where a slow run outlives its lock.

context.task: Prevent overlapping reconciliation runs

method: OpenHands wrote app/api/reconcile/route.ts with redis.set using nx and px options and a random owner value from crypto.randomUUID, then ran two concurrent curl requests and a vitest case for the release path.
limitations: The release path was tested with a mocked client; the live lock was exercised only with two curl calls.

summary: A custom agent built on the Anthropic SDK stored per-user conversation summaries as Redis hashes and loaded them at the start of each session. Read p50 came out at 27 ms across the synthetic session. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A single hgetall call returned every summary field for the user, which cut session startup from three requests to one.
Storing each summary as its own hash field meant an update rewrote one field instead of the full history value.

context.task: Persist conversation summaries per user

method: A TypeScript agent loop called the Anthropic messages API, wrote each summary with hset on a per-user key, read it back with hgetall before the next turn, and loaded Upstash credentials from a local .env file.
limitations: One synthetic user with 40 turns; no concurrent users were simulated and no eviction was checked.

summary: Measured GET and SET latency from an EU client to a database in another region with a small Python benchmark. GET p50 came out at 96 ms. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: GET p50 was 96 ms and SET p50 was 101 ms over 500 sequential calls from the EU client.
The p99 reached 240 ms on about 1 percent of calls, which the agent guessed came from client scheduling rather than the database.

context.task: Measure REST latency from Europe

method: Cline wrote bench.py with the upstash-redis Python client, ran 500 sequential get and set calls against a test key from a small Linux VM in eu-west-1, and computed p50 and p99 with statistics.quantiles.
limitations: One VM and one database region; the run was not repeated on other days, so the numbers reflect one session.

summary: A load test hit the free plan command quota partway through 900 writes. The agent paused, then resumed the remaining writes from a saved index after the quota reset. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Writes started failing after about 600 calls, and the remaining 300 went through only after a pause and a second run of the script.
The script stored the last completed index in a checkpoint file, so the resumed run did not repeat any of the first 600 writes.

context.task: Load test write path

method: Devin wrote load.ts to issue 900 set calls with a checkpoint file, ran it against a free plan database, waited out the quota errors, resumed from the saved index and counted keys with dbsize at the end.
limitations: Free plan database only, one client process; concurrency limits were not probed.

summary: The rate-limit test expected a 429 on the sixth request, but the config allowed six per window. The agent moved the expectation to request seven, and the case passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first assertion failed because the config allowed six requests and the test expected the block on request six.
Moving the expectation to request seven matched the config, and the 429 came back on request seven in the rerun.

context.task: Test limiter behaviour

method: OpenHands read the limiter config in lib/limit.ts, ran bun test on the route suite, changed the expected block from request six to request seven, then reran the suite with a fresh key prefix.
limitations: Unit suite with a mocked clock; the real window timing was not checked against wall clock time.

summary: The client constructor rejected the copied connection URL, and the agent spent three attempts on the scheme before stopping. The stray character in the pasted value was never found. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The constructor threw an invalid URL error on the first attempt, and the same error came back after two edits to the scheme and port.
The agent kept editing the scheme and did not print the raw length of the environment value, which would have shown the extra character.

context.task: Connect Bun service to Redis

method: Windsurf pasted the connection URL into .env, loaded it with Bun's built-in env support, passed it to the Redis constructor, changed the scheme and port twice, then stopped after the third failure on macOS.
limitations: Local development on one macOS machine; the pasted value was never diffed against the console copy.

summary: Connected a Next.js App Router repo through the GitHub integration and the first push produced a production deployment. The build log showed the default install command without changes. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The production branch was picked up from the repo default, and the first push created a deployment without any settings edit.
The log listed the framework detection line and the install step before the Next.js build started.

context.task: Deploy a Next.js App Router site from a GitHub repo

method: Claude Code connected the repository from the Vercel dashboard, pushed a commit to main, and watched the deployment list until the production build completed. Checked the page title on the deployed URL.
limitations: A single static-leaning Next.js site; server actions and dynamic routes were not exercised in this run.

summary: A Stripe webhook route returned 400 on every event because the body was parsed as JSON before the signature check. Reading the raw body fixed verification on the second deploy. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The signature check failed because the route handler received a parsed body, and the raw bytes had already been changed.
The example route in the docs showed the raw body call, but the agent had copied an older pattern from a blog post.

context.task: Verify Stripe webhook signatures in a Next.js route

method: Cursor agent wrote a POST route, sent a test event with the Stripe CLI, and read the 400 responses in the function logs. Switched to reading the raw request body and redeployed to preview.
limitations: Test-mode events only, one endpoint; signature tolerance and replay handling were not reviewed.

summary: An edge route imported a Node-only crypto helper and the deploy failed at build with an incompatibility error. The agent moved the route to the Node runtime and the next build passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build reported that the imported module was not available in the Edge runtime, and the error named the file rather than the import.

context.task: Add a signed-link helper to an edge route

method: Codex CLI added a route with the edge runtime export, imported a Node crypto helper, then ran the production build locally and in a preview deploy. Stopped when the same error returned on the preview.
limitations: One route on one framework version; the agent did not try a Web Crypto replacement before stopping.

summary: Pulled the development environment values into a local env file with the CLI and vercel dev started on the first try. The pulled file carried the preview scope values. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The pull command wrote the variables into the local env file, and the file header named the environment it came from.
The preview values were pulled because the command defaulted to the development target, which the agent did not expect.

context.task: Run a Next.js app locally with the project's cloud environment values

method: Aider linked the folder with the link command, ran the env pull command, then started vercel dev and loaded the home page. Checked which values were present in the pulled file.
limitations: Local dev only; the run did not check the production values or any integration secrets.

summary: Automated webhook tests against a preview URL returned 401 because deployment protection blocked them, until the agent turned protection off for previews. The next test run passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The protected preview returned an authentication page to the test client, which did not send any credential.
The protection setting sat in a separate section from the preview URL, and the agent found it only after the test had failed twice.

context.task: Run a webhook integration test against a preview deployment

method: Devin pointed the test runner at a preview deployment and recorded the 401 responses. Changed the preview protection setting in the project and reran the suite against the same URL.
limitations: One preview and one test suite; the setting was changed only for the duration of this run and not verified on shared projects.

summary: A monorepo project was set to the repository root, so the build could not find the web package and failed at install. Setting the root directory to apps/web fixed the next build. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build log showed the install running at the repo root with no matching package, and the error did not mention the root setting.

context.task: Deploy one app from a Turborepo monorepo
context.blocker: root directory set to repo root

method: Windsurf created a project from the repository, left the root directory at default, and ran a deploy from the CLI. Stopped after the agent could not find the root setting in the first two attempts.
limitations: A single app in the monorepo on the Hobby plan; the run did not try a second project for the same repository.

summary: Added a cron entry in vercel.json that calls a cleanup route every night, and the first scheduled invocation appeared in the logs at the configured time. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The schedule was declared in vercel.json and showed up in the project's cron list after the deploy completed.

context.task: Run a nightly cleanup route on a schedule

method: Goose added a crons block to vercel.json pointing at the cleanup route, deployed to production, and read the invocation entry in the logs after the scheduled time passed.
limitations: One scheduled job observed once; retry behaviour after a failed run was not tested.

summary: A client-side key read as undefined in the production bundle because it was added without the public prefix and the build had already run. A new deploy after the rename fixed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The bundle had no value for the variable, since client code only sees values prefixed for the browser and set before the build.
Adding the variable did not change the running build, and the next deployment picked it up.

context.task: Read a public analytics key in the browser

method: Cline added the variable in the dashboard, checked the built JavaScript for its value, then renamed it, redeployed, and searched the bundle again.
limitations: A single public value in a Vite app; server-only variables were not compared.

summary: A CI job used the CLI with a deploy token from the secrets store and the production deploy completed in under two minutes. The job printed only the deployment URL. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The deploy command took the token from the environment and needed no interactive login step.

context.task: Deploy to production from a CI job

method: Custom SDK agent in a Linux CI runner installed the CLI, passed the stored token through the environment, and ran the production deploy command from the repository root.
limitations: One project and one runner; token scoping and rotation were not part of this run.

summary: The sandbox had no outbound access, so the vercel deploy command could not reach the platform and exited with a network error. Local builds still passed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The CLI exited with a connection error on the first upload request and did not retry.

context.task: Deploy a Next.js preview from a sandboxed coding agent

method: OpenHands agent ran the local build successfully, then ran the preview deploy command from the project root and read the error. No retry was attempted after the connection failure.
limitations: Sandbox with no outbound network; a run with normal egress was not attempted in this session.

summary: Added a redirect for a renamed pricing page to vercel.json, and the old path returned a 308 on the next production deploy. The check was done with curl. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The redirect entry used a permanent flag and the response carried the new location header on the first request.

context.task: Redirect a renamed marketing page

method: Claude Code added one entry to the redirects array in vercel.json, pushed to main, and requested the old path with curl to read the status and location header.
limitations: A single redirect on a small site; wildcard and regex patterns were not tested.

summary: Built a route handler for file uploads to Vercel Blob and the uploaded file came back with a public address on the first run. The handler streamed the request without buffering the whole file. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The put call returned the stored address, and the agent saved it in the response body for the client.
The quickstart showed a token variable set by the store creation step, and the agent had to check it was present in preview.

context.task: Accept image uploads and store them in Blob storage

method: Devin created a POST route handler, connected a Blob store from the storage tab, pulled the environment values locally, and uploaded a test image with curl to the preview deployment.
limitations: A single test image and one store; access modes beyond public and size checks were not explored.

summary: A server route wrote a cache file to the project folder and the function returned 500 because the deployed filesystem is read-only outside the temp folder. Switching the write to the temp folder fixed it. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The write failed with a read-only error at the project path, while the same code passed in local dev.
The error named the path but not the platform rule, so the agent checked the docs before changing the path.

context.task: Cache rendered output to disk in a route handler

method: Windsurf wrote a cache helper that saved files next to the route, deployed to a preview, and called the route until the write error appeared. Moved the cache path to the temp folder and redeployed.
limitations: Single route with a small cache file; temp folder contents were not checked across cold starts.

summary: Pointed a custom subdomain at the project with a CNAME record and the domain showed as valid after the DNS change spread. The certificate was issued on the same day. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The domain page listed the record type to add and the agent copied it from the dashboard without editing the zone otherwise.

context.task: Attach a subdomain to a Vercel project

method: Cursor added the CNAME record in the DNS provider for the subdomain, added the domain in the project settings, then polled the endpoint with curl until it answered over HTTPS.
limitations: A single subdomain on one DNS provider; apex domains and wildcard subdomains were not configured.

summary: A route handler responded to browser requests from another origin without CORS headers, and the browser blocked the call until an OPTIONS handler was added. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The preflight request returned 405 because the route exported only a POST handler.

context.task: Call a Vercel route handler from a separate frontend

method: Custom SDK agent sent a preflight with curl, read the 405 response, then exported an OPTIONS handler that returned the allow headers and redeployed the preview.
limitations: Only one allowed origin tested; credentials mode and cached preflight responses were not checked.

summary: Started the project locally with vercel dev and the API routes responded on the same port as the pages. The first request to the route handler worked without extra setup. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The CLI served pages and API routes together, so the front end could call the route with a relative path.

context.task: Run pages and API routes together during local development

method: Aider ran the dev command through the CLI from the project root, opened the home page, and called one route with curl to confirm the response.
limitations: Local run only with one route; production behaviour for the same route was not compared.

summary: A cursor-driven change was pushed to main but the deployment was skipped by the ignored build step, so the live site stayed on the previous commit. The agent noticed the stale page after one hour. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The deployment list showed a skipped build with no log, and the cause was a path filter in the ignore script.

context.task: Ship a copy change to the production site

method: Cursor agent pushed a copy change to main, checked the dashboard deployments list, and found the build skipped. Stopped after the production page still showed the previous text.
limitations: A single push and one ignore rule; the agent did not edit the ignore script before the run ended.

summary: Rolled production back to an earlier deployment from the dashboard, and the older build served traffic within a few seconds of the promote action. The rollback was confirmed in the logs. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Promoting the earlier deployment switched production without a rebuild, and the page showed the old copy right away.

context.task: Roll back a broken production deploy

method: Devin opened the deployments list, promoted the previous production deployment to the production domain, and checked the home page and one API route with curl.
limitations: A rollback to one previous deploy with no database changes involved; schema migrations were not part of the test.

summary: A Vite app set the output directory to dist but the build wrote to build, so the deploy showed an empty site until the setting was corrected. The second build was fine. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The build log finished without errors, and the empty deployment gave no warning about the output folder mismatch.
Changing the output directory in the settings page was enough, and no code change was needed.

context.task: Fix a Vite site that deploys as an empty page

method: Windsurf read the build output folder name in the log, changed the output directory in the project settings, and triggered a redeploy from the dashboard.
limitations: One Vite project using default build commands; custom build scripts were not reviewed.

summary: Enabled speed insights for a marketing site and the first page views showed up in the dashboard after a short wait. The script tag was added through the package. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Data appeared after the first real page load, and the dashboard showed no samples until then.

context.task: Turn on performance monitoring for a marketing site

method: Claude Code added the speed insights component to the root layout, deployed a preview, loaded two pages in a browser, and checked the dashboard for the new samples.
limitations: Two pages on one preview; sampling rates and long-term trends were not reviewed.

summary: A preview build read a variable that existed only for production, so the preview returned a 500 until the variable was added to the preview target as well. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The variable had only the production target checked, which the agent did not see until the preview failed.
After the preview target was added, the same route returned data and the logs showed no further errors.

context.task: Set a third-party key for preview deployments

method: Goose opened the environment settings, added the variable to the preview target, triggered a new preview build, and called the route from the preview address.
limitations: A single variable on one project; development target values were not compared.

summary: Pointed an apex domain at the project with a CNAME record and the dashboard refused it, so the agent switched to the records the dashboard listed. The domain stayed unverified. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The DNS provider accepted the CNAME on the apex, but the dashboard reported an invalid record type for that name.

context.task: Attach an apex domain to a Vercel project

method: Cline created a CNAME record on the apex name in the DNS provider, then tried to add the domain in the project settings. Stopped after the dashboard kept rejecting the record.
limitations: Single apex domain on one DNS provider; the run did not try the address records the dashboard suggested after the second attempt.

summary: Added a middleware that redirects visitors to a locale prefix based on the accept-language header, and the redirect fired on the first preview request. The static assets were excluded from the matcher. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The matcher pattern skipped the static asset paths, so images kept loading without a redirect.

context.task: Redirect visitors to a locale prefix by browser language

method: Claude Code wrote middleware.ts with a matcher that excluded asset paths, deployed a preview, and requested the root path with two different accept-language headers using curl.
limitations: Two locales tested from one machine; cookie-based overrides were not part of this run.

summary: A route that streamed a model response worked locally, but on Vercel the stream ended early until the handler returned the streaming response object directly. The second preview kept the stream open. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The handler awaited the full text before returning, so the browser saw a single chunk at the end.
The streaming example used a different helper name than the one in the installed package, and the agent matched the installed version instead.

context.task: Stream a chat completion from a route handler to the browser

method: Goose wrote a POST route that awaited the full completion, deployed a preview, and read the response chunks in the browser console. Changed the handler to return the stream object and redeployed.
limitations: A single chat route with one model provider; backpressure and reconnect behaviour were not measured.

summary: Set www to redirect to the apex domain in the project domains, and the first attempt looped between the two hosts until the redirect target was flipped. The second deploy resolved cleanly. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Both hosts were set to redirect to each other in the domain list, which produced a loop in the browser.
Changing only the www entry to point at the apex fixed the loop without touching DNS.

context.task: Canonicalize www and apex hostnames

method: Cursor checked the domain settings for both hostnames, changed the www entry to redirect to the apex, and confirmed the response chain with curl across two requests.
limitations: One domain pair on one project; HSTS and certificate handling for the redirect were not reviewed.

summary: Listed the production environment variable names with the CLI for an audit and compared them with the README table, which showed two undocumented keys. Values were never printed. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The list command showed names, targets and the last update time, which was enough for the audit without exposing values.

context.task: Audit production environment variable names against documentation

method: Aider ran the env list command for the production target, filtered the output by name, and compared it with the variable table in the project README.
limitations: Name-level audit only; the run did not check whether values were correct or still in use.

summary: Added a remote image pattern to the Next.js config for a CDN host, and the image component returned 400 for that host until the pattern matched the path prefix. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The 400 response came from the optimizer and named the host, but not the missing path pattern.

context.task: Serve CDN images through the Next.js image component

method: Devin added a remotePatterns entry to next.config with the CDN hostname and a path prefix, deployed a preview, and requested an optimized image URL with curl.
