method: Cursor agent with a Vite React frontend and a small Express API on another port. Added a /api/me route that reads the session cookie and returns the user from the Node SDK, then checked the request in the browser network tab.
limitations: Ran on localhost with two ports; production domains and cross-site cookie behavior were not tested.

summary: Background worker wrote one audit event per role change, and the events showed up in the log view within seconds of the job run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The create call needed an actor object, a target, and an occurred-at timestamp, and the agent filled all three from the queue payload.
Events appeared in the dashboard log view after a short delay, so the agent did not add any polling for them.

context.task: Emit audit events for role changes from a worker

method: Claude Code in a Node worker that consumes a role-change queue. Installed @workos-inc/node, added a helper that calls the audit event create call with actor and target from the message, and sent three sample messages through a local queue.
limitations: Three sample messages only; no failed-write or duplicate-delivery path was exercised in this run.

summary: Email lookup in a Go admin tool returned a 404 for an address with no account, and the handler treated that case as an empty result rather than a failure. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The handler checked the status on the error and returned an empty result only for the 404 case; other errors went to the logger.
Lookups worked for seven of the eight seeded addresses on the first pass, and the eighth returned the expected 404.

context.task: Look up users by email in an internal Go tool

method: Codex CLI in a small Go module on macOS. Added the Go SDK, wrote a findUserByEmail helper, and called it from a CLI command with eight seeded addresses. Ran go test with a table case for the 404 response.
limitations: Eight seeded addresses in one test environment; case-insensitive email matching was not checked.

summary: Audit event backfill stopped after repeated 429 responses; the custom client gave up after six retries with the job roughly 40 percent complete. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: 429 responses started within the first minute of the backfill, and the client's retry window was shorter than the wait the responses asked for.
The agent sent one event per request, which meant far more calls than the batched design it had sketched for the job.

context.task: Backfill historical audit events for a customer

method: Custom SDK agent running a Python backfill script on a Linux host. Looped over stored events and sent one create call per event, with exponential backoff capped at 30 seconds between attempts.
limitations: One customer's events only, and the rate limit behavior was observed in a single job rather than across several.

summary: SvelteKit sign-in redirected once to the callback and then to the dashboard on the first browser test, with the session attached on every later request. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: A handle hook read the session cookie and attached the user to locals, so load functions read it without another fetch.
The integration example used route folder names that the agent renamed to match its own project layout.

context.task: Add sign-in to a SvelteKit app

method: Windsurf in a SvelteKit project with TypeScript. Added login and callback routes, a hooks file that reads the session, and a logout form action. Ran the dev server and walked through sign-in in a clean browser profile.
limitations: One test user on localhost; logout across two open tabs was not checked.

summary: Sinatra user lookup returned 401 because the local env file still held the value from an older project; replacing it and restarting the server fixed the call on the second try. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The API answered 401 with no detail in the body, so the stale value stayed hidden until the agent printed the variable names.
The config loader read the value at boot, so the server had to restart before an edit to the env file took effect.

context.task: Fix a 401 on user lookup in a Sinatra app

method: Claude Code in a Sinatra app on macOS. Installed the workos gem, ran a user lookup script that returned 401, printed the names of the set variables, replaced the stale value in the local env file, restarted the server, and reran the script.
limitations: Local development only; deployed environment variables were not compared against the local file.

summary: Connections list call returned 14 SSO connections over two pages, and the admin table showed all 14 after the agent followed the after cursor. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The first page held ten items, and the list metadata included an after value for the next call.
Sorting by connection type worked in the admin table without server support, because the merged list fit in memory.

context.task: Render all SSO connections in an internal admin table

method: OpenHands agent in a TypeScript React admin page with a Node proxy route. Wrote a loop that calls the connections list with the after cursor until it comes back empty, merged the pages, and passed the result to a sortable table component.
limitations: Fourteen connections in one test organization; the table was not checked with a large connection count.

summary: Sign-in on Vercel preview deployments failed because every preview build had a new hostname missing from the redirect list, and the run stopped once the list edit was clearly out of reach. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: Each preview build got a new hostname, and sign-in returned a redirect error on every one because the hostname was not on the list.
The session had no dashboard access, so the agent could only report which redirect entries were missing.

context.task: Enable sign-in on Vercel preview deployments

method: Claude Code in a Next.js app deployed to Vercel. Pushed a branch to open a preview deployment, opened sign-in from the preview page, read the redirect error, and checked the redirect configuration in the repo. Dashboard access was not part of this session.
limitations: Two preview builds only; the production redirect list was not compared against them.

summary: FastAPI dependency checked the access token against the key set and returned 401 for a token whose signature had been altered, as the test expected. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The verifier cached the key set for the life of the process, so a rotated key was picked up only after a restart.
A token with one signature character changed got a 401 from the dependency before the route handler ran.

context.task: Verify session tokens in a FastAPI admin API

method: Cursor agent in a FastAPI service. Added a dependency that fetches the key set, verifies the bearer token with the PyJWT library, and checks the issuer and audience claims. Wrote pytest cases for valid, expired, and altered tokens.
limitations: Tokens minted in one test session; key rotation was simulated by restarting the process, not by rotating keys live.

summary: Session cookie was dropped on plain http localhost because it was marked secure; making the flag depend on the environment name got sign-in working on the second attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The browser ignored the Set-Cookie header over plain http, so the callback succeeded on the server while the next page still showed signed out.
Tying the secure flag to NODE_ENV kept production on secure cookies and fixed local sign-in.

context.task: Fix signed-out state after SSO callback on localhost

method: Aider in an Express TypeScript app on Linux. Added session middleware with a cookie config, ran the callback against localhost and watched the response headers with curl, then tied the secure flag to NODE_ENV and retested in the browser.
limitations: Local http only; HTTPS behavior of the production cookie was not observed in this run.

summary: Read-only script listed organizations, counted the ones with an empty domain list, and made no writes, finishing in under two minutes on staging. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script called only list endpoints, so the audit run had no path to change an organization record.
Four organizations had an empty domain list, which the script counted separately instead of treating as errors.

context.task: Audit organization records for empty domain lists

method: Devin in a sandboxed Linux shell. Installed the workos package, wrote a script that pages through the organizations list and prints a count of records with empty domain lists, and ran it against staging.
limitations: Small staging organization count, so the pagination loop ran only two pages and was not stress tested.

summary: Sign-out server action cleared the session cookie and sent the browser to the signed-out page; the header kept the user name until one reload. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The sign-out helper needed the session ID from the cookie, so the action read that value before clearing the cookie.
The header kept showing the user name until a hard reload, and the agent traced that to a client cache rather than the server.

context.task: Add sign-out to a Next.js header

method: Claude Code in a Next.js App Router project. Wrote a server action that reads the session cookie, calls the sign-out helper, and clears the cookie, then wired it to a header button. Tested by signing in and out twice in one tab.
limitations: Single browser on localhost; sign-out from other tabs and devices was not covered.

summary: Nightly directory sync exited on its first run because the directory ID was missing from the job environment; the second run, after the value was added to the cron config, imported every user. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script read the directory ID with a plain lookup, so the missing value surfaced as a KeyError with no hint about the variable name.
The cron entry passed the API key secret name but not the directory ID, so only the first variable reached the job.

context.task: Schedule a nightly directory sync job
context.blocker: missing directory ID in job env

method: Goose session on a Linux VM with a cron job. Wrote sync_directory.py with the workos package to page through directory users, ran it by hand, then through the cron entry, and compared the environment inside each run with env.
limitations: A directory of a few dozen users; the cron schedule was checked for one night only.

summary: Fastify preHandler hook loaded the session on protected routes, and the health route stayed public without an exception on the first run. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The hook ran only on routes registered inside the protected plugin scope, so the health route needed no exception.
The session cookie arrived as a raw header string, and the agent parsed it with the cookie plugin already in the project.

context.task: Guard routes in a Fastify API with sessions

method: Codex CLI in a Fastify TypeScript service. Added a protected plugin, a preHandler hook that loads the session through the Node SDK, and two route tests with and without a cookie, run with the project test script.
limitations: Two routes covered by tests; no load testing and no concurrent session refresh was checked.

summary: Remix loader sent the browser back to sign-in on every request because it read the session before the callback action wrote the cookie; reordering the loader fixed it on the second attempt. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The loader read the session before the callback action wrote the cookie, so the first load after sign-in looked anonymous.
Moving the session read after the redirect check removed the loop, and the next request returned the user to the dashboard loader.

context.task: Stop a redirect loop in a Remix app after SSO

method: Cline in a Remix project with the Node SDK. Read the auth loader and callback action, traced the redirect in the browser network panel, reordered the loader calls, and retested sign-in from a clean profile.
limitations: One account and a single localhost port; the nested route case was not covered.

summary: Node onboarding script created a test customer organization and attached an admin user, and the new organization was in the list call before the script exited. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The script stored the organization ID from the create response and used it for the membership step, with a guard that stops the run if the ID is missing.
The organization showed up in the list call on the first attempt, so the script needed no polling loop.

context.task: Onboard a test customer organization from a script

method: Claude Code in a Node script. Called the organization create method with the customer name, took the returned ID, and called the membership step with a test admin user ID. Ran it once against staging and listed organizations afterward.
limitations: A single test customer on staging; the duplicate-name path was not exercised.

summary: Admin setup failed at the metadata step because the link the agent pasted returned the sign-in page, not the metadata document, and the run stopped after three validation errors. [SAMPLE FOR DEMO]

observations.observation: The form accepted the input but the validation message reported no signing certificate, which sent the agent to the wrong identity provider settings page.
The setup page said the metadata link could be a file or a link, but it did not say what format the link should return.

context.task: Connect a SAML identity provider from metadata

method: Cursor agent driving the dashboard in a browser, the only setup path in this run. Copied the identity provider metadata link into the connection form, read the validation message, and tried the sign-in page link before stopping. No code was written.
limitations: One identity provider test tenant; the metadata format was judged only from the form's validation message.
